# Command reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask commands` from the command registry. Don't edit it by hand: `cargo xtask check` fails if it differs from what the registry generates. -->

Every action a person or an agent can take in Beatlayer is a command in the registry (`crates/commands`). Menus, shortcuts, key and MIDI mapping, the agent API, and tests all run commands by the IDs below, so an action has one implementation however it's reached (decisions D16 and D17 in [the architecture](02-architecture.md#decisions-log)).

Each command has:

- an **ID** that never changes, which key maps, MIDI maps, agents, and logs use;
- a **label**: what a person sees in menus and key-mapping lists;
- a **description** written for a model: what it does, when to use it, and what it changes;
- a **permission class**, which decides whether an agent asks first;
- **contexts**: the parts of the interface where a person reaches it, as [the UI parity reference](ui-parity/README.md) names them;
- **default keys**: shortcuts from [the UI parity reference](ui-parity/shortcuts.md), by ID, with any arguments they fix. The UI supplies the other arguments from the selection in the shortcut's context, a text field, or a gesture. A command Live has no shortcut for has no default keys;
- **arguments** and a **result** as JSON Schemas generated from the Rust types. An agent sends the arguments as a JSON object. The types they use are under [Types](#types);
- a **readback** for every command that isn't `read`: the read command or query that shows its effect, so an agent can check what it did ([Readback](#readback)).

810 commands in 47 areas.

## Permission classes

| Class | What a command in it may do | An agent |
|---|---|---|
| `read` | Changes nothing in the project or on disk: queries, and moving the keyboard focus or the view. | Runs it |
| `edit` | An undoable change to the project, or a preference that's trivially changed back. | Runs it |
| `destructive` | Removes project content (deleting tracks, clips, or devices), or loses work that undo can't restore: discards unsaved changes, overwrites a file, or quits. An agent asks first even when undo could restore the content. | Asks the user first, unless the user has turned on autonomous mode for it |
| `external` | Reaches outside the project: files outside the project folder, the network, audio and MIDI devices, or other applications. | Asks the user first, unless the user has turned on autonomous mode for it |

## Commands

### Area `agent`

#### `agent.approve_client`

**Allow Agent**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Allows the agent called `client` to connect to the agent server, as answering Allow when it first connects does, and makes it its own token. Its approval and its autonomous mode belong to that token, not to its name: a client that connects with the agent's token isn't asked about again, and one that connects with the server's token is asked each time and is never autonomous, whatever name it gives. The approval is kept for the next start. It changes what agents may do, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client` | string | yes | The agent's name, as it gives it when it connects. |

Result: [`AgentServerState`](#agentserverstate).

#### `agent.forget_client`

**Forget Agent**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Withdraws the approval of the agent called `client`, so the person is asked again the next time it connects. Its sessions end. It changes what agents may do, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client` | string | yes | The agent's name, as it gives it when it connects. |

Result: [`AgentServerState`](#agentserverstate).

#### `agent.new_client_token`

**New Agent Token**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Replaces the own token of the allowed agent called `client` with a new random one, so a client configured with the old one can no longer speak for that agent until it's given the new one: requests carrying the old one are refused. Use it if the agent's token may have leaked. It changes what agents may do, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client` | string | yes | The agent's name, as it gives it when it connects. |

Result: [`AgentServerState`](#agentserverstate).

#### `agent.new_token`

**New Token**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Replaces the agent server's token with a new random one, so agents configured with the old token can no longer connect until they're given the new one, which the Settings window shows. Use it if the token may have leaked. It changes what agents may do, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`AgentServerState`](#agentserverstate).

#### `agent.set_autonomous`

**Autonomous**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches autonomous mode for the allowed agent called `client`. With it on, the agent runs destructive commands (deleting, discarding, overwriting, or placing clips over others) and external ones (files outside the project, devices, other applications) without asking the person first; with it off, as it starts, each one waits for the person's confirmation. It applies only to requests that carry the agent's own token. It changes what agents may do, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client` | string | yes | The agent's name, as it gives it when it connects. |
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether it runs destructive and external commands without asking. |

Result: [`AgentServerState`](#agentserverstate).

#### `agent.set_server`

**Agent Server**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches the agent server on or off, or moves it to another port. While it's on, agent clients on this computer reach the agent API over Streamable HTTP at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`, each request carrying a token as a bearer token: an allowed agent's own token, or the server's token, with which a client is asked about each time it connects. Requests from web pages are refused. Switching it on the first time makes the server's token. The setting is kept for the next start. It changes what agents may do, so only a person can run it, in the Settings window: the agent API refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Whether the server runs. |
| `port` | integer or null | no | The port to listen on, from 1024 to 65535. |

Result: [`AgentServerState`](#agentserverstate).

### Area `arrangement`

#### `arrangement.automation_arm`

**Automation Arm**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Switches Automation Arm, the Control Bar's button beside Arrangement Record: while it's on and the transport records, moving a control (a track's volume, pan, mute, or send, or a device's parameter) writes its values into that parameter's envelope at the playback position, replacing what was there over the range written, and the envelope resumes where the control is released. The whole recording is one undo step, made when recording stops. Changes only the view until then.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | On or off. Left out, the switch toggles. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.automation_mode`

**Automation Mode**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Switches Automation Mode: while it's on, every track shows an automation lane under its lane, with the device and parameter choosers that pick the parameter it shows, and its envelope is drawn and edited there. A (the View menu item and the button above the track headers) does the same. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ENV-001 | `A` | `A` | `arrangement` | Show or hide automation lanes (Automation Mode) | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | On or off. Left out, the switch toggles. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.consolidate`

**Consolidate**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Joins the material in a range on each selected track into one new clip per track, replacing the clips it covers: the time selection, or the span of the selected clips (`clips`, or `tracks` with `start` and `end`). Clips the range's edges cross are split there first and the parts inside replaced; a track with no clip in the range gets nothing, and the new clips are selected. On an audio track the new clip plays a file rendered offline from what the clips played over the range, before the track's devices and mixer, normalised with the clip gain making up for it, mono when its channels are equal; on a MIDI track it holds every note the range played, with each repetition of a looped clip written out, and the source clips' clip envelopes. Cmd-J (Ctrl-J) and Edit ▸ Consolidate run it on the selection. It's destructive, since it deletes the clips it replaces, so an agent asks first.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-002 | `Cmd+J` | `Ctrl+J` | `arrangement` | Consolidate the selection into one clip | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array or null | no | Whole clips to act on. Give either `clips` or a span of time, not both. |
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span ends, after `start`. Left out, the time selection's end. |
| `lanes` | array or null | no | The lanes a span of time covers, each a track's own lane or one of its take lanes (the comping spec, R27). Left out, the lanes of the time selection, or `tracks`' own lanes. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks a span of time covers. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`ConsolidateResult`](#consolidateresult).

#### `arrangement.consolidate_to_scene`

**Consolidate Time to New Scene**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Consolidates a span of the Arrangement into a new Session scene, leaving the Arrangement as it was: a new scene is inserted directly after `scene` (left out, the scene the Session View has selected, or the last one), and each track the span covers that holds a clip in it gets one new clip in that track's slot of the new scene, made as Consolidate makes it. `tracks`, `start`, and `end` give the span (left out, the time selection). The result's `scene` is the new scene.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span ends, after `start`. Left out, the time selection's end. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) or null | no | The scene to insert the new one after. Left out, the scene the Session View has selected, or the last scene. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks a span of time covers. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`ConsolidateSceneResult`](#consolidatesceneresult).

#### `arrangement.copy`

**Copy**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Copies clips (`clips`, or the selected clips), or the material in a span of time on tracks, to the Arrangement's clipboard with the tracks they're on, for `arrangement.paste`. Cmd-C (Ctrl-C) runs this on the selection. The clipboard isn't part of the set, and copying changes nothing in it.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-002 | `Cmd+C` | `Ctrl+C` | `global` | Copy | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array or null | no | Whole clips to act on. Give either `clips` or a span of time, not both. |
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span ends, after `start`. Left out, the time selection's end. |
| `lanes` | array or null | no | The lanes a span of time covers, each a track's own lane or one of its take lanes (the comping spec, R27). Left out, the lanes of the time selection, or `tracks`' own lanes. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks a span of time covers. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`ClipboardState`](#clipboardstate).

#### `arrangement.copy_time`

**Copy Time**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Copies the time selection (or `start` to `end`) from every track, whichever tracks are selected, to the clipboard in place of what it held: each track's clips and parts of clips on its main lane and take lanes, each track's envelopes over the span, the tempo over it, the time-signature markers and locators inside it, and its length. Cmd-Shift-C (Ctrl-Shift-C) runs this, and so does Shift with Copy. The clipboard isn't part of the set, and copying changes nothing in it. The result says what the clipboard holds.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-016 | `Cmd+Shift+C` | `Ctrl+Shift+C` | `arrangement` | Copy time across all tracks | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span ends, after `start`. Left out, the time selection's end. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |

Result: [`TimeClipboardState`](#timeclipboardstate).

#### `arrangement.create_fade`

**Create Fade**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Makes fades and crossfades from the Arrangement's selection, as Create Fade (Cmd-Option-F) does, on the selected audio clips (`clips`) or the time selection on its audio tracks (`tracks`, `start`, `end`). With a span of time: a clip whose start the span holds, and not its end, gets a fade-in from its start to the span's end; a clip whose end it holds, and not its start, gets a fade-out from the span's start to its end; two audio clips that meet inside the span get a crossfade over it; a clip the span holds whole, or holds neither edge of, is left as it is. With clips, each boundary where two of them meet gets a 4 ms crossfade, 2 ms each side, whatever the Create Fades on Clip Edges setting. Each fade is kept within its clip's limits, so a span longer than a clip allows makes the longest fade there is. One undo step, named Create Fade or Create Crossfade. Refused where the selection gives no fade. Read the result back from the clips' `data` with the query tool: `fade_in`, `fade_out`, their curves, `fade_in_before` and `fade_out_after`.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-008 | `Cmd+Option+F` | `Ctrl+Alt+F` | `arrangement` | Create a fade or crossfade from the selection | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array or null | no | Whole clips to act on. Give either `clips` or a span of time, not both. |
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span ends, after `start`. Left out, the time selection's end. |
| `lanes` | array or null | no | The lanes a span of time covers, each a track's own lane or one of its take lanes (the comping spec, R27). Left out, the lanes of the time selection, or `tracks`' own lanes. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks a span of time covers. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.delete`

**Delete**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Deletes clips (`clips`, or the selected clips), or the material in a span of time on tracks (`tracks`, `start`, `end`, or the time selection on the selected tracks): clips inside the span are deleted and clips that cross its edges are shortened or split, leaving the time empty. Nothing after the span moves. Delete runs this on the Arrangement's selection. Undo restores what it deleted, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-005 | `Delete` | `Delete` | `global` | Delete | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array or null | no | Whole clips to act on. Give either `clips` or a span of time, not both. |
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span ends, after `start`. Left out, the time selection's end. |
| `lanes` | array or null | no | The lanes a span of time covers, each a track's own lane or one of its take lanes (the comping spec, R27). Left out, the lanes of the time selection, or `tracks`' own lanes. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks a span of time covers. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.delete_crossfade`

**Delete Crossfade**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Ends the crossfade between the two audio clips on a track that meet at `boundary`, leaving neither a fade there. Refused where they have no crossfade. The shell's `arrangement.delete_fades` does what Delete does on a selected fade handle, which with Create Fades on Clip Edges on gives the clips a 4 ms crossfade instead.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `boundary` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the earlier clip ends and the later one starts. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `arrangement.delete_fades`

**Delete Fades**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Deletes the fades and crossfades of audio clips (`clips`, or the selected clips), or only those at one `edge` of each, as Delete does with a fade handle selected. With Create Fades on Clip Edges on, a fade goes back to 4 ms and a crossfade to the 4 ms crossfade of two clips that meet; with it off, fades go, and a crossfade with them, leaving the clips meeting with no fade. One undo step, named Delete Fade or Delete Fades. Cmd-Option-Delete (Ctrl-Alt-Backspace) runs this.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-009 | `Cmd+Option+Delete` | `Ctrl+Alt+Backspace` | `arrangement` | Delete the fades in the selected clips | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array or null | no | The audio clips. Left out, the selected clips. |
| `edge` | [`Edge`](#edge) or null | no | Only the fade at this edge of each clip, as Delete does with one fade handle selected. Left out, both edges. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.delete_time`

**Delete Time**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Removes the time selection (or `start` to `end`) from every track, whichever tracks are selected, so what follows closes up: clips inside it are deleted, a clip across an edge is cut or split there, and everything after it moves earlier. An envelope keeps its shape up to the span's start and from there takes the shape it had from the span's end, stepping between the two values over one tick where they differ; the tempo steps at the span's start. Time-signature markers and locators inside the span are deleted. The insert marker goes to the span's start with no time selected. One undo step, `Delete Time`. Cmd-Shift-Delete (Ctrl-Shift-Delete) runs this, and so does Shift with Delete. Undo restores it, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-019 | `Cmd+Shift+Delete` | `Ctrl+Shift+Delete` | `arrangement` | Delete time across all tracks | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span ends, after `start`. Left out, the time selection's end. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.follow`

The Sample Editor follows playback on the same switch (Option-Shift-F there too). With no arguments it toggles Follow, which also resumes it. Changes only the view.

#### `arrangement.insert_silence`

**Insert Silence**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Opens as much empty time as the time selection (or `start` to `end`) is long, at its start, on every track, whichever tracks are selected: a clip across that point is split there, and every clip (main lane and take lanes), automation breakpoint, tempo breakpoint, time-signature marker and locator at or after it moves later. Each envelope, the tempo and the signature hold across the new time the value they had at the point. The Session View's slots and the loop brace are left as they are. The new time becomes the time selection. One undo step, `Insert Silence`. Cmd-I (Ctrl-I) runs this with the Arrangement focused. To give the position and length in ticks, use `song.insert_time`.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

**Loop Selection**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Sets the Arrangement's loop brace to span from `start` to `end`, or the time selection (or the selected clips) when they're left out, and switches the loop on, as one undo step, as Cmd-L (Ctrl-L) does. With nothing selected and no span given, it switches the loop on or off instead. Playback that reaches the brace's end then goes on from its start.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where it ends, after `start`. Left out with `start`, the selection's end. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the loop brace starts. Left out with `end`, the selection's start. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.move_clips`

**Move Clips**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves clips (`clips`, or the selected clips) in time by `by` ticks, or so that `anchor` starts at `to`, and to other tracks: `anchor` goes to `track` and each other clip keeps its distance from it in the track list. With `copy`, copies go there and the originals stay. A clip placed over another clip on its new track replaces the part it covers: a clip covered entirely is deleted, one covered at an end is shortened, and one covered in the middle is split around it. Audio clips go only to audio tracks and MIDI clips to MIDI tracks, and no clip can start before 1.1.1; if any would, nothing moves. The moved clips (or the copies) are selected afterwards. Dragging a clip's title bar runs this, with Option (Ctrl on Windows) held to copy; the whole drag is one undo step. A move or copy that would replace part of another clip is destructive, so an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anchor` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The clip that `to` and `track` place. Left out, the earliest clip (the topmost of those that start together). |
| `by` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | How far to move them in time, in ticks; negative is earlier. Give `by` or `to`, or neither to move them only between tracks. |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips. Left out, the selected clips. |
| `copy` | boolean | no | Copy the clips instead, leaving the originals where they are. |
| `lane` | [`Lane`](#lane) or null | no | The lane `anchor` moves to, a track's own lane or one of its take lanes (the comping spec, R27); the other clips keep their distance from it among the track's lanes. Give `track` or `lane`, not both. |
| `to` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where `anchor` starts after the move; the other clips keep their distance from it. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track `anchor` moves to; the other clips keep their distance from it in the track list. Left out, every clip stays on its track. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.paste`

**Paste**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Places the clipboard's material starting at `at` (left out, the time selection's start or the insert marker), its first track's clips on `track` (left out, the first selected track) and its other tracks' clips on the tracks after it, keeping their spacing. The material replaces what it covers (destructive, so an agent asks first, when that's part of another clip) and is selected afterwards. It fails, changing nothing, if a clip would land on a track of another kind or there's nothing on the clipboard. Cmd-V (Ctrl-V) runs this.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-003 | `Cmd+V` | `Ctrl+V` | `global` | Paste | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the material starts. Left out, the time selection's start, or the insert marker. |
| `lane` | [`Lane`](#lane) or null | no | The lane the clipboard's first lane goes to, a track's own lane or one of its take lanes (the comping spec, R27); its other lanes keep their distance from it, among the tracks and among a track's lanes. Left out, the first lane selected, or the first selected track's main lane. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track the clipboard's first track goes to; its other tracks go to the tracks after it, keeping their spacing. Left out, the first selected track, or the track the material was copied from. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.paste_time`

**Paste Time**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Opens as much time as the clipboard holds at `at` (left out, the time selection's start or the insert marker) on every track, as `arrangement.insert_silence` does, and puts the clipboard's material in it. Material copied with `arrangement.copy_time` or `arrangement.cut_time` goes back on the tracks it came from (a track deleted since gets nothing), with its envelopes, the tempo, the time-signature markers and the locators; clips copied with `arrangement.copy` or `arrangement.cut` go where `arrangement.paste` puts them. The pasted time becomes the time selection. Refused, changing nothing, with nothing on the clipboard. One undo step, `Paste Time`. Cmd-Shift-V (Ctrl-Shift-V) runs this, and so does Shift with Paste.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-017 | `Cmd+Shift+V` | `Ctrl+Shift+V` | `arrangement` | Paste time across all tracks | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the time opens. Left out, the time selection's start, or the insert marker. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.resize_clips`

**Resize Clips**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves the `start` or `end` edge of clips (`clips`, or the selected clips) by `by` ticks, or so that `anchor`'s edge lands at `to`, every clip's edge moving as far. Moving the start edge keeps the clip's contents where they play, so the clip shows more or less of them; it can't go before where the contents begin or before 1.1.1, and a clip can't become shorter than a tick. Lengthening a clip over its neighbour replaces the part it covers. Dragging a clip's edge runs this, and so does Enter, then Left or Right, then Enter, from the keyboard; each is one undo step. Lengthening a clip over another is destructive, so an agent asks first.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-004 | `Enter then Left`, `Right` | `Enter then Left`, `Right` | `arrangement` | Resize a clip from its edge: Enter, then arrows, then Enter (Esc cancels) | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `edge` | [`Edge`](#edge) | yes | Which edge moves. |
| `anchor` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The clip whose edge `to` places. Left out, the earliest clip. |
| `by` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | How far each clip's edge moves, in ticks; negative is earlier. Give `by` or `to`. |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips. Left out, the selected clips. |
| `to` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where `anchor`'s edge goes; the other clips' edges move as far. |

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `arrangement.reverse`

**Reverse Clip(s)**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Reverses the audio in a span of the Arrangement, across several clips: the time selection, or the span of the selected clips (`tracks`, with `start` and `end`). The clips the span's edges cross are split there first, each part inside is reversed, and the parts are mirrored within the span on their tracks, so the span plays backwards as a whole. A span holding a MIDI clip isn't reversed, and nothing changes. R (Ctrl-R) runs it on the selection.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-029 | `R` | `R` | `arrangement` | Reverse the selected clips | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span ends, after `start`. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the span starts. Left out, the time selection's start. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks a span of time covers. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`ReverseRangeResult`](#reverserangeresult).

#### `arrangement.scroll`

**Scroll Arrangement**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Scrolls the Arrangement View by `x` points sideways (positive goes later in the song) and `y` points down the track list, as the scroll wheel, Shift with the wheel, and dragging with Cmd-Option (Ctrl-Alt) held do. It can't scroll before 1.1.1 or past the last track. Scrolling sideways while the song plays pauses Follow. Changes only the view; turns Optimize Width off when it scrolls sideways.

Default keys:

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ZOOM-006 | `Shift+scroll` | `Shift+scroll` | `global` | Scroll left or right | runs it |
| S-ZOOM-007 | `Cmd+Option+drag` | `Ctrl+Alt+drag` | `global` | Pan the display around the selection | runs it |
| S-ARR-024 | `Cmd+Option+drag` | `Ctrl+Alt+drag` | `arrangement` | Pan the display around the selection | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | number | no | How far to scroll sideways, in points: positive moves later in the song. |
| `y` | number | no | How far to scroll the tracks, in points: positive moves down the track list. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

#### `arrangement.select_clips`

**Select Clips**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Selects clips in the Arrangement, as clicking a clip's title bar does: `replace` selects only these, `toggle` adds or removes each (Cmd-click, Ctrl-click on Windows), `add` adds them, and `extend` adds them and every clip between them and the first selected clip (Shift-click). Their tracks become the selected tracks and the time they span the time selection, which Z zooms to. Selecting is never an undo step and changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-010 | `Cmd+click` | `Ctrl+click` | `global` | Add or remove one item from the selection | fixes `mode` = `"toggle"` |
| S-ZOOM-010 | `Cmd+click` | `Ctrl+click` | `global` | Add non-adjacent clips, tracks or scenes to the selection | fixes `mode` = `"toggle"` |
| S-EDIT-011 | `Shift+click` | `Shift+click` | `global` | Select a range from the first to the last clicked item | fixes `mode` = `"extend"` |
| S-ZOOM-009 | `Shift+click` | `Shift+click` | `global` | Add adjacent clips, tracks or scenes to the selection | fixes `mode` = `"extend"` |
| S-ZOOM-008 | `Shift+click`, `Shift+drag` | `Shift+click`, `Shift+drag` | `global` | Add items to the selection | fixes `mode` = `"add"` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clips. Empty with `replace` clears the clip selection. |
| `mode` | [`SelectMode`](#selectmode) | no | How to change the selection; `replace` if left out. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.select_fade_handle`

**Select Fade Handle**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Selects one of an audio clip's fade handles, as clicking it does: the `peak` handle where the fade reaches full level, the `outer` handle where it reaches silence, or the `curve` handle, of the fade-in at the clip's `start` or the fade-out at its `end`. A selected handle shows how far it can go, and Delete deletes its fade (`arrangement.delete_fades`). Left without `clip`, it clears the selection. Changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The audio clip. Left out, no handle is selected. |
| `edge` | [`Edge`](#edge) or null | no | Which edge's fade: the fade-in at `start`, the fade-out at `end`. |
| `handle` | [`FadeHandle`](#fadehandle) or null | no | Which of the fade's handles; `peak` if left out. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.select_take_lanes`

**Select Take Lanes**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Selects take lanes by their headers, as clicking a take lane's header does, replacing the lane headers selected or, with `add`, adding to them; with `toggle`, Cmd-clicking: each lane selected is taken away and the others added. Their tracks become the selected tracks, and the clips and time selected are let go, so Enter, T, Cmd+D, Delete and Cmd+Up and Cmd+Down act on the lanes. An empty list clears the selection of lane headers. Changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lanes` | array of [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) | yes | The take lanes whose headers to select. Empty clears the selection of lane headers. |
| `add` | boolean | no | Add them to the lanes already selected instead of replacing them. |
| `toggle` | boolean | no | Take away from the selection each of them that is selected, as Cmd-clicking a header does, and add the others. |

#### `arrangement.select_time`

**Select Time**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Selects the span from `start` to `end` on `tracks` (or the selected tracks), as dragging across track lanes does. `lanes` names the lanes the selection covers, each a track's own lane, one of its take lanes or its automation lane; left out, the tracks' own lanes. `arrangement.zoom_to_selection` zooms to it. Changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the selection starts. |
| `end` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where it ends. Before `start` is fine: the two are swapped. |
| `lanes` | array or null | no | The lanes it covers: each a track's own lane, a take lane under it, or its automation lane (the automation editing spec, R1; the comping spec, R26). Left out, the tracks' own lanes. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks it covers. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.select_tracks`

**Select Tracks**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Selects tracks in the Arrangement, replacing the selection or, with `add`, adding to it; with `title_bars`, their title bars, as clicking a title bar does, so the fold and grouped-track keys apply; with `automation_lane` and one track, its automation lane, as Up and Down select it while Automation Mode is on, and the lane gets the keyboard. Changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracks` | array of [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The tracks to select. Empty clears the track selection. |
| `add` | boolean | no | Add them to the tracks already selected instead of replacing them. |
| `automation_lane` | boolean | no | Select the track's automation lane, as Up and Down do through the lanes while Automation Mode is on (the automation editing spec, R20): the lane gets the keyboard. One track only. |
| `title_bars` | boolean | no | Select their title bars, so the track-header shortcuts (fold, show and hide grouped tracks) apply, as clicking a title bar does. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.set_crossfade`

**Set Crossfade**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Makes or changes the crossfade between two audio clips on a track that meet, the earlier one ending exactly where the later one starts: `boundary` is that position. The crossfade runs from `before` seconds before the boundary to `after` seconds past it, at least one of them above 0; over it the earlier clip fades out and the later one fades in, each playing what it would play there if its edge were moved to the span's far end, as resizing it would. `curve`, from -1 to 1, shapes both fades; 0, the default, is a straight line, so the two gains add to 1. Refused where no two audio clips meet at the boundary, or past a clip's fade limits: a crossfade reaches no further into a clip than the clip's other fade allows, takes in no point where a clip goes round its loop brace, and reads nothing before the start of a file. Read it back with the query tool's `clip` field `data`: the earlier clip's `fade_out` and `fade_out_after` and the later clip's `fade_in` and `fade_in_before`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `boundary` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the earlier clip ends and the later one starts. |
| `before` | number, at least 0 | yes | How many seconds before the boundary the crossfade starts. |
| `after` | number, at least 0 | yes | How many seconds after the boundary the crossfade ends. |
| `curve` | number from -1 to 1 | no | The curve of both fades, from −1 to 1: 0 is a straight line, so the two gains add to 1. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `arrangement.set_grid`

**Grid**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Chooses the Arrangement's editing grid directly, as its context menu does: an adaptive setting (`widest` to `narrowest`) or a fixed spacing (`eight_bars` to `thirty_second`), and the triplet and snap switches. Fields left out keep their values. Changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adaptive` | [`AdaptiveGrid`](#adaptivegrid) or null | no | Choose this zoom-adaptive setting and make the grid adaptive. |
| `fixed` | [`FixedGrid`](#fixedgrid) or null | no | Choose this fixed spacing and make the grid fixed. Give `adaptive` or `fixed`, not both. |
| `snap` | boolean or null | no | Whether to snap to the grid. |
| `triplet` | boolean or null | no | Whether note values divide into triplets. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.set_insert_marker`

**Set Insert Marker**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Places the Arrangement's insert marker at `at` and, with `track`, selects that track, as clicking in a track's lane does; a click also snaps to the grid when Snap to Grid is on, and resumes Follow. Clears the time selection. With `automation_lane`, the track's automation lane is selected too, as clicking its background does, and gets the keyboard. Not an undo step; changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where to put it. It isn't snapped: snap first if you want the grid. |
| `automation_lane` | boolean | no | Select the track's automation lane too, as clicking the lane's background does (the automation editing spec, R1): the lane gets the keyboard. |
| `lane` | [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) or null | no | The take lane the click was on, as clicking a take lane's lane does: the lane is selected with the marker, and its track with it (the comping spec, R26). |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track to select with it, as clicking a track's lane does. Left out, the selected tracks stay selected. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `arrangement.set_track_height`

**Set Track Height**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Sets the height of unfolded tracks (`tracks`, or the selected ones) and take lanes (`take_lanes`, or the selected ones when they are) to `height` points, or changes it by `delta`, from 18 to 800, as dragging a track's lower edge and Option with + or - (Alt on Windows) do. Turns Optimize Height off. Changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `delta` | number or null | no | Points to add to each track's height (negative makes it shorter). |
| `height` | number or null | no | The new height of each unfolded track or take lane, in points, from 18 to 800. |
| `take_lanes` | array or null | no | Take lanes to resize as well (the comping spec, R28). |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks. Left out, the selected take lanes if any are, otherwise the selected tracks. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).
