|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-023 | `S` | `S` | `rack-chains` | Solo the selected rack chain | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `add` | boolean | no | Add or remove the chain without touching the others' solo, as Cmd-click (Ctrl-click) does; otherwise it's the only one soloed. |
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) or null | no | The chain; the selected chains if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

### Area `clip`

#### `clip.close_slice_dialog`

**Close Slice to New MIDI Track**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Closes the Slice to New MIDI Track dialog. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SliceDialogStatus`](#slicedialogstatus).

#### `clip.create`

**Create Clip**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Puts a new clip on an audio or MIDI track's arrangement lane, at `clip.start` for `clip.length` ticks (705,600 to the quarter note). An audio clip names its audio file by content hash and plays it unwarped, at the file's own speed, from the moment the song reaches the clip; its optional settings (Start and End markers, loop, gain, fades) default to playing the whole file once at 0 dB with no fades. A MIDI clip carries its notes, placed from the clip's start. Audio clips go only on audio tracks and MIDI clips only on MIDI tracks. `clip.id` must be a new ID the project has issued for it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `clip` | [`Clip`](#clip) | yes | The clip, with a new ID. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.create_in_slot`

**Create Clip in Slot**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Puts a clip in a track's Session slot at `scene`, as Insert Empty MIDI Clip (Cmd+Shift+M) and dropping a clip in a slot do. Only audio and MIDI tracks hold slot clips, the slot must be empty, and the clip's data must match the track. A slot clip is a clip like an Arrangement clip, but it has no position there, so its `start` must be 0. `clip.id` must be a new ID the project has issued for it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it goes in. |
| `clip` | [`Clip`](#clip) | yes | The clip, with a new ID. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.crop`

**Crop Clip**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `session`, `clip-view`.

Crops a clip to the part of it that plays, or to a span of song time: an audio clip's region is written as a new, shorter file and the clip plays it, with its Start and End markers, loop brace, and warp markers moved back so it plays exactly what it played before; a MIDI clip loses the notes that start outside the region, and writes no file. `clip` names the clip (left out, the selected one); `start` and `end` give the span to keep as song positions (left out, the region the clip's own markers hold). A span the clip goes round its loop over isn't one stretch of its file, and is refused, with a message naming Consolidate, which writes such a stretch out. An audio clip's new file goes through the processed-file writer, and the edit is one undo step when it is whole. It's an edit, and destructive as well when it removes anything: audio outside the region, or notes.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-003 | `Cmd+Shift+J` | `Ctrl+Shift+J` | `arrangement` | Crop the selected clips | runs it |
| S-SES-028 | `Cmd+Shift+J` | `Ctrl+Shift+J` | `session` | Crop the selected clip | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The clip to crop. Left out, the one clip the Arrangement or the Session View has selected. |
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where it ends, after `start`. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the part to keep starts in the song. Give `start` and `end` together, or neither to keep the region the clip's own Start and End markers or loop brace hold. |

Result: [`CropResult`](#cropresult).

#### `clip.crop_region`

**Crop Clip to Region**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Crops a clip to a region of its contents: an audio clip plays the file `media` names, whose frames are the region of its old file's audio, and a MIDI clip loses the notes that start outside the region, writing no file. The clip's Start and End markers, loop brace, and warp markers move back by the region's start, so it plays exactly what it played, and the clip stays where it is in the Arrangement. `from` and `to` are in the form the clip shows: seconds into an unwarped audio clip's file, or whole ticks of a warped audio clip's or a MIDI clip's contents. `clip.crop` is the command a person and an agent run: it works the region out, writes the new file through the processed-file writer, and applies this one. Used directly, it changes the clip and names a file the caller has already written.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `from` | number | yes | Where the region starts, in the form the clip shows: seconds into an unwarped audio clip's file, or whole ticks of a warped audio clip's or a MIDI clip's contents. |
| `to` | number | yes | Where it ends, after `from`, in the same form. |
| `media` | [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) or null | no | The new file: the region's frames, written through the processed-file writer. `null` (or nothing) for a MIDI clip, which writes no file; an audio clip's crop must name one. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.crop_span`

**Crop Clip to Span**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Crops a clip to a span of song time: its edges move to the span, and it plays the part of itself the span covered, at the same moments. An audio clip plays the file `media` names, whose frames are the span's part of its old file's audio; a MIDI clip loses the notes the span didn't hold, writing no file. `clip.crop` is the command a person and an agent run: it works the span out, writes the new file through the processed-file writer, and applies this one.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the span starts in the song. |
| `end` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where it ends, after `start`. |
| `media` | [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) or null | no | The new file: the span's frames. `null` (or nothing) for a MIDI clip, which writes no file. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.defaults`

**Clip Defaults**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Reads the defaults saved for an audio clip's file by `clip.save_default`: its `file`, the `<sample file name>.beatlayer-clip` beside the sample, and the `defaults` in it, or `null` when none are saved or the file does not hold settings for this content. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |

Result: [`SavedDefaults`](#saveddefaults).

#### `clip.delete`

**Delete Clip**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Deletes a clip, from the Arrangement or from a track's Session slot. Undo restores it, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first. To keep a clip but stop it playing, use `clip.set_mute`. To delete the clips or the time selected in the Arrangement, use `arrangement.delete`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.delete_envelope`

**Clear Envelope**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Deletes a clip's envelope for a parameter, as Clear Envelope in the Envelopes tab does: the parameter goes back to what it does without the clip envelope. `clip` and `target` name the envelope as `clip.set_envelope_breakpoint` does. Nothing changes if the clip has no envelope for it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter of the clip's track. |
| `kind` | [`EnvelopeKind`](#envelopekind) | no | Which of the clip's envelopes for the parameter: `modulation` (the default) or a Session clip's `automation`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.delete_envelope_breakpoint`

**Delete Envelope Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Deletes one of a clip envelope's breakpoints, so the segments either side of it become the one starting at the breakpoint before it, as clicking a breakpoint in the Envelopes tab does. `clip` and `target` name the envelope as `clip.set_envelope_breakpoint` does, and `at` is where the breakpoint is. Deleting the last one takes the envelope with it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter of the clip's track. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the breakpoint is. |
| `kind` | [`EnvelopeKind`](#envelopekind) | no | Which of the clip's envelopes for the parameter: `modulation` (the default) or a Session clip's `automation`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.delete_transients`

**Delete Transients**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Takes transients out of an audio clip: `times` are their times in the file, in seconds, as `clip.transients` lists them. A transient put in by hand is forgotten; a detected one is noted as taken away and stays away until `clip.reset_transients`. Refused for a time that is none of the clip's transients, once the file's analysis is ready. One undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SAMPLE-012 | `Cmd+Shift+Delete` | `Ctrl+Shift+Delete` | `sample-editor` | Delete the selected transient | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `times` | array of number | yes | The transients to take out, by their times in the file as `clip.transients` lists them. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.delete_warp_markers`

**Delete Warp Markers**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Deletes the warp markers named in `markers` (their place in the map, the first being 0) of each of the warped audio clips `clips`, which must hold files of the same length: the segments either side of each join into one straight segment. Deleting the last marker leaves the audio after the new last one at the clip's tempo. A warped clip keeps at least one marker: deleting them all is refused.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SAMPLE-010 | `Delete` | `Delete` | `sample-editor` | Delete the selected warp marker | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped audio clips: their files must be as long as each other's. |
| `markers` | array of integer, at least 0 | yes | The markers to delete, by their place in the map, the first being 0. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.duplicate_loop`

**Duplicate Loop**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `loop-brace`.

Doubles the loop brace of each MIDI clip (`clips`, or the clips of the selected loop bars, or the clip shown) and copies the notes inside it into the new half; notes after the loop's end move later with it, keeping their distance from the end. Cmd-D (Ctrl-D) with the loop brace or loop bars selected, and Duplicate in a loop bar's menu, run it. A clip whose loop would reach past the clip's end is refused. One undo step, named Duplicate Loop.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-LOOP-012 | `Cmd+D` | `Ctrl+D` | `loop-brace` | Duplicate Loop: double the loop and copy its notes into the new half | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array or null | no | The MIDI clips. Left out, the clips of the selected loop bars, or the clip shown. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `clip.edit_sample`

**Edit Sample**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Opens an audio clip's file in the external sample editor, as the Edit button in the Clip View's Audio Utilities panel does: the editor the File & Folder page's Sample Editor row names, or that page itself when it names none. The file's content is checked when Beatlayer comes to the front again: if it has changed, every clip of the set that played the old file plays the new one, in one undo step, each keeping its warp markers only if the file kept its length. Opens a program outside the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The audio clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |

Result: [`EditedSample`](#editedsample).

#### `clip.insert_transient`

**Insert Transient**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Puts a transient into an audio clip at `time`, seconds in its file: Insert Transient, at the Sample Editor's insert marker when the app runs it. Putting one where a detected transient was taken away brings that one back. The edit belongs to the clip, is saved with the set, and shows in `clip.transients`. One undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SAMPLE-011 | `Cmd+Shift+I` | `Ctrl+Shift+I` | `sample-editor` | Insert a transient | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `time` | number, at least 0 | yes | The time in the file, in seconds. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.insert_warp_marker`

**Insert Warp Marker**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Adds a warp marker to each of the warped audio clips `clips`, which must hold files of the same length: at a `beat` of the clip's contents (ticks from its 1.1.1, negative before it), at the time in the file the map already places there, or at a `time` in the file (seconds), on the beat the map already places it. Give one of the two. Nothing moves; the audio either side stays where it is. Inserting where a marker is already changes nothing. Markers are named by their place in the map (`data.audio.warp_markers`), the first being 0. The edit is made to every clip in one undo step, or to none if it's refused for one. With `pin_neighbours` (Cmd or Ctrl held on a pseudo-warp marker) it also puts markers at the transients just before and just after the new one, read from the clip's transients (`clip.transients`) unless `transients` lists them; it works on one clip.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SAMPLE-009 | `Cmd+I` | `Ctrl+I` | `sample-editor` | Insert a warp marker | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped audio clips: their files must be as long as each other's. |
| `beat` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The beat, in ticks from the clip's 1.1.1, to put the marker on, at the time in the file the map already places there. Give this or `time`. |
| `pin_neighbours` | boolean | no | Also put markers at the transients either side of the new one (WP-4.3): Cmd (Ctrl) held on a pseudo-warp marker. Needs one clip. |
| `time` | number or null | no | The time in the file, in seconds, to put the marker at, on the beat the map already places it. Give this or `beat`. |
| `transients` | array or null | no | The clip's transients, as times in the file, that `pin_neighbours` looks among. Left out, the app uses the clip's current ones. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.insert_warp_markers`

**Insert Warp Markers**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Puts warp markers in a range of a warped audio clip's contents, `from` to `to` (ticks from the clip's 1.1.1): at every transient of the clip in the range, or, when it holds none, at its start and its end. The transients are the clip's own (`clip.transients`) unless `transients` lists times in the file. Each marker sits on the beat the map already places its time, so nothing moves; a marker already there is left. Refused for a clip that isn't warped, or while the file's analysis is not ready and `transients` is left out. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped audio clip. |
| `from` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | The start of the range, in ticks from the clip's 1.1.1. |
| `to` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | The end of the range, in ticks, after `from`. |
| `transients` | array or null | no | The clip's transients, as times in the file, that the range is searched for. Left out, the app uses the clip's current ones. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.move`

**Move Clip**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves a clip so it starts at `start`, on the same track or another track of the same kind (audio or MIDI). Its length and contents don't change. To move several clips together, use `clip.move_by`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track it moves to. |
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Its new start. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.move_by`

**Move Clips**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves several clips earlier or later by the same number of ticks, keeping them on their tracks and keeping their spacing; a negative `by` moves them earlier. Either every clip moves or, if any would start before 0, none does. List each clip once.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clips, each listed once. |
| `by` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How far to move them; negative moves them earlier. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.move_envelope_breakpoint`

**Move Envelope Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Moves one of a clip envelope's breakpoints from `at` to `to`, as dragging it in the Envelopes tab does. `clip` and `target` name the envelope as `clip.set_envelope_breakpoint` does. `to` is 0 or later, and not where another breakpoint of the same envelope already is. `value` gives the breakpoint a new value in the parameter's own units; left out, it keeps the one it has.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter of the clip's track. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the breakpoint is now. |
| `to` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where it goes: 0 or later, and not where another breakpoint of the same envelope already is. |
| `kind` | [`EnvelopeKind`](#envelopekind) | no | Which of the clip's envelopes for the parameter: `modulation` (the default) or a Session clip's `automation`. |
| `value` | number or null | no | The value it takes there, in the parameter's own units, or `null` (or nothing) to keep the value it has. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.move_to_lane`

**Move Clip to Lane**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves a clip so it starts at `start` on the main lane of `track`, or, with `lane`, on that take lane of the track, out of the lane or Session slot it sat in. The track must be an audio or MIDI track of the clip's kind. It does not clear what the destination holds there; to move clips as the Arrangement does, replacing what they land on, use `arrangement.move_clips`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track it moves to. |
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Its new start. |
| `lane` | [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) or null | no | The take lane it moves to; the track's main lane when left out. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.move_to_slot`

**Move Clip to Slot**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Moves a clip into a track's Session slot at `scene`, out of the slot or the Arrangement lane it sits in, as dragging a clip between slots does. The target slot must be empty, unless it's the clip's own slot, and the clip's data must match the track. A slot clip has no position in the Arrangement: it arrives with its start at 0.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track whose slot it goes in. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it goes in. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.move_transient`

**Move Transient**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Moves the transient at `from` (seconds in the file, as `clip.transients` lists it) to `to`, as Shift-dragging a pseudo-warp marker does. It changes no audio and no warp marker. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `from` | number, at least 0 | yes | The transient's time in the file, in seconds, as `clip.transients` lists it. |
| `to` | number, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes, in seconds. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.move_warp_markers`

**Move Warp Markers**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Moves the warp markers named in `markers` (their place in the map, the first being 0) of each of the warped audio clips `clips`, which must hold files of the same length, by the same number of ticks `by` (negative moves them earlier). Each keeps its time in the file, so the audio either side of it stretches or squeezes to fit. Refused, changing nothing, if a marker would pass or reach a neighbour that isn't moving with it. Moving the last marker sets the clip's tempo to the new last segment's, so the audio after it carries on at that speed.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped audio clips: their files must be as long as each other's. |
| `markers` | array of integer, at least 0 | yes | The markers to move, by their place in the map, the first being 0. |
| `by` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How far to move them, in ticks: negative moves them earlier. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.open_slice_dialog`

**Slice to New MIDI Track**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`, `session`, `clip-view`.

Opens the Slice to New MIDI Track dialog for an audio clip (`clip`, or the one audio clip selected in either view). The dialog holds the Slice By chooser (the beat divisions, Transients, and Warp Markers), the Slicing Preset chooser, and Preserve warped timing, and its OK runs `clip.slice_to_midi_track`. Changes nothing in the set: an agent calls `clip.slice_to_midi_track` instead.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The audio clip to slice. Left out, the one audio clip selected in either view. |

Result: [`SliceDialogStatus`](#slicedialogstatus).

#### `clip.quantize_audio`

**Quantize**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Quantises a warped audio clip: for each line of the quantise grid inside the time selection (`from` to `to` in ticks from 1.1.1, or the whole clip with none), the clip's transient nearest that line, if one lies within half a grid step of it, gets a warp marker at its time in the file (made if there is none) and moves `amount` percent of the way to the line, keeping its time in the file. Transients nearest no line get no marker. `grid` is the spacing between grid lines in ticks; left out, it uses the Clip View's Quantize settings (`clip_view.quantize_settings`), which follow the editing grid until a grid is set. `amount` is from 0 to 100 percent (left out, the settings' amount). 100 percent lands each on its line; 0 changes nothing and is no undo step; otherwise it is one undo step. Refuses an unwarped clip.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SAMPLE-001 | `Cmd+U` | `Ctrl+U` | `sample-editor` | Quantise the selection | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | integer or null | no | How far each warp marker moves toward its grid line, from 0 to 100 percent. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The audio clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |
| `from` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The start of the time selection, in ticks from the clip's 1.1.1. Left out, the clip's start. |
| `grid` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The grid line spacing in ticks, over the Quantize settings. |
| `to` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The end of the time selection, in ticks from the clip's 1.1.1. Left out, the clip's end. |
| `transients` | array or null | no | The transient times in the file in seconds to use over the clip's analysis. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `clip.rename`

**Rename Clip**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Renames a clip. A name may be empty. It changes only the name shown on the clip.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-008 | `Cmd+R` | `Ctrl+R` | `global` | Rename the selection | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The new name. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | no | The clip. |
| `clips` | array of integer, at least 1 or object | no | Clips to make the same change to, as one undo step, in place of `clip`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.replace_sample`

**Replace Sample**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Replaces an audio clip's file with the file at `path`, as dropping a file from the browser on the Clip View does: the clip keeps its gain and pitch, and its warp markers only if the new file is exactly as long as the old one. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The file the clip plays instead. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The audio clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |

Result: [`ReplacedSample`](#replacedsample).

#### `clip.reset_transients`

**Reset Transients**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Takes away all of an audio clip's transient edits: the transients put in by hand go, and the detected ones that were taken away come back. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.reverse`

**Reverse Clip**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `session`, `clip-view`.

Gives an audio clip a backwards copy of its file: the copy is written through the processed-file writer, and the clip plays it, with its Start and End markers, loop brace and warp markers mirrored about the file, so it plays the same stretch of sound backwards. The clip's envelopes stay where they are, and its loop switch, gain, transpose, detune, warp mode and fades don't change. Reversing a clip whose file is already a reversed copy gives it back the file it was made from, writing nothing. `clip` names the clip (left out, the selected one). A MIDI clip isn't reversed, and nothing changes.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The clip to reverse. Left out, the one clip the Arrangement or the Session View has selected. |

Result: [`ReverseResult`](#reverseresult).

#### `clip.reverse_file`

**Reverse Clip**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Reverses an audio clip's file: the clip plays `media`, a reversed copy of its file, with its Start and End markers, loop brace and warp markers mirrored about the file, so it plays the same stretch of sound backwards. Its clip envelopes stay where they are, and its loop switch, gain, transpose, detune, warp mode and fades don't change. `seconds` is the length of the file the markers are mirrored about. `clip.reverse` is the command a person and an agent run: it writes the new file through the processed-file writer and applies this one.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `seconds` | number | yes | The length of the file in seconds, which the markers are mirrored about. |
| `media` | [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) or null | no | The file it plays now: the reversed copy. `null` (or nothing) leaves the file as it is, for a clip whose file is already a reversed copy and goes back to the one it was made from. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.save_default`

**Save Default Clip**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Saves an audio clip's Warp switch, warp markers and tempo, warp mode and mode controls (which hold its Transpose and Detune), and gain as its file's defaults, as the Save button in the clip's title bar does: into a small file of Beatlayer's own, `<sample file name>.beatlayer-clip`, beside the sample, so the defaults travel with it, replacing any saved before. A clip made from the file afterwards (dropped from the browser, loaded with Enter or imported) starts with them and is not auto-warped; clips already in the set don't change. Fails with the reason, and writes nothing, if the folder can't be written or the clip's file isn't known. Changes nothing in the set and is no undo step; writes a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |

Result: [`SavedDefaults`](#saveddefaults).

#### `clip.save_file`

**Save Clip as File**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `browser`, `session`.

Saves a clip from the Arrangement or a Session slot as a clip file (`.blclip`) in `folder` (the User Library's `Clips` folder if left out), as dragging the clip onto a folder in the browser does. The file keeps the clip as the set saves it (its notes or its warp markers, envelopes and launch settings) and the devices of its track with their state. It is named `name`, the clip's name, or its track's when the clip has none, with " 2", " 3" added for a name already taken, and written whole or not at all. The audio the clip and the devices play is copied into the `Samples/Imported` folder of the project the file lands in or left where it is, as Collect Files on Export says (`settings.state`'s `library.collect_files_on_export`); under Ask, `copy` answers for the person and leaving it out refuses the command. The new row is selected with its name open for editing (`browser.state`'s `renaming`; `browser.rename_file` finishes it). Changes nothing in the set. Writes files outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip to save: one in the Arrangement or in a Session slot. |
| `copy` | boolean or null | no | Answers Collect Files on Export when it is set to Ask: `true` copies the audio files the clip and its track's devices play, `false` leaves the clip file naming them where they are. Under Always and Never it is ignored; under Ask, leaving it out refuses the command. |
| `folder` | string or null | no | The folder to save it in. Left out, the User Library's `Clips` folder. |
| `name` | string or null | no | The file's name, without the extension. Left out, the clip's name, or its track's when the clip has none. A name already taken in the folder gets " 2", " 3" and so on. |

Result: [`SaveClipFileResult`](#saveclipfileresult).

#### `clip.scale_tempo`

**Scale Clip Tempo**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Multiplies every segment's tempo and the clip's own tempo of a warped audio clip by `factor`: 2 is Live's ×2 and 0.5 its ÷2, which correct a tempo found at half or double. Each marker's distance in ticks from the first marker is multiplied by it, and the Start and End markers and loop brace move with them about the first marker, so each keeps its place in the audio. The clip's place and length in the arrangement don't change. Refused if the clip's tempo would leave 1 to 1,000 BPM.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped audio clip. |
| `factor` | number | yes | What to multiply by: 2 for ×2, 0.5 for ÷2. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.select_envelope_breakpoint`

**Select Envelope Breakpoint**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `envelope`.

Selects a breakpoint of a clip's envelope in the Clip View's Envelope Editor, as `automation.select_breakpoint` does in an automation lane: the insert marker moves to it, and an edit begins that ends when the selection is cleared with `at` `null` or the focus leaves; every change in between is one undo step. `clip_view.state` reports the selection. Changes nothing in the set itself.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip whose envelope holds the breakpoint. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter of the clip's track the envelope modulates. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The position of the breakpoint to select, in ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents, or `null` to keep the edit and select none. |

Result: [`EnvelopeKeyState`](#envelopekeystate).

#### `clip.set_1_1_1_here`

**Set 1.1.1 Here**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Makes a point of a warped audio clip's file its 1.1.1, the downbeat of its first bar: at the selected warp marker (`marker`, its place in the map, the first being 0) or at the Sample Editor's insert marker (`beat`, ticks from the clip's current 1.1.1, or `time`, seconds in the file); give one of the three. A warp marker is made there if there was none. Every marker, the End marker and the loop brace then move by the same ticks, so no segment changes tempo and each keeps its place in the audio, and the Start marker goes to 1.1.1. Refused for a clip that isn't warped, or if the End marker or the loop brace would end up before 1.1.1. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped audio clip. |
| `beat` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The Sample Editor's insert marker as a beat, in ticks from the clip's 1.1.1: a warp marker is made there, at the time the map already places it. |
| `marker` | integer or null | no | The selected warp marker, by its place in the map, the first being 0. |
| `time` | number or null | no | The insert marker as a time in the file, in seconds: a warp marker is made there, on the beat the map already places it. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_data`

**Replace Clip Contents**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Replaces what a clip plays: for an audio clip, the audio file it names by content hash with all its settings at once; for a MIDI clip, its whole list of notes. Use it to write or change a MIDI clip's notes, sending every note the clip should hold; for one setting of an audio clip, the `clip.set_region`, `clip.set_loop`, `clip.set_gain`, and `clip.set_fades` commands are simpler. The data must match the clip's track: audio on audio tracks, MIDI on MIDI tracks. Sending fewer notes than a MIDI clip has deletes notes, which is destructive, so an agent asks first; adding notes or keeping their count isn't.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `data` | [`ClipData`](#clipdata) | yes | The new data. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_envelope_breakpoint`

**Add Envelope Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Sets the value of one of a clip's envelopes at a position, adding a breakpoint there or replacing the one that's there, as clicking or dragging a breakpoint in the Envelopes tab does. `clip` is the clip, `target` the parameter of the clip's track the envelope modulates (a control of its mixer, one of its sends, or a parameter of a device in its chain; an audio clip's can instead be one of its sound settings, `{"type": "clip", "param": "transpose"}`, whose value is a share from 0 to 100 for `gain` and otherwise an amount added to the setting, in its own units), `at` the position in ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents, and `value` the value there, in the parameter's own units. A MIDI clip's `target` can instead be a MIDI controller (MIDI Ctrl in the Envelopes tab): `{"type": "midi.cc", "number": 1}` (a controller from 1 to 31 or 33 to 119, value 0 to 127), `{"type": "midi.pitch_bend"}` (-8192 to 8191, 0 at rest) or `{"type": "midi.channel_pressure"}` (0 to 127); the value is the message the clip sends to its track's devices while it plays, on any channel. A parameter with no clip envelope gets one, linked to the clip, with this breakpoint as its first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter of the clip's track the envelope modulates: a control of its mixer, one of its sends, or a parameter of a device in its chain; or, in a MIDI clip, a MIDI controller (`midi.cc`, `midi.pitch_bend` or `midi.channel_pressure`). |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the breakpoint sits, in ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents, as a note's start is: 0 or later. |
| `value` | number | yes | The value there, in the parameter's own units; a MIDI controller's own range (0 to 127, pitch bend -8192 to 8191). |
| `kind` | [`EnvelopeKind`](#envelopekind) | no | Which of the clip's envelopes for the parameter: `modulation` (the default) or a Session clip's `automation`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_envelope_curve`

**Curve Envelope Segment**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Curves the segment starting at one of a clip envelope's breakpoints, as holding Alt (Windows) or Option (macOS) while dragging a segment in the Envelopes tab does. `clip` and `target` name the envelope as `clip.set_envelope_breakpoint` does, `at` is the breakpoint the segment starts at, and `bend` is from -1 to 1: 0 makes the segment a straight line again, and the sign chooses which side it bows to.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter of the clip's track. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the segment starts: the breakpoint there. |
| `bend` | number | yes | The bend, from −1 to 1: 0 is the straight line, and the sign chooses which side the segment bows to. |
| `kind` | [`EnvelopeKind`](#envelopekind) | no | Which of the clip's envelopes for the parameter: `modulation` (the default) or a Session clip's `automation`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_envelope_linked`

**Link Envelope**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Switches a clip envelope's Linked switch: linked (`true`, the default), it follows the clip's region and loop, playing what the clip's contents play; unlinked, it plays once from the clip's start, one tick per tick, for as long as the clip lasts. `clip` and `target` name the envelope as `clip.set_envelope_breakpoint` does; a target with no envelope gets an empty linked one, so a switch thrown before anything is drawn sets what drawing will use.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter of the clip's track. |
| `linked` | boolean | yes | Whether the envelope follows the clip's timeline. |
| `kind` | [`EnvelopeKind`](#envelopekind) | no | Which of the clip's envelopes for the parameter: `modulation` (the default) or a Session clip's `automation`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_fades`

**Set Clip Fades**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Sets the lengths, in seconds, of an audio clip's fade-in, from silence at the clip's start in the arrangement, and its fade-out, to silence at its end; 0 is no fade. `fade_in_curve` and `fade_out_curve`, from -1 to 1, shape each: 0, the default, is a straight line in amplitude, a positive curve bows the fade towards full level and a negative one towards silence; left out, a curve stays as it is. Short fades stop a clip that starts or ends mid-waveform from clicking: 0.004 (4 ms) is the length that Create Fades on Clip Edges gives new clips. Lengths must be finite, at least 0 and within the clip's limits: a fade-in ends no later than the fade-out begins, and a fade takes in no point where the clip goes round its loop brace. Where a crossfade begins or ends at the clip, this sets the crossfade's part inside the clip and its curve, and the clip it meets follows; if it can't (its file doesn't reach back that far), the crossfade ends and each clip keeps its own fade. Read the result back with the query tool's `clip` field `data` and the clip's `fade_in_before` and `fade_out_after`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `fade_in` | number, at least 0 | yes | The fade-in's length in seconds from the clip's start: 0 for none. Where a crossfade begins at the clip's start, this is how far past the start it runs. |
| `fade_out` | number, at least 0 | yes | The fade-out's length in seconds up to the clip's end: 0 for none. Where a crossfade ends at the clip's end, this is how far before the end it begins. |
| `fade_in_curve` | number or null | no | The fade-in's curve, from −1 to 1: 0 is a straight line, a positive curve bows towards full level and a negative one towards silence. Left out, the curve stays as it is. |
| `fade_out_curve` | number or null | no | The fade-out's curve, from −1 to 1. Left out, the curve stays as it is. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_follow_actions`

**Set Clip Follow Actions**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Changes a Session clip's follow actions, as the Launch Properties panel does (`clip` is the ID of a clip that sits in a slot). `enabled` is the Follow Action switch; `action_a` and `action_b` are one of `no_action`, `stop`, `play_again`, `previous`, `next`, `first`, `last`, `any`, `other` and `jump`; `chance_a` is action A's chance in whole percent, 0 to 100, and action B has the rest; `jump_a` and `jump_b` are the slot (scene) numbers Jump goes to, 1 up to the number of scenes, and 0 for none, where Jump stops the clip; `linked` is Linked: the follow time is the multiplier times the clip's loop, or the clip's end when its Loop switch is off; Unlinked: `time`; `multiplier` is the Linked multiplier, a whole number from 1; and `time` is the Unlinked follow time in ticks, from a sixteenth (a bar is 2822400 ticks in 4/4). Fields left out stay as they are, and a number past its limit is held at the limit. One undo step. The defaults are off, A Next, B No Action, 100 %, Linked, 1x, one bar. While the song plays the action runs when the follow time has passed after the clip started, and the global switch (`session.set_follow_actions_enabled`) must be on.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip, which sits in a Session slot. |
| `action_a` | [`FollowAction`](#followaction) or null | no | Action A. |
| `action_b` | [`FollowAction`](#followaction) or null | no | Action B. |
| `chance_a` | integer or null | no | The chance of action A in whole percent, 0 to 100; B has the rest. |
| `enabled` | boolean or null | no | The Follow Action switch. |
| `jump_a` | integer or null | no | The slot (scene) number action A's Jump goes to: 1 up to the number of scenes, and 0 for none. |
| `jump_b` | integer or null | no | The slot (scene) number action B's Jump goes to. |
| `linked` | boolean or null | no | Linked (on a scene, Longest) or Unlinked. |
| `multiplier` | integer or null | no | The Linked multiplier, a whole number from 1. |
| `time` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The Unlinked follow time in ticks, from a sixteenth. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_gain`

**Set Clip Gain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Sets an audio clip's gain as a linear gain: 1 is 0 dB (where every clip starts), 0.5 is about -6 dB (10^(dB/20) converts decibels), 2 is about +6 dB, and 0 is silence (-inf dB). Use it to balance one clip against others on its track; to change the whole track, use `mixer.set_volume`. The value must be finite and at least 0.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `gain` | number, at least 0 | yes | The gain: 1 is 0 dB, 0.5 about −6 dB, and 0 silence. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_groove`

**Set Clip Groove**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `clip-view`.

Sets the Clip Groove of MIDI or audio clips to a groove of the Groove Pool (`groove`), or to none when `groove` is left out. `clips` names the clips; left out, the selected ones are set. The groove changes when a clip's notes play and how loud, or where its audio plays, and changes nothing in the clip until `groove.commit`; an audio clip plays its groove only while it is warped. One undo step, `Change Clip Groove`, however many clips it sets.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | no | The clips; left out, the ones selected. |
| `groove` | [`GrooveId`](#grooveid) or null | no | The groove; left out, none. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_high_quality`

**Set Clip High Quality**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Switches an audio clip's high-quality interpolation (`data.audio.high_quality`, on for a new clip). On, the clip is resampled by a band-limited interpolator wherever it is read at a rate other than 1, as Re-Pitch does at any speed but 1, at more CPU and with less distortion; off, by a cheaper one. Where no resampling happens it changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `high_quality` | boolean | yes | Whether the clip is resampled by the band-limited interpolator. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_launch_mode`

**Set Clip Launch Mode**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Sets what a press and a release of a Session clip's launch button do (a clip that sits in a slot; `clip` is its ID): `trigger` (the default) starts the clip on the launch grid and it plays on, a second press restarts it; `gate` starts it on a press and stops it on the grid after the release; `toggle` starts it on a press and the next press stops it on the grid; `repeat` starts it on a press and restarts it every launch quantisation step while the press lasts, then stops it on the grid after the release. A new clip starts with the Default Launch Mode setting. The mode is read at each press and release, so changing it doesn't touch a clip that is playing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `mode` | [`LaunchMode`](#launchmode) | yes | What a press and a release of its launch button do. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_launch_quantization`

**Set Clip Launch Quantization**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Sets a Session clip's own launch quantisation, the grid its launches wait for: one of the global quantisation's steps (`none`, `8_bars`, `4_bars`, `2_bars`, `1_bar`, `half`, `half_triplet`, `quarter`, `quarter_triplet`, `eighth`, `eighth_triplet`, `sixteenth`, `sixteenth_triplet`, `thirty_second`), or `null` (the default, Live's "Global") to follow the global quantisation. `clip` is the ID of a clip that sits in a slot. The setting is saved with the clip and is one undo step; launching doesn't read it yet.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip, which sits in a Session slot. |
| `quantization` | [`LaunchQuantization`](#launchquantization) or null | no | The step the clip's launches wait for; `null` (or nothing) follows the global quantisation, Live's "Global". |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_legato`

**Set Clip Legato**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Switches Legato on or off for a Session clip, one that sits in a slot (`clip` is its ID). A Legato clip takes over the play position of the clip playing on its track when it launches, so the two stay in sync. Off is the default. The setting is saved with the clip and is one undo step; launching doesn't read it yet.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip, which sits in a Session slot. |
| `legato` | boolean | yes | Whether Legato is on. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_length`

**Resize Clip**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Changes how long a clip is, in ticks, keeping its start and its contents. The length must be positive.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | The new length. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_loop`

**Set Clip Loop**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Moves an audio clip's loop brace, in seconds into its audio file for an unwarped clip or in ticks of its contents (`ticks` true) for a warped one (a command in the other form is refused; `end` `null` for the end of the file), as the Clip View's loop Position and Length fields do. It doesn't switch the loop on or off: use `clip.set_loop_enabled`. While the loop is on, the clip plays from its Start marker into the brace, then repeats the brace until the clip ends in the arrangement; make the clip longer with `clip.set_length` to hear more repeats. A new clip's brace is the whole file.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `start` | number | yes | Where the brace starts, in seconds into the file: 0 or more. A warped clip's is whole ticks of its contents (`ticks` true). |
| `end` | number or null | no | Where it ends, in seconds into the file, after `start`; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the file. |
| `ticks` | boolean | no | Whether `start` and `end` are ticks of a warped clip's contents instead of seconds in the file of an unwarped one: they must be the form the clip shows. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_loop_enabled`

**Clip Loop On/Off**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Switches an audio or MIDI clip's Loop switch on or off, leaving its loop brace where it is. On, the clip repeats its brace (`clip.set_loop` or `clip.set_midi_loop`) for as long as it lasts in the arrangement; off, it plays from its Start marker to its End marker once. The Start marker must be before the brace's end to switch it on. An audio clip can only loop while Warp is on (`clip.set_warp`): switching the loop on for an unwarped audio clip is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether the clip repeats its loop brace. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | no | The clip. |
| `clips` | array of integer, at least 1 or object | no | Clips to make the same change to, as one undo step, in place of `clip`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_midi_loop`

**Set MIDI Clip Loop**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Moves a MIDI clip's loop brace, in ticks from the clip's beginning (`end` `null` for the end of the clip), as the Clip View's loop Position and Length fields do. It doesn't switch the loop on or off: use `clip.set_loop_enabled`. While the loop is on, the clip plays from its Start marker into the brace, then repeats the brace until the clip ends in the arrangement; make the clip longer with `clip.set_length` to hear more repeats.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the brace starts, in ticks from the clip's beginning. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | no | The MIDI clip. |
| `clips` | array of integer, at least 1 or object | no | Clips to make the same change to, as one undo step, in place of `clip`. |
| `end` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | Where it ends, in ticks, after `start`; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the clip. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_midi_region`

**Set MIDI Clip Start and End**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Moves a MIDI clip's Start and End markers, in ticks from the clip's beginning: the clip starts playing at `start` when the song reaches the clip, and, while its loop is off, plays until `end` (`null` for the end of the clip) or the clip's own end in the arrangement, whichever comes first, then is silent. While the loop is on, `start` must be before the loop's end. Use `clip.set_length` to change how long the clip lasts in the arrangement.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The MIDI clip. |
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | The Start marker, in ticks from the clip's beginning. |
| `end` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The End marker, in ticks from the clip's beginning, after `start`; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the clip. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_mute`

**Activate/Deactivate Clip**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Switches a clip's activator: `mute` true deactivates the clip, so it stays in place but doesn't play, and false activates it again.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-027 | `0` | `0` | `arrangement` | Deactivate the selection | toggles `mute` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mute` | boolean | yes | Whether it's muted. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | no | The clip. |
| `clips` | array of integer, at least 1 or object | no | Clips to make the same change to, as one undo step, in place of `clip`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_pitch`

**Set Clip Pitch**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Sets an audio clip's pitch: `transpose`, in whole semitones from -48 to 48, and `detune`, in cents from -50 to 50 (`data.audio.transpose` and `data.audio.detune`; a new clip has neither). Give either of them, or both, in one undo step; a value out of range refuses the whole command. The clip's pitch moves by the sum, and its timing stays with its warp map. In Re-Pitch the two are drawn switched off and don't act, and their values stay with the clip. With Warp off the clip's speed changes with its pitch, as a tape running faster does.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `detune` | number or null | no | The Detune, in cents, from −50 to 50. |
| `transpose` | integer or null | no | The Transpose, in whole semitones, from −48 to 48. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_ram_mode`

**Set Clip RAM Mode**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Switches an audio clip's RAM mode (`data.audio.ram`, off for a new clip). On, the clip's whole file is held in memory instead of streamed from disk, so it never underruns; the audio it plays is the same. Switching it while the clip plays leaves no gap.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `ram` | boolean | yes | Whether the clip's whole file is held in memory. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_region`

**Set Clip Start and End**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Moves an audio clip's Start and End markers: the clip starts playing at `start` when the song reaches the clip, and, while its loop is off, plays until `end` (`null` for the end of the file) or the clip's own end in the arrangement, whichever comes first, then is silent. An unwarped clip plays at its file's own speed and its positions are seconds into the file (`ticks` false, the default). A warped clip (`clip.set_warp`) follows the set's tempo and its positions are ticks of its contents, from the clip's 1.1.1, with `ticks` true; a command in the other form is refused. While the loop is on, `start` must be before the loop's end. Use `clip.set_length` to change how long the clip lasts in the arrangement.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `start` | number | yes | The Start marker, in seconds into the file: 0 or more. While the loop is on, it must be before the loop brace's end. A warped clip's is whole ticks of its contents (`ticks` true). |
| `end` | number or null | no | The End marker, in seconds into the file, after `start`; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the file. |
| `ticks` | boolean | no | Whether `start` and `end` are ticks of a warped clip's contents instead of seconds in the file of an unwarped one: they must be the form the clip shows. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_scale`

**Set Clip Scale**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `clip-view`.

Sets a clip's scale: whether its Scale Mode is on (`enabled`), its root note (`root`, 0 is C and 11 is B) and its scale (`name`, one of the names `song.scales` reads). `clips` names the clips to set; left out, the selected ones are set. It leaves the values it isn't given as they were, and it is one undo step, named "Change Clip Scale", however many clips it sets. A scale the list doesn't hold, or a root outside C to B, is refused and nothing changes. A clip's scale never changes what it plays: it tells the rest of the set which keys belong.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clips. |
| `enabled` | boolean or null | no | Whether the clips' Scale Mode is on. |
| `name` | string or null | no | The scale's name, from the scale list. |
| `root` | integer or null | no | The root note: 0 (C) to 11 (B). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_segment_bpm`

**Set Warp Segment BPM**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Sets a warped audio clip's BPM field. With `marker` (its place in the map, the first being 0), `bpm` is the tempo of the segment that starts at that marker: every later marker moves by the same number of ticks, so that segment alone changes and each later one keeps its tempo; for the last marker it is the clip's own tempo, from 1 to 1,000. Without `marker`, `bpm` is the first segment's tempo (the clip's when there's one marker) and every tempo of the clip scales by the same factor, as `clip.scale_tempo` does.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped audio clip. |
| `bpm` | number | yes | The tempo in BPM: positive, and from 1 to 1,000 for the clip's. |
| `marker` | integer or null | no | The marker whose segment to set, by its place in the map, the first being 0: `null` (or nothing) for the first segment's tempo, which scales every segment. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_signature`

**Set MIDI Clip Signature**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Sets a MIDI clip's time signature, as the Clip View's Signature fields do; `signature` `null` makes the clip follow the song's signature at its position.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | no | The MIDI clip. |
| `clips` | array of integer, at least 1 or object | no | Clips to make the same change to, as one undo step, in place of `clip`. |
| `signature` | [`TimeSignature`](#timesignature) or null | no | The clip's signature; `null` (or nothing) follows the song's at the clip's position. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_tempo_leader`

**Switch Lead/Follow**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Switches a warped Arrangement clip's Lead/Follow switch (`data.audio.tempo_leader`, off for a new clip). Set to Lead, the set takes its tempo from the clip's warp markers over the clip's span and the clip plays as if unwarped, while the Control Bar's tempo field is off and the tempo commands are refused there; every other clip follows that tempo. Any number of clips may lead, and where leaders overlap the one on the track lowest in the track list sets the tempo. Refused for a Session clip and for an unwarped clip; switching a leader's Warp off makes it a follower in the same undo step. `song.unfollow_tempo_automation` makes every leader a follower.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped Arrangement audio clip. |
| `leader` | boolean | yes | Whether the clip leads, or follows, the set's tempo. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_velocity_amount`

**Set Clip Velocity Amount**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Sets how much the velocity of the MIDI note that launches a Session clip changes the clip's volume: `amount` is from 0 (no influence, the default) to 1 (100 %, where the softest note plays the clip silently). `clip` is the ID of a clip that sits in a slot. The setting is saved with the clip and is one undo step; launching doesn't read it yet.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip, which sits in a Session slot. |
| `amount` | number from 0 to 1 | yes | 0 for no influence, up to 1 for 100 %. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_warp`

**Clip Warp On/Off**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Switches an audio clip's Warp on or off. Off, the clip plays at its file's own speed whatever the set's tempo, and its Start and End markers and loop brace are seconds into the file. On, it follows the set's tempo through its warp map (`data.audio.warp_markers`: each pairs a time in the file with a beat, in ticks from the clip's 1.1.1, and `data.audio.tempo` is the speed of the file after the last marker), and its markers and brace are ticks of its contents. Switching on a clip that has no map gives it one marker at its Start marker on 1.1.1, at the set's tempo there, so it goes on playing at the speed it did; switching off keeps the map. Either way the markers and brace convert, so each keeps its place in the audio, and the clip keeps its place and length in the arrangement. A warped clip plays through its warp map at the set's tempo, in its warp mode (`clip.set_warp_mode`); only a warped clip can loop, so switching Warp off also switches the clip's loop off in the same undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `warp` | boolean | yes | Whether the clip follows the set's tempo through its warp map. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_warp_mode`

**Set Warp Mode**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Sets how a warped audio clip's audio is fitted to the speed its warp map sets: `beats`, `tones`, `texture`, `re_pitch`, `complex` or `complex_pro` (`data.audio.warp_mode`; a new clip is `beats`). `re_pitch` plays the file faster or slower, so its pitch moves with the speed. An unwarped clip keeps its mode for when Warp goes back on, and every mode's controls stay with the clip. Until the other modes are built, they play as `re_pitch` does.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `mode` | [`WarpMode`](#warpmode) | yes | The mode: Beats, Tones, Texture, Re-Pitch, Complex or Complex Pro. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.set_warp_settings`

**Set Warp Settings**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Sets controls of an audio clip's warp modes, named by mode, any of them in one undo step (`data.audio.warp_settings`; a control at its default isn't listed there). `beats`: `preserve` (`transients`, `1_bar`, `half`, `quarter`, `eighth`, `sixteenth`, `thirty_second`), `transient_loop_mode` (`loop_off`, `loop_forward`, `loop_back_and_forth`), `transient_envelope` (0 to 100, default 100). `tones`: `grain_size` (10 to 100 ms, default 30). `texture`: `grain_size` (10 to 500 ms, default 65), `flux` (0 to 100 %, default 25). `complex_pro`: `formants` (0 to 100 %, default 100), `envelope` (8 to 512, default 128). Give at least one control; a value out of range refuses the whole command.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |
| `beats` | [`BeatsUpdate`](#beatsupdate) or null | no | Beats' controls to change. |
| `complex_pro` | [`ComplexProUpdate`](#complexproupdate) or null | no | Complex Pro's controls to change. |
| `texture` | [`TextureUpdate`](#textureupdate) or null | no | Texture's controls to change. |
| `tones` | [`TonesUpdate`](#tonesupdate) or null | no | Tones' controls to change. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.shift_warp_marker`

**Shift Warp Marker**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Moves the time in the file of warp marker `marker` (its place in the map, the first being 0) of each of the warped audio clips `clips`, which must hold files of the same length, by `by` seconds (negative moves it earlier), keeping its beat: the waveform moves under the marker. Refused, changing nothing, if the marker would pass a neighbour or leave the file.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped audio clips: their files must be as long as each other's. |
| `marker` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The marker, by its place in the map, the first being 0. |
| `by` | number | yes | How far to move its time in the file, in seconds: negative moves it earlier. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.slice_to_midi_track`

**Slice to New MIDI Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`, `session`, `clip-view`.

Cuts an audio clip into slices on a new MIDI track. The clip is sliced over its region: from its Start marker to its End marker, or, with the loop on, from the earlier of its Start marker and its loop's start to the loop's end. `by` is a beat division (`eight_bars`, `four_bars`, `two_bars`, `one_bar`, `half`, `quarter`, `eighth`, `sixteenth` — the default — or `thirty_second`), `transients` (one slice at each of the clip's transients in the region), or `warp_markers` (one at each of its warp markers; refused for an unwarped clip). With `preserve_warped_timing` on (the default) the slices are cut from the clip's warped audio, so each sounds as it did and its note falls where it played; off, they are cut from the clip's own file, unwarped. `preset` names a slicing preset: Beatlayer's factory presets (the default makes a Drum Rack of one sampler per slice, each chain receiving a note from C1 up and playing C3; `One Sampler` makes one sampler in Slice mode) or a user preset in the User Library's Defaults/Slicing folder. The new MIDI track goes directly after the clip's track, takes the clip's name, and holds a MIDI clip with one note per slice, rising chromatically, each lasting to the next, at velocity 127. More than 128 slices are refused (64 for `One Sampler`). Slicing leaves the audio clip as it was and is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `by` | [`SliceBy`](#sliceby) or null | no | How to cut it: a beat division, `transients`, or `warp_markers`. Left out, `sixteenth` (R2). |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The audio clip to slice. Left out, the one audio clip selected in either view. |
| `preserve_warped_timing` | boolean or null | no | Whether the slices are cut from the clip's warped audio, keeping the timing warping gave them. Left out, `true` (R2, R6). |
| `preset` | string or null | no | The slicing preset's name: one of Beatlayer's factory presets or a user preset in the User Library's `Defaults/Slicing/` folder (R11). Left out, the default preset. |

Result: [`SliceResult`](#sliceresult).

#### `clip.slide_contents`

**Slide Clip Contents**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Slides a warped audio clip's contents inside the clip, which stays where it is and keeps its length: `by` is how far the contents move in ticks, positive later. Its Start marker, its End marker and its loop brace move the other way through its contents by that much, so the same audio - its warp markers included - plays `by` ticks later (or earlier). Shift+Option-dragging a clip's contents in the Arrangement runs it, snapping to the grid unless Cmd is held as well. Refused for a clip that isn't warped, and for a slide that would take a marker out of the file. One undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-005 | `Shift+Option+drag` | `Shift+Alt+drag` | `arrangement` | Slide a clip's contents inside the clip | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio or MIDI clip. |
| `by` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How far the contents move, in ticks: negative moves them earlier. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.stretch`

**Stretch Clip**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Stretches a warped audio clip so its dragged `edge` (left or right) lands on the tick `at`, the other edge staying put. Its length becomes the dragged one and every beat in its contents - its warp markers, its Start and End markers and its loop brace - scales by the new length over the old about the beat at the fixed edge, so the same audio fills the new length and its tempo changes with it. Shift-dragging a warped clip's title-bar edge in the Arrangement runs it; Shift-dragging an unwarped clip's edge resizes it as a plain drag does. One undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-006 | `Shift+drag the clip title bar` | `Shift+drag the clip title bar` | `arrangement` | Stretch a warped clip | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped audio clip. |
| `edge` | [`ClipEdge`](#clipedge) | yes | The edge being dragged. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where that edge goes, in ticks: 0 (1.1.1) or later, and past the other edge. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.transients`

**Clip Transients**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Lists an audio clip's transients: where its file starts notes and hits, found once in the background and kept by the file's content hash, with the clip's own edits applied (`clip.insert_transient`, `clip.delete_transients`, `clip.move_transient`, `clip.reset_transients`). Each has its `time` in the file in seconds, its `beat` in ticks from the clip's 1.1.1 when the clip is warped, and whether it was put in `by_hand`. `analysis_ready` says whether the file's analysis is done; until it is, only the transients put in by hand are listed, and asking starts the analysis. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip. |

Result: [`ClipTransients`](#cliptransients).

#### `clip.trim_start`

**Trim Clip Start**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves a clip's left edge to `start`, keeping its end and keeping its contents where they play, as dragging the clip's left edge does: a later `start` hides the beginning of the clip, an earlier one shows more of it. An audio clip's Start marker moves by the time the edge moved (seconds under the tempo map), as Live's does, so it can't go before the start of the file; a MIDI clip's offset moves by as many ticks and stays at 0 or more. The clip can't start before 0, or at or after its end. To move a clip with its contents, use `clip.move`; to change where it ends, use `clip.set_length`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where its left edge goes, before its end. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.warp_as_loop`

**Warp as Loop**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Warps a warped audio clip's whole file as a loop of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32 bars of 4/4, the number whose tempo is nearest the set's tempo at the clip's start: a warp marker at the start of the file on 1.1.1 and one at its end on the last bar's end, the Start and End markers and the loop brace on the whole file, the loop on, and that tempo as the clip's. The clip keeps its place and length in the arrangement. Refused for a clip that isn't warped, or while the file's analysis is not ready. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped audio clip. |
| `analysis` | [`FileBeats`](#filebeats) or null | no | The file's length. Left out, the app reads it from the file, and refuses while the file's analysis is not ready. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.warp_from_here`

**Warp From Here**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Warps a warped audio clip from a point on: at the selected warp marker (`marker`) or at a new one at the insert marker (`beat` or `time`, as for `clip.set_1_1_1_here`). The markers before it stay and those after it are replaced. `method` is `auto`, a marker on the first beat of every bar after the point from the tempo found there; `start_at`, the same starting from the tempo `bpm`, the set's tempo at the point unless given, which settles whether a beat is counted at double or half the speed; `straight`, which deletes the markers after the point and sets the clip's tempo to the tempo found after it; or `bpm`, which deletes them and sets the clip's tempo to `bpm`, the set's tempo at the point unless given. The file's tempo and beats come from its analysis (`analysis` gives them), so every method but `bpm` is refused while it is not ready. Refused for a clip that isn't warped. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped audio clip. |
| `method` | [`WarpFrom`](#warpfrom) | yes | How the audio after the point is warped. |
| `analysis` | [`FileBeats`](#filebeats) or null | no | The file's tempo and beats. Left out, the app uses the file's analysis, and refuses while it is not ready. |
| `beat` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The Sample Editor's insert marker as a beat, in ticks from the clip's 1.1.1: a warp marker is made there, at the time the map already places it. |
| `bpm` | number or null | no | The tempo for `start_at` and `bpm`: the set's tempo at the point unless given. |
| `marker` | integer or null | no | The selected warp marker, by its place in the map, the first being 0. |
| `time` | number or null | no | The insert marker as a time in the file, in seconds: a warp marker is made there, on the beat the map already places it. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `clip.warp_selection_as_loop`

**Warp Selection as Loop**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Warps the part of a warped audio clip's file from `from` to `to` (seconds in the file) as a loop of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32 bars of 4/4, the number whose tempo is nearest the set's tempo at the clip's start: a warp marker at each end of the part, the Start and End markers and the loop brace on it, the loop on. The clip keeps its place and length in the arrangement. Refused for a clip that isn't warped. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The warped audio clip. |
| `from` | number, at least 0 | yes | The start of the part, in seconds in the file. |
| `to` | number, at least 0 | yes | The end of the part, in seconds, after `from`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `clip_view`

#### `clip_view.focus_mode`
