**Focus Mode**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Switches Focus Mode (N, or the Focus button): a tap switches it, and holding N switches it while it's held. It acts while the note editor shows several clips: with it on, edits, drawing and the filters reach the foreground clip alone, and the others show grey. It is off when the app starts and isn't saved or an undo step. `on` says which way; left out, it switches. The result is the Clip View's state.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-040 | `N` | `N` | `note-editor` | Toggle Focus Mode for multi-clip editing (momentary while held) | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Whether Focus Mode ends up on; left out, it switches. |

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `clip_view.foreground`

**Foreground Clip**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Makes one of the clips the note editor shows the foreground clip, as clicking its note or its loop bar does: the expression lanes and the footer edit its notes alone, and with Focus Mode on it is the active clip. Changes only the view: it isn't saved with the set and isn't an undo step. The result is the Clip View's state.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The shown clip to make the foreground clip. |

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `clip_view.invert_selection`

**Invert Selection**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Selects every note in the clip's span that was not selected and deselects those that were, as Edit ▸ Invert Selection does (Cmd-Shift-A, Ctrl-Shift-A on Windows). The time selection follows the new selection. It needs a clip that holds notes, is never an undo step, and changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-034 | `Cmd+Shift+A` | `Ctrl+Shift+A` | `note-editor` | Invert the note selection | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `clip_view.note_filters`

**Note Filters**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Find and Select Notes. Shows or hides the filter bar (`visible`, or `toggle`, as Cmd-Shift-F does), chooses the filter whose controls it shows (`shown`), and sets the controls and Invert of any filter (`pitch`, `time`, `chance`, `condition`, `count`, `duration`, `scale`, `velocity`). Setting a control, or Invert, switches that filter on, and while any filter is on the selection is the notes in the clip's span that every filter that is on lets through, worked out again each time, with the time selection following it. `select` presses the Select button of each filter it lists: it is switched on and the notes are selected again. `off` switches filters off, keeping their settings; a click in the note area switches all eight off. Time's Start, Length and Repeat are in beats of the clip's time signature, to a hundredth, Start from 1; a Repeat of `null` is one bar. Duration's Min and Max are in beats too, a Max of `null` being the clip's span. Chance is in percent. Moving Min past Max takes Max with it, and the other way round. The settings belong to the editor: they are kept while the app runs, every filter is switched off when the editor shows another clip, and none of it is saved with the set or is an undo step. The result is every filter's settings and the selected notes.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-037 | `Cmd+Shift+F` | `Ctrl+Shift+F` | `note-editor` | Show or hide the note filters | fixes `toggle` = `true` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chance` | [`ChanceArgs`](#chanceargs) or null | no | Chance controls. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |
| `condition` | [`ConditionArgs`](#conditionargs) or null | no | Condition controls. |
| `count` | [`CountArgs`](#countargs) or null | no | Count controls. |
| `duration` | [`DurationArgs`](#durationargs) or null | no | Duration controls. |
| `off` | array of [`NoteFilter`](#notefilter) | no | Filters to switch off, keeping their settings. |
| `pitch` | [`PitchArgs`](#pitchargs) or null | no | Pitch controls. |
| `scale` | [`ScaleArgs`](#scaleargs) or null | no | Scale controls. |
| `select` | array of [`NoteFilter`](#notefilter) | no | Filters whose Select button is pressed: each is switched on, and the notes are selected again. |
| `shown` | [`NoteFilter`](#notefilter) or null | no | Chooses the filter whose controls the bar shows. |
| `time` | [`TimeArgs`](#timeargs) or null | no | Time controls. |
| `toggle` | boolean | no | Switches the bar, as Cmd-Shift-F does; `visible` wins if both are given. |
| `velocity` | [`VelocityArgs`](#velocityargs) or null | no | Velocity controls. |
| `visible` | boolean or null | no | Shows or hides the filter bar. |

Result: [`NoteFiltersResult`](#notefiltersresult).

#### `clip_view.quantize_settings`

**Quantize Settings**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`, `sample-editor`.

Reads or changes the Clip View's Quantize settings, the values `note.quantize`, `clip.quantize_audio` and Cmd-U use when their arguments leave them out: `grid`, the spacing between the quantise grid's lines in ticks (positive; left unset, it follows the note or sample editor's editing grid), `target`, whether quantise moves note starts or note ends, and `amount`, how far each note moves toward its grid line as a percentage from 0 to 100. Fields left out keep their values, and the result reports all of them. The settings belong to the view, like Draw Mode: changing them changes nothing in the set and is no undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SAMPLE-002 | `Cmd+Shift+U` | `Ctrl+Shift+U` | `sample-editor` | Open the quantise settings | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | integer or null | no | How far each note moves toward its grid line, from 0 to 100 percent. |
| `grid` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The quantise grid's line spacing in ticks; must be positive. A new view follows the Clip View's editing grid until one is set. |
| `target` | [`QuantizeTarget`](#quantizetarget) or null | no | What quantise moves toward the grid. |

Result: [`QuantizeSettings`](#quantizesettings).

**Sample Editor State**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Reports what the Clip View's Sample Editor shows for the audio clip it shows: whether the clip is warped, the selected warp markers (by their place in the clip's warp map), whether the Start marker is selected, the selected transients (by their times in the file), the insert marker, the time selection, and the span shown. Changes nothing.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

#### `clip_view.sample_view`

**Zoom Sample Editor**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`.

Changes the part of the file the Sample Editor shows: `selection` zooms to the time selection (Z, remembering the view before), `back` goes back to the view before the last zoom (X, a step at a time), `whole` fits the whole file across the editor (W), `height` switches fitting the waveform to the editor's height (H), and `span` shows `start` to `end`, in seconds in the file or, with `ticks`, in ticks of a warped clip's contents, and `scroll` does the same without remembering the view before, as dragging the ruler or the wheel does (scrolling pauses Follow until playback starts or stops); `page` is Follow turning the page, which doesn't pause it. Changes only the view.

| S-SAMPLE-013 | `W` | `W` | `sample-editor` | Fit the content to the editor's width | fixes `show` = `"whole"` |
| S-SAMPLE-014 | `H` | `H` | `sample-editor` | Fit the content to the editor's height | fixes `show` = `"height"` |

| `start` | number or null | no | With `span`, where the view starts: seconds in the file, or ticks of a warped clip's contents with `ticks`. |
| `ticks` | boolean | no | Whether `start` and `end` are ticks of a warped clip's contents instead of seconds in the file. |

Result: [`SampleEditorState`](#sampleeditorstate).

#### `clip_view.select_loop_bars`

**Select Loop Bars**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Selects the loop bars above the note editor of the given clips, in place of the selected ones, or with `toggle` adds each to the selection or takes it out, as Cmd-click does (Ctrl-click on Windows). The last clip given becomes the foreground clip. With Focus Mode on only one bar can be selected. Changes only the view: it isn't an undo step. The result is the Clip View's state.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | no | The clips whose loop bars to select; empty selects none. |

#### `clip_view.select_notes`

**Select Notes**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Selects notes in the Clip View's MIDI Note Editor, as clicking a note or dragging a marquee over them does: `replace` selects only these, `toggle` adds or removes each (Cmd-click, Ctrl-click on Windows). Notes are named by their place in the clip's notes in order, by start and then pitch, so place 0 has the earliest start, and of notes that start together the lowest pitch. With no notes named, `select` chooses them instead: `nearest` (the note whose start is nearest the insert marker), `previous` and `next` (the previous or next note in the clip's order), `same_pitch_previous` and `same_pitch_next` (the previous or next note at the selected note's pitch), `all` (every note in the clip's span, as Cmd-A does), or `key` (every note at a pitch, as clicking a key in the piano ruler does). `add` adds to the selection instead of replacing it, as Shift with the note-jump keys does. Selecting is never an undo step and changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-001 | `Cmd+A` | `Ctrl+A` | `note-editor` | Select all notes | fixes `select` = `"all"` |
| S-EDIT-009 | `Cmd+A` | `Ctrl+A` | `global` | Select everything in the focused view | fixes `select` = `"all"` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `add` | boolean | no | Add to the selection instead of replacing it, as Shift with the note-jump keys does. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips, each with its notes, in place of `clip` and `notes` (Spec: multi-clip-editing R18). Left out with `clip` and `notes`, the selected notes of every clip shown, or of the active clip alone in Focus Mode. |
| `mode` | [`NoteSelectMode`](#noteselectmode) | no | How to change the selection; `replace` if left out. |
| `notes` | array of integer, at least 0 | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Empty with `replace` clears the selection, and empty with `select` chooses the notes `select` names. |
| `select` | [`NoteSelection`](#noteselection) or null | no | What to select when `notes` is empty: the notes the keyboard reaches (Option with the arrows), every note in the clip's span (Cmd-A), or the notes at a pitch (a key in the piano ruler). |

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

Makes a time selection in the editor from `start` to `end`, in seconds in the file or, with `ticks`, in ticks of a warped clip's contents; with neither the selection is cleared. Dragging across the waveform runs this. In the MIDI Note Editor `start` and `end` are ticks of the clip's contents, and the selection is drawn across the note area and the lanes. A marker is named by its place in the clip's warp map (`data.audio.warp_markers`), the first being 0. With `start_marker` the clip's Start marker is selected too. #### `clip_view.set_insert_marker`

**Set Insert Marker**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `sample-editor`, `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Puts the editor's insert marker, the point the editor's commands act at, at a `time` in the file in seconds or at a `beat` of a warped clip's contents in ticks from its 1.1.1; with neither it is taken away. Clicking the waveform runs this, on the nearest grid line while snapping is on. In the MIDI Note Editor the marker is a `beat` of the clip's contents in ticks from their beginning, and it stays inside the clip's span. Never an undo step, and changes nothing in the set.

| `time` | number or null | no | Where to put the marker, as a time in the file in seconds. Give this or `beat`; give neither to take the marker away. |

**MIDI Note Editor Preview**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `clip-view`, `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Sets the MIDI Note Editor's Preview switch (`on`), the one above the piano ruler and Options ▸ MIDI Note Editor Preview: with it on, clicking a key, drawing, clicking and keyboard-selecting a note, and dragging notes to a new pitch play into the clip's track, and an armed track can be step-recorded. ### Area `device`

#### `device.add`

**Add Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`, `browser`.

Adds a device as a person does from the browser: to the selected track (or `track`), after the selected device or at the end of its role's place in the chain (or at `index`), switched on, with its type's default preset if one was saved, and selects it. The chain keeps Live's order: MIDI effects, the instrument, then audio effects. An instrument or MIDI effect added while an audio, group, or return track is selected goes on a new MIDI track at the end of the track list, which becomes the selected track, as one undo step (Insert Device and Track). With `chain` it goes into that rack chain instead. A chain holds one instrument; a rack holds more.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`NewDevice`](#newdevice) | yes | The device to add. |
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) or null | no | A rack's chain to add it to, at any depth, in place of the track's own chain (WP-5.1). |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where it goes in the chain; after the selected device, or at the end of its role's place in the chain, if left out. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track; the selected track if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceAdded`](#deviceadded).

#### `device.add_layers`

**Add Samples**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Adds audio files to a multisampler as layers, as dropping them on the zone editor's layer list does: each file is imported into the set's media, and gets one layer after the selected layers (or at the end), or at `index`, or straight after the layer `after`, with every zone whole and unfaded (or copied from the layer `like`, so the new layers sound together with it), its Root Key from the file's sampler metadata (C3 where it has none), Sample Start and End at the file's ends, and its loop points from the file's first loop with Sustain Mode left off. The new layers become the selected ones. A file that isn't audio is skipped and named in `skipped`. One undo step. It reads files outside the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paths` | array of string | yes | The audio files, one layer each. |
| `after` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | Puts the first straight after this layer, instead of at `index` or after the selected ones (R61). |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where in the layer list the first goes; after the selected layers (or at the end with none selected) if left out. |
| `like` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | Gives each new layer this layer's key, velocity and sample select zones with their fades, so the two sound together (R61). |

Result: [`LayersAdded`](#layersadded).

#### `device.add_preset`

**Add Preset**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Adds the device or rack a preset file (.blpreset) holds, as choosing it in the browser (Enter, a double-click or a drag) does: where `device.add` puts a device of its role, on `track` (the shown track if left out) or in the rack chain `chain`, after the selected device if that keeps the chain's order. A device takes the preset's values and name; a rack comes whole, with new IDs for its chains and devices. One undo step, named Insert Device (Insert Device and Track when it goes on a new MIDI track). The new device is selected. A chain preset is refused: `chain.load_preset` loads it. Reads a file outside the project; the samples a rack preset carries are written to the User Library's Samples/Preset Samples folder if the set's media store lacks them.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The preset file: a device's or a rack's. |
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) or null | no | The rack chain that takes it, instead of a track's own chain. |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where it goes in the chain; after the selected device, or at the end of its role's place, if left out. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track, as `device.add` takes it; the shown track if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceAdded`](#deviceadded).

#### `device.add_sample_edit`

**Edit Sample**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Adds one edit to the end of a sample's edit list without looking at the audio: `edit.kind` is `trim`, `cut`, `reverse`, `fade_in`, `fade_out` or `normalize`, and `edit.range` (`from` to `to`, in frames of the sample as the earlier edits left it) is its selection, left out for the whole sample (Trim and Cut need one). With a `layer` the edit joins that layer's list and its length and markers follow the audio; with none it joins the sample of the device itself, which this command doesn't check against the sample's length. The source file is never written. One undo step named for the edit. `device.edit_sample` checks the selection against the sample.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `edit` | [`SampleEdit`](#sampleedit) | yes | The edit. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | The layer, or `null` for the device's own sample. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.add_slice`

**Add Slice**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Adds a manual slice at a frame into the sample (WP-5.15b). In Slice mode, slices play chromatically from C3.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `frame` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Frame into the sample. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.audition_sample`

**Audition Sample**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Plays a sampler's sample from a point through the device, as a click in its display does: `from` is the start as a share of the sample from 0 to 1, `layer` a multisampler's layer (its first selected layer if left out). The voice plays at the sample's root pitch (C3 for Simpler, the layer's root key for the multisampler) through the device's settings, and goes on until the same command comes with `down: false`, as the button's release. It needs the audio engine on; `sent` says whether it was. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The sampler device; the selected device if left out. |
| `down` | boolean | no | Whether the button goes down (`true`, the default) or comes up. |
| `from` | number | no | Where in the sample to start, as a share of its length from 0 to 1. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | A multisampler's layer; its first selected layer if left out. |

Result: [`Auditioned`](#auditioned).

#### `device.autosample`

**Autosample**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Samples an instrument across a range of notes and velocities into a new multisampler on a new MIDI track: the native instrument, the plug-in instrument, or the external instrument, rendered alone with its current settings. The notes are the lowest one and every `step` above it up to the highest, which is always sampled; each is played at `velocity_layers` velocities, held for `note_length` seconds and followed by `release_tail` seconds of render, and sampled `round_robins` times for the round robins. The samples are 32-bit floating-point WAVs in the project's `Samples/Processed/Autosample` folder, named for the instrument, the note and the velocity, and they join the set's media. With `detect_loops` on, each sample gets a sustain loop so a sustained sound holds past the note. The result is a new MIDI track straight after the source's, holding a multisampler with one layer per sample, its zones spread between the sampled notes, Round Robin on in Forward mode where there are round robins, and the volume envelope's release as long as the release tail. One undo step; undoing it leaves the files on disk. It writes files, and plays hardware for the external instrument.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `detect_loops` | boolean or null | no | Whether a loop is found in each sample. Off by default. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The instrument to sample: a native instrument, a plug-in instrument, or the external instrument. The one selected in the Device View when it is left out. |
| `highest` | integer or null | no | The highest note sampled, from 0 to 127 (C-2 to G8). C6 by default. |
| `lowest` | integer or null | no | The lowest note sampled, from 0 to 127 (C-2 to G8). C1 by default. |
| `name` | string or null | no | The name of the instrument the samples are named for, and of the new track. The instrument's own name by default. |
| `note_length` | number or null | no | How long each note is held, in seconds, from 0.1 to 30. 2 by default. |
| `release_tail` | number or null | no | How long the render goes on after the note is released, in seconds, from 0 to 30. 1 by default. |
| `round_robins` | integer or null | no | How many times each note is sampled, from 1 to 8, for the round robins. 1 by default. |
| `step` | integer or null | no | How many semitones between the sampled notes, from 1 to 12. 3 by default. |
| `velocity_layers` | integer or null | no | How many velocity layers each note is sampled at, from 1 to 16. 1 by default. |
| `wait` | boolean or null | no | Whether to wait for the samples to be made before returning. True by default; with it off the command starts the samples and returns at once, and the progress is read from the dialog. |

Result: [`Autosampled`](#autosampled).

#### `device.autosample_cancel`

**Stop Autosampling**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Stops a running autosample: the files it wrote are deleted and the set is left as it was. It does nothing when no autosample is running.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`AutosampleCancelled`](#autosamplecancelled).

#### `device.autosample_open`

**Autosample…**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Opens the autosampler's dialog for an instrument: the notes and velocities to sample, the note length and release tail, the round robins, whether a loop is found in each sample, and the name the samples are given. It changes nothing in the set; the dialog's Autosample button runs `device.autosample`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The instrument to sample. The one selected in the Device View when it is left out. |

Result: [`AutosamplerOpened`](#autosampleropened).

#### `device.clear_sample_edits`

**Revert Edits**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Empties a sample's edit list, a layer's (`layer`) or the device's own (none given). A layer's sample is `length` frames long again, the unedited sample's length at its own rate, and its markers keep their share of it. One undo step. `device.edit_sample` with `revert` reads the length itself.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `length` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The unedited sample's length in frames at its own rate. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | The layer, or `null` for the device's own sample. |

#### `device.compare_copy`

**Compare: Copy**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Copies every value of a native device's active state, A or B, over the other, as the Edit menu's and the device menu's Compare: Copy A to B (Copy B to A while B is active) do. What the device plays doesn't change, and no envelope is overridden. One undo step, named as the item that ran it. Racks and plug-ins have no states, so a command for one is refused. From the menus it copies the selected device's state.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.compare_switch`

**Compare: Switch**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Makes the other of a native device's two states, A and B, the active one, as the Edit menu's and the device menu's Compare: Switch to B/A and the P key do. Every parameter whose value differs between the states moves to the newly active state's value, a continuous one gliding as any change does, and every parameter of the device that has an envelope is overridden until Re-Enable Automation. One undo step, named as the item that ran it. A change to a parameter goes to the active state only. Racks and plug-ins have no states, so a command for one is refused. `device.parameters` says which state is active and each parameter's value in the other; the query tool's `device` has both in `compare`. From the keyboard and the menus it switches the selected device.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-011 | `P` | `P` | `device-view` | Switch the device between its A and B states | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.convert`

**Convert Sampler**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Converts Simpler to a multisampler (`to: multisampler`) or a multisampler to Simpler (`to: snapshot`), keeping the device's place in its chain, its name, its on or off state and its sample, as one undo step. Simpler becomes one layer with every zone whole, its region as Sample Start and Sample End, its loop as a sustain loop and its edits, with its envelope, volume and pan as the multisampler's; a multisampler becomes Simpler in Classic mode playing its first layer. Slicing and One-Shot, and layers past the first, don't carry over, and the result's `dropped` names what didn't. The new device has a new ID, which the result gives.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | [`ConvertTo`](#convertto) | yes | What to convert it to. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The sampler device; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`Converted`](#converted).

#### `device.copy`

**Copy Device**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Copies a device to the clipboard, with its settings, for `device.paste`. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-002 | `Cmd+C` | `Ctrl+C` | `global` | Copy | runs it |

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

#### `device.crop_sample`

**Crop Sample**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Removes the sample outside Simpler's region, or outside a multisampler layer's Sample Start and Sample End, by writing a processed copy: a WAV with the sample's edits applied, at its rate and channels, in the project's `Samples/Processed/Crop/` folder. The device or layer then plays the copy, with its edit list empty and the region the whole of it, as one undo step; the original file stays as it was. A set that has never been saved has no project folder, and the command is refused with a message in the Status Bar. The copy is the sample's new media, which reads back in the device's `media` or the layer's `media`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The sampler device; the selected device if left out. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | A multisampler's layer; its first selected layer if left out. |

Result: [`SampleProcessed`](#sampleprocessed).

**Cut Device**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `device-view`.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Delete Samples**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |

**Delete Slice**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

#### `device.display`

**Device Display**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Reports what a device's display shows now, read from the display data its node publishes after each block and from its parameters: curves and spectra (an EQ's spectrum, its bands' responses and their sum per curve; a compressor's transfer curve), the markers on them (an EQ's band dots, a compressor's threshold and level), and single readings (a compressor's gain reduction and levels), each with its unit and how it reads; the view the display shows, if it has views; and whether an engine is publishing (`live`). Empty for a device whose type draws no display. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

**Distribute Ranges**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Spreads the listed layers' ranges, in list order and without fades: `equally` gives each an equal share of the range of the zone named by `kind` (keys from 0 to 127, velocities 1 to 127, select 0 to 127), and `around_root_key` splits the keyboard between the layers' root keys, layers that share a root dividing its zone. With one layer or none listed, every layer. One undo step.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |

| `how` | [`Distribution`](#distribution) | yes | How to spread them. |
| `kind` | [`ZoneKind`](#zonekind) | yes | The zone editor in view: which zone `equally` spreads. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

**Duplicate Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Puts a copy of a device, with its settings, straight after it, and selects the copy: one undo step, named Duplicate Device. A chain holds one instrument, so an instrument can't be duplicated; a rack is copied whole, with new IDs for its chains and devices.

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |

| S-EDIT-004 | `Cmd+D` | `Ctrl+D` | `global` | Duplicate | runs it |

**Duplicate Samples**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Copies the listed layers, each copy straight after its original with the next layer ID, as the layer list's Duplicate does. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |

#### `device.edit_sample`

**Edit Sample**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Edits a sampler's sample without writing a file, as the sample display's context menu does: `kind` is `trim` (keep the selection), `cut` (remove it and close the gap), `reverse`, `fade_in`, `fade_out` (a straight line in gain over the selection) or `normalize` (scale the selection so its largest magnitude reaches 0 dBFS). `range` is the selection, `from` to `to` in frames of the sample as the earlier edits left it, at its own rate; left out it is the whole sample, except for trim and cut, which need one. The edit joins the sample's list, kept with the set and applied to the file's audio in order; the file is never written. A multisampler's `layer` (its first selected layer if left out) keeps its markers on the audio they marked: those after a cut move earlier by its length, those inside it to its start, and those outside a trim to its nearer end; Simpler's Start, Length and Loop are shares of the sample and stay. `revert: true` clears the list instead. One undo step named for the edit. The list reads back as `sample_edits` in the query tool's `device` result for Simpler and as `edits` in each layer of `layers` for the multisampler.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The sampler device; the selected device if left out. |
| `kind` | [`SampleEditKind`](#sampleeditkind) or null | no | What the edit does. Leave it out with `revert`. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | A multisampler's layer; its first selected layer if left out. Simpler has one sample and no layers. |
| `range` | [`SampleRange`](#samplerange) or null | no | The selection it acts on, in frames of the sample as the earlier edits left it, at its own rate. Left out it acts on the whole sample; Trim and Cut need one. |
| `revert` | boolean | no | Clears the sample's edit list instead of adding to it. |

Result: [`SampleEdited`](#sampleedited).

**Expand Device**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Only devices with an expanded part (`expandable` in `device_view.state`) have one. Like folding, it changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and isn't saved with the set. The device's width in the chain follows it.

Folds a device to a narrow strip showing only its title bar on its side, or unfolds it, as double-clicking its title bar or the context menu's Fold does; switches unless `folded` says which. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and isn't saved with the set.

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |

#### `device.group`

**Group**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`, `rack-chains`.

Wraps the selected devices (or `devices`, all in one chain) in a new rack, as Group does: the rack takes the first device's place and holds one chain, named after the first device, that holds the devices in their order, each keeping its settings and running state; the rack is selected. The rack is the kind that can hold them: an audio effect rack for audio effects alone, a MIDI effect rack for MIDI effects alone, and an instrument rack for any other mix. A selection that grouping would put out of the chain's order is refused. With `chains` (several chains of one rack) they become the chains of a new rack of the same kind, inside a new chain in the first one's place. One undo step (Group).

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-001 | `Cmd+G` | `Ctrl+G` | `device-view` | Group the selected devices into a rack | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chains` | array or null | no | Several chains of one rack to group instead: they become the chains of a new rack of the same kind, in a new chain in the first one's place. |
| `devices` | array or null | no | The devices to wrap in a new rack, all in one chain; the selected device if both lists are left out. |

Result: [`Grouped`](#grouped).

#### `device.group_to_drum_rack`

**Group to Drum Rack**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Wraps the selected devices (or `devices`, all in one chain of a MIDI track) in a new drum rack, which takes the first device's place: the rack holds one chain, named after the first device, that receives note 36 (C1, the first pad a new drum rack shows) and plays C3, and holds the devices in their order, each keeping its settings and running state. They must fit one chain of an instrument rack: MIDI effects, then at most one instrument, then audio effects. One undo step (Group).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `devices` | array or null | no | The devices, all in one chain of a track; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`Grouped`](#grouped).

**Hot-Swap Presets**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`, `browser`.

Starts or ends hot-swapping a device's presets, as the title bar's Hot-Swap Presets button does; switches unless `on` says which. While it lasts, the browser shows a bar (Swapping Audio Effect) and opens the User Library's folder of the device's presets, and loading a preset from the browser (Enter or a double-click) loads it into the device. Any device, preset or rack preset of the same role replaces it (`device.replace`), and hot-swap stays on after each load. With no `device` and none selected, it arms the first audio effect of the shown track, or its instrument on a MIDI track. Changes only the view.

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |

| S-DEV-008 | `Q` | `Q` | `device-view` | Hot-swap the selected device | runs it |
| S-VIEW-006 | `Q` | `Q` | `global` | Toggle hot-swap mode for the selected device or item | runs it |

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Start (true) or end (false) hot-swapping; switches if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `device.hot_swap_layer`

**Hot-Swap Sample**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Starts hot-swapping a layer's sample (`layer`, or the first selected layer), as the zone editor's Hot-Swap Sample button does: the sample the browser then loads (Enter or a double-click on a file) replaces the layer's, keeping its zones and settings, as one undo step. `on: false` ends it. It changes nothing in the set by itself.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | The layer; the first selected layer if left out. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Start (true) or end (false) hot-swapping; starts if left out. |

Result: [`MultisamplerState`](#multisamplerstate).

#### `device.import_sfz`

**Import SFZ**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Imports an SFZ multisample instrument, the open text format, as a multisampler: each region becomes a layer (its sample, key and velocity zones with their crossfades as fades, Root Key, tuning, Volume, Pan, start and end points, loop and loop mode), and the device-wide settings most regions agree on (the volume, filter, filter and pitch envelopes, Vel > Vol, Pitch Bend Range, reverse, the fade law) set the new device's controls. Sequences (`seq_length`) turn Round Robin on in Forward mode, random windows (`lorand`) in Random mode. With `device`, a multisampler, only the layers are added, at the end of its list; otherwise a multisampler is made on `track`, or on a new MIDI track below the last. The samples join the set's media where they lie. Regions whose sample is missing or isn't audio, or whose `trigger` isn't `attack`, are left out and named in `left_out`; opcodes the import doesn't read are listed in `unread`. A file with no region left changes nothing. One undo step. It reads files outside the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The `.sfz` file. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | A multisampler to add the regions to as layers, at the end of its list. Left out, the import makes a multisampler: on `track`, or on a new MIDI track below the last track. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The MIDI track to put a new multisampler on, after its other devices. Ignored with `device`. |

Result: [`SfzImported`](#sfzimported).

#### `device.insert`

**Insert Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`, `browser`.

Inserts a device into a track's device chain at `index`, where 0 is first in the signal flow. The device is a native Beatlayer device named by its type ID, or a plug-in named by its format and plug-in ID, with its `name` (the device's own, such as the title bar shows), its `role` (`midi_effect`, `instrument`, or `audio_effect`, the default), and any parameter values to set. A chain keeps Live's order: MIDI effects first, then at most one instrument, then audio effects, and only MIDI tracks hold MIDI effects and instruments; an index that breaks the order is refused. `device.id` must be a new ID the project has issued for it. To add a device as a person does, after the selected device and with its default preset, use `device.add`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in the chain, from 0 to the chain's length. |
| `device` | [`Device`](#device) | yes | The device, with a new ID. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.insert_in_chain`

**Insert Device in Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Inserts a device into a rack's chain at `index`, where 0 is first in the chain's signal flow, as `device.insert` does for a track's chain. The chain may belong to a rack at any depth. The device is described as for `device.insert`, with a new ID. A chain keeps the order for its kind of rack: an audio effect rack's chains hold only audio effects, a MIDI effect rack's only MIDI effects, and an instrument or drum rack's chains hold MIDI effects, then at most one instrument, then audio effects; an index or device that breaks it is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in the chain, from 0 to the chain's length. |
| `device` | [`Device`](#device) | yes | The device, with a new ID. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.insert_layers`

**Add Samples**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Adds layers to a multisampler at `index` (`null` for the end), each a sample named by content hash with its zones (every zone whole and unfaded in a new layer), Root Key, loop points and levels. The multisampler gives each layer the next of its own layer IDs, in order, ignoring the `id` you send; read them back from the device's `layers` in the query tool's `device` result. A sample must be in the media store to play; to add files from disk as a person does, use `device.add_layers`. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `layers` | array of [`Layer`](#layer) | yes | The layers. |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where in the layer list the first goes, or `null` for the end. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.load_preset`

**Load Preset**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Loads a Beatlayer preset file (.blpreset) into a device of the kind it was saved from, as choosing it while hot-swapping does: every parameter takes the preset's value (or its default, if the preset doesn't set it), and the device's title shows the preset's name. One undo step. A preset for another kind of device is refused. A rack preset loads into a rack of the kind it was saved from and replaces the rack with the preset's, as one undo step (the rack's ID changes; `device.replace` loads a preset into a device of another kind). A chain preset loads with `chain.load_preset`. Reads a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The preset file. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`PresetResult`](#presetresult).

#### `device.load_sample`

**Load Sample**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Loads an audio file into a device that plays samples (the sampler, or the eight-slot drum sampler), as dropping the file on the device does: the file goes into the set's media store, named by its content hash, and the device keeps that reference, so the set reopens playing it. `slot` says which of a device's sample slots takes it (counted from 0); left out, it is the slot selected in the panel, or the only one. One undo step, named Load Sample. Reads a file outside the project. A device whose type doesn't play a sample, or a slot it doesn't have, is refused. `device.set_sample` with a null `media` clears a slot.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The audio file to load into the device. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `slot` | integer or null | no | The sample slot to load it into, counted from 0; the slot the panel has selected for a device with several, and 0 for one with one. |

Result: [`LoadSampleResult`](#loadsampleresult).

#### `device.move`

**Move Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Moves a device to `index` in a track's chain, on the same track or another, with its settings. The index counts positions after the device is taken out of its current place. The chain must stay in Live's order (MIDI effects, the instrument, then audio effects), so an audio effect can't go before an instrument, and MIDI effects and instruments only go on MIDI tracks.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track it moves to. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in that chain. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.move_layers`

**Move Samples**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Moves the listed layers, keeping their order, so the first sits at `index` among the layers that stay; the list's order decides Round Robin's turns and which layer a sort leaves first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `layers` | array of [`LayerId`](#layerid) | yes | The layers to move. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where the first goes among the layers left. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.move_slice`

**Move Slice**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Moves a manual slice from `from` frame to `to` frame into the sample (WP-5.15b).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `from` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The existing slice's frame. |
| `to` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The new frame. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.move_to_chain`

**Move Device to Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Moves a device to `index` in a rack's chain, from a track's chain or another chain, on the same track or another, keeping its settings and running state. The index counts positions after the device is taken out of its current place. The chain must stay in order for its kind of rack. A rack can't be moved into one of its own chains. To move a device out of a rack, use `device.move`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The chain it moves to. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in that chain. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.normalize_layers`

**Normalize**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Normalize Volume sets each layer's Volume (`layers`, or the selected ones) so its sample's largest magnitude between Sample Start and Sample End reaches 0 dBFS; Normalize Pan sets each layer's Pan so its left and right channels play at equal RMS level after the pan. A silent layer, and a mono one for Normalize Pan, keep their value. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `what` | [`Normalize`](#normalize) | yes | What to normalise. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `layers` | array or null | no | The layers; the selected layers if left out. |

Result: [`LayersChanged`](#layerschanged).

#### `device.parameters`

**Device Parameters**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Reports a device's parameters, in the order its type lists them: each one's number (what `device.set_param` takes), name, what it does, its kind (a continuous value with its range, unit, and taper; a gain, whose value is a linear factor from 0, which is -inf dB, up to its top; a switch; a choice with its names; or a whole number), its default, whether it can be automated (every parameter can), its value now, and how that value reads. Empty for a device whose type doesn't describe its parameters, such as a plug-in that couldn't be loaded. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceParameters`](#deviceparameters).

#### `device.paste`

**Paste Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Pastes the clipboard's device, as a new device with its settings, before the selected device (or `before`), or at the end of the chain with none selected, on the selected track (or `track`), and selects it: one undo step, named Copy Device. The chain keeps Live's order, so an audio effect can't go before an instrument, and instruments and MIDI effects only go on MIDI tracks. With `chain` it pastes into that rack chain, or before a device that is in one.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-003 | `Cmd+V` | `Ctrl+V` | `global` | Paste | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `before` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | Paste before this device, which may be in a rack's chain; before the selected device, or at the end of the chain with none selected, if left out. |
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) or null | no | A rack's chain to paste into, at any depth, in place of the track's own chain (WP-5.1). |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track; the selected track if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceAdded`](#deviceadded).

#### `device.remove`

**Delete Device**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Deletes a device from its track's chain, with its settings. Undo restores it, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first. To bypass a device but keep it, use `device.set_enabled`. From the keyboard it deletes the device selected in the Device View.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-005 | `Delete` | `Delete` | `global` | Delete | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.rename`

**Rename Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Renames a device: the name its title bar shows while Show Preset Name is on (`device.set_show_preset_name`). An empty name gives the device back its own name, such as `Auto Filter`. It changes nothing in the sound.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-008 | `Cmd+R` | `Ctrl+R` | `global` | Rename the selection | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `name` | string | yes | The new name. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.rename_layer`

**Rename Sample**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Renames a layer, as the layer list's Rename does. The name is what the title bar shows for the first layer while Show Preset Name is on.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) | yes | The layer. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its new name. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.replace`

**Replace Device**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces a device or rack with another of the same role, in its place, as loading from the browser does while the device is hot-swapped (an audio effect or audio effect rack for an audio effect; an instrument, an instrument rack or a drum rack for an instrument; a MIDI effect or MIDI effect rack for a MIDI effect). Give a `preset` file, or a `new_device` as `device.add` describes one. `device` is the one being hot-swapped, else the selected one, if left out. A device preset of the device's own kind loads into it as `device.load_preset` does, keeping its ID and automation; anything else replaces it with a new device with new IDs, without the automation of a device of another kind, and a rack's chains go with it. With `chain`, the new device becomes the only one in that chain, which keeps its name and mixer. One undo step, named Load Preset for a preset and Insert Device for a device. Hot-swap stays on for the replacement. Reads a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | [`ChainId`](#chainid) or null | no | A chain to give the new device to as its only one, instead of replacing a device: the chain keeps its mixer and name. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device or rack to replace; the device being hot-swapped, or else the selected one, if left out. |
| `new_device` | [`NewDevice`](#newdevice) or null | no | A new device, as `device.add` describes one. |
| `preset` | string or null | no | A preset file: a device's or a rack's. |

Result: [`DeviceAdded`](#deviceadded).

#### `device.reverse_sample`

**Reverse Sample**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Reverses the whole sample by writing a processed copy: a WAV with the sample's edits applied and then reversed, at its rate and channels, in the project's `Samples/Processed/Reverse/` folder. The device or layer then plays the copy with its edit list empty and its markers where they were, as one undo step; the original file stays as it was. A set that has never been saved is refused with a message in the Status Bar. The copy reads back as the device's or layer's `media`. `device.edit_sample` with `kind: reverse` reverses without a file.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The sampler device; the selected device if left out. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | A multisampler's layer; its first selected layer if left out. |

Result: [`SampleProcessed`](#sampleprocessed).

#### `device.save_default_preset`

**Save as Default Preset**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Saves a device's state as the default preset for its type, as the context menu's Save as Default Preset does: to the User Library's Defaults/<Audio Effects, Instruments, or MIDI Effects>/<the device's own name>.blpreset, replacing any default saved before. Every device of that type added from then on (`device.add`) starts with it; for a rack, every new rack of its kind starts as the saved one is, chains and all. Writes a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`PresetResult`](#presetresult).

#### `device.save_preset`

**Save Preset**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Saves a device's state (its parameter values) as a Beatlayer preset file (.blpreset), as the title bar's Save Preset button does: to `path`, or to a new file named after the device's title in the User Library, under Presets/<Audio Effects, Instruments, or MIDI Effects>/<the device's own name>/, numbered if the name is taken. The device's title then shows the preset's name. A rack is saved whole, as a rack preset: its chains in order with their names, colours and mixers, every device in them (nested racks too) with its state, a plug-in's own state included, and the samples its devices play, so it loads in a set that lacks them. The file is written whole or not at all. Writes a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `path` | string or null | no | The file to write, ending `.blpreset`; a new file in the User Library's folder for the device's presets, named after its title, if left out. |

Result: [`PresetResult`](#presetresult).

#### `device.scale_tempo`

**Scale Device Sample Tempo**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Multiplies a device's sample tempo by a factor, Live's ×2 and ÷2 (WP-5.15b): 2 doubles the tempo, 0.5 halves it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `factor` | number | yes | What to multiply by: 2 for ×2, 0.5 for ÷2. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.select`

**Select Device**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Selects a device, as clicking its title bar does, or none with `null`. The Device View's keys (Delete, Cmd-C, Cmd-D, Cmd-R) act on it. A device that floats in its own window also brings that window to the front. Selecting changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device, or `null` to select none. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `device.select_layers`

**Select Samples**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Selects layers in a multisampler's layer list, as clicking does: `replace` makes the listed layers the selection (every layer with none listed), `add` joins them to it, `toggle` flips each, and `same_range` selects every layer whose range in the editor in view equals the first listed layer's. The selection shows in the Sample tab and reads back in `device_view.state`. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `layers` | array of [`LayerId`](#layerid) | no | The layers; every layer if left out with `replace`. |
| `mode` | [`LayerSelectMode`](#layerselectmode) | no | How they change the selection. |

Result: [`MultisamplerState`](#multisamplerstate).

#### `device.select_slot`

**Select Sample Slot**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Selects one of a device's sample slots, as clicking its cell in the panel does: the panel then shows that slot's controls, and a sample loaded without naming a slot goes into it. Only a device with sample slots has any (the eight-slot drum sampler has eight, counted from 0). It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and isn't saved with the set. The selected slot is `selected_slot` in the device's panel (`device.state`).

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The slot, counted from 0. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `device.set_configured_params`

**Configure Plug-In**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces a plug-in device's list of configured parameters (clap-hosting R5, WP-5.40): the parameters its panel knobs and the automation and clip-envelope choosers show, in order. `params` holds them in their new order. One undo step. The list is saved with the set; `device.parameters` marks each parameter configured or not. The higher-level `plugin.configure_param`, `plugin.unconfigure_param` and `plugin.move_configured_param` edit one entry at a time and are what a person or an agent usually runs.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

| `params` | array of [`ParamId`](#paramid) | yes | The parameters in their new order. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

**Set Display View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Chooses the view a device's display shows, as its view buttons do: a compressor's Transfer Curve, Activity, or Collapsed. Only a device whose display has views takes one, and only one of them. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and `device_view.state` and `device.display` report the view chosen.

**Activate/Deactivate Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a device on or off, as its Device Activator in the title bar does. A device that's off passes its input through unchanged, so you can hear the track with and without it; it keeps its settings and its state.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether it's on. |

**Switch Device and Contents**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a device and every device inside it, at any depth, on or off with `enabled`: Option-click (Alt-click) on a rack's Device Activator. On a device that isn't a rack it is `device.set_enabled`. One undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-003 | `Option+click a device activator` | `Alt+click a device activator` | `device-view` | Turn every device in a rack on or off | toggles `enabled` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
