#### `device.set_external`

**Set External Device**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the routing of a device that works with hardware outside the computer (the External Instrument and the External Audio Effect), as the choosers in its title bar do; give only the settings to change. `midi_to` is `{ "type": "none" }` (No Output, a new device's) or `{ "type": "port", "name": ... }` with a MIDI output port's name as `midi.ports` lists it, with its Track switch on; `channel` is the MIDI channel to send on, 1 to 16 (1 on a new device); `audio_from` is the audio interface's inputs the hardware's sound comes back on, a channel or a pair (`{ "type": "pair", "channel": 1 }`, the first pair on a new device); `audio_to` is the audio interface's outputs an External Audio Effect sends its signal to, a channel or a pair (the first pair on a new device); `hardware_latency` is the delay the hardware adds that the computer can't detect, in the unit the unit switch is on: `{ "unit": "milliseconds", "value": 12.5 }` (0 to 1000, kept in milliseconds when the sample rate changes) or `{ "unit": "samples", "value": 600 }` (0 to 192000, kept in samples); to switch the unit, send the converted value. Each change recompiles the song's audio, so these are settings, not parameters. Read them back in the query tool's `device` result, under `external`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `audio_from` | [`Channel`](#channel) or null | no | Audio From: the audio interface's inputs it comes back on. |
| `audio_to` | [`Channel`](#channel) or null | no | Audio To: the audio interface's outputs an external effect sends its signal to. |
| `channel` | integer or null | no | The MIDI channel, 1 to 16. |
| `hardware_latency` | [`HardwareLatency`](#hardwarelatency) or null | no | Hardware Latency with its unit: the unit switch is the unit given, so switching the unit sends the converted value. |
| `midi_to` | [`ExternalPort`](#externalport) or null | no | MIDI To: `none` for No Output, or `port` with the MIDI output port's name. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_floating`

**Float**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Floats a native device in a window of its own (`floating`: true), or docks it back in the Device View (false), as the device's context menu item Float, its window's Dock button, and closing its window do. While it floats, its place in the chain shows as a narrow strip, so the signal order stays readable, and its window can be made larger: only its displays grow, its controls keeping their size and place. Floating and docking are one undo step each (Float Device, Dock Device); whether a device floats is saved with the set. Moving or resizing the window is `device.set_window`, which isn't an undo step. Plug-ins open their own editor windows instead, so they can't float. It changes nothing in the sound. From the keyboard (Option-F on macOS, Ctrl-Alt-F on Windows and Linux, with the Device View or a floating device's window focused) and the menu it switches the selected device.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-015 | `Option+F` | `Ctrl+Alt+F` | `device-view` | Float the selected device in its own window, or dock it | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `floating` | boolean | yes | Float (true) or dock (false). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_layer`

**Change Sample Settings**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Changes settings of layers (`layers`, or the selected ones) as the Sample tab does: Root Key, Detune, Volume (a linear gain), Pan, Sample Start and End, Link, the sustain and release modes, Loop Start and End, the Release Loop point, the loop's Crossfade and Detune. While the multisampler's Snap is on, every marker set lands on the nearest zero crossing of the layer's left channel. Markers are in frames of the sample at its own rate. The markers must stay ordered; one setting out of range refuses the whole change. One undo step. `device.update_layers` sets them exactly, without snapping.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `settings` | [`LayerSettings`](#layersettings) | yes | The settings to set; the ones left out stay as they were. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `layers` | array or null | no | The layers; the selected layers if left out. |

Result: [`LayersChanged`](#layerschanged).

#### `device.set_layer_media`

**Replace Sample**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces one layer's sample with another already in the media store, keeping the layer's zones and settings and its markers at the same share of the new length, as hot-swapping a sample does. `length`, `sample_rate` and `channels` describe the new sample. To pick a file from disk, use `device.set_layer_sample`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) | yes | The layer. |
| `media` | [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) | yes | The new sample, by content hash. |
| `length` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Its length in frames at its own rate. |
| `sample_rate` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Its own rate in hertz. |
| `channels` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | Its channels. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_layer_options`

**Change Sample Options**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the multisampler options that aren't parameters: `ram_mode` (decode every layer whole into memory; off, long layers stream from disk), `snap` (markers set afterwards land on zero crossings of the left channel) and `linear_loop_fades` (the title bar's Use Constant Power Fade for Loops, off when true). Options left out stay as they were.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `linear_loop_fades` | boolean or null | no | Whether loop crossfades are linear rather than constant-power. |
| `ram_mode` | boolean or null | no | RAM Mode: decode every layer whole into memory. |
| `snap` | boolean or null | no | Snap: markers land on zero crossings. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_layer_sample`

**Replace Sample**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces a layer's sample (`layer`, or the first selected layer) with an audio file, keeping its zones and settings and its markers at the same share of the new length, as hot-swapping a sample does. The file is imported into the set's media. One undo step. It reads a file outside the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The audio file. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) or null | no | The layer; the first selected layer if left out. |

Result: [`LayersChanged`](#layerschanged).

#### `device.set_layer_zone`

**Change Zones**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets one kind of zone (`key` 0 to 127, `velocity` 1 to 127, or `select` 0 to 127) of the listed layers, each with its own `low`, `high` and fades (`fade_low` and `fade_high`, how many values each fade spans). A zone holds at least one value and its fades stay inside it. In a fade the layer is silent at the zone's edge and reaches full level at the fade's inner edge, linearly or constant-power as the device's Fade Mode says. One undo step, as one drag in the zone editor is.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `kind` | [`ZoneKind`](#zonekind) | yes | Which zone. |
| `zones` | array of [`LayerZone`](#layerzone) | yes | Each layer's new zone. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_midi_sidechain_source`

**Set MIDI Sidechain Source**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the MIDI track a device's MIDI sidechain listens to, as the MIDI source chooser in its sidechain parameters does: `track` is a MIDI track (the device's own track too), or left out for No Input, a new device's. The device hears the notes and channel messages that track's clips and input play, before its own devices change them; the track still plays as before. Only devices that declare a MIDI sidechain input have one. Deleting the track leaves No Input.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The MIDI track whose notes and channel messages the device hears (its own track too), or `None` for No Input. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_multisampler_view`

**Set Multisampler View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets what a multisampler's views show, as its title bar's tabs and the zone editor's controls do: the `tab` in its body (`sample`, `pitch_osc`, `filter_global`, `modulation` or `midi`), whether the zone editor shows above the Device View (`zone_editor`, the Zone tab), which editor shows (`editor`: `key`, `velocity` or `select`), its row `size`, and Auto Select. The views are saved with the set but are no undo step, and change nothing in the sound. They read back in `device_view.state`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto_select` | boolean or null | no | Auto Select: notes select the layers they play. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `editor` | [`ZoneKind`](#zonekind) or null | no | Which zone editor shows: Key, Vel or Sel. |
| `size` | [`EditorSize`](#editorsize) or null | no | The zone editor's row size. |
| `tab` | [`SamplerTab`](#samplertab) or null | no | The tab shown in the body. |
| `zone_editor` | boolean or null | no | Whether the zone editor shows above the Device View (the Zone tab). |

Result: [`MultisamplerState`](#multisamplerstate).

#### `device.set_param`

**Set Device Parameter**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets one of a device's parameters to a value in the parameter's own units. The value must be finite. Parameters that haven't been set keep their defaults.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `param` | [`ParamId`](#paramid) | yes | The parameter. |
| `value` | number | yes | The value, in the parameter's own units. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_processed_layer_sample`

**Replace With Processed Copy**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces a layer's sample with a processed copy of its edited sample that is already in the media store (`media`, `length` frames at its own rate): the copy holds the edits, so the layer's list empties. `crop` is the span of the edited sample the copy keeps, which moves the markers as a Trim does; with none the markers stay where they are. One undo step, named Crop with a `crop` and Reverse without. `device.crop_sample` and `device.reverse_sample` write the copy.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `layer` | [`LayerId`](#layerid) | yes | The layer. |
| `media` | [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) | yes | The copy, by content hash. |
| `length` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Its length in frames at its own rate. |
| `crop` | [`SampleRange`](#samplerange) or null | no | The edited sample's span the copy keeps, or `null` for all of it. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_role`

**Use as MIDI Effect**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Places a device in another position of its chain (IMP-24): a plug-in that sends notes on from a note output can sit in the MIDI-effect position, before the instrument; `role` is where it goes (`midi_effect`, `instrument` or `audio_effect`), or left out to take the other position. A plug-in without a note output is refused, as is a role that breaks the chain's order (MIDI effects, then the instrument, then audio effects). The device keeps where it was placed, saved with the set. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `role` | [`DeviceRole`](#devicerole) or null | no | Where it goes in the chain; the other position if left out. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sample`

**Set Sample**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the audio a device plays (`media`, a content hash, or null to play none), which the media store holds like a clip's audio, in sample slot `slot` (counted from 0, and 0 unless given: the sampler has the one, the eight-slot drum sampler eight). A device whose type plays samples plays that file; other devices ignore it. The set keeps the reference, so it reopens playing the same file. Null clears the slot, one undo step named Clear Sample. To load a file from disk as a person does, use `device.load_sample`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `media` | [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) or null | no | The media, by content hash, or `null` to play none. The media store is where the audio comes from; a device given media the store doesn't hold is silent. |
| `slot` | integer from 0 to 255 | no | The sample slot to set: 0, the only one the sampler has, unless given; the eight-slot drum sampler's are 0 to 7 (WP-5.17). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sample_bpm`

**Set Device Sample BPM**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets a device's sample tempo in BPM, from 1 to 1,000 (WP-5.15b).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `bpm` | number | yes | The tempo in BPM: positive, from 1 to 1,000. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_show_preset_name`

**Show Preset Name**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a device's Show Preset Name, the context menu item: on (as every new device is), the title bar shows the name of the preset last loaded or saved, or the name Rename gave it; off, the device's own name. It changes nothing in the sound.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `shown` | boolean | yes | Whether the preset's or given name shows. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sidechain_enabled`

**External Sidechain On/Off**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a device's sidechain on or off, as the External switch in its sidechain section does. On, the device's detector (a compressor's level detector, say) listens to its sidechain input instead of the track's own signal; its output is still the track's signal, processed. Off, as on a new device, it listens to its own input.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether the sidechain is on. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sidechain_gain`

**Set SC Gain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the gain a device's sidechain signal gets before its detector hears it, as linear gain: 1 is 0 dB (a new device's), 2 about +6 dB, 0 silence. Raise it when the sidechain source is too quiet to trigger the device.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `gain` | number | yes | The gain: 1 is 0 dB. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sidechain_input`

**Set Sidechain Input**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets where a device's sidechain listens, as the Source chooser in its sidechain section does: `none` (No Input, a new device's), or `track` with another audio, group, or return track, Main, or the device's own track, and a `tap`: `pre_fx`, `post_fx` (what choosing a track in the window picks), or `post_mixer`. Only devices that declare a sidechain input have one. The source track still plays as before; the device only listens to it. The detector hears it only while External is on (`device.set_sidechain_enabled`). To make a kick duck a bass, set the bass compressor's source to the kick's track and switch External on.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `input` | [`Input`](#input) | yes | `none` (No Input), or `track` with an audio, group, or return track or Main (the device's own track too) and a `tap`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sidechain_listen`

**Sidechain Listen**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a device's Sidechain Listen: on, the device's output is what its detector hears (the sidechain, after its gain and mix) instead of the processed track, so you can check what triggers it. Switch it off to hear the track again.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `listen` | boolean | yes | Whether to listen. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_sidechain_mix`

**Set Sidechain Mix**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets how much of what a device's detector hears is its sidechain, from 0 (only the track's own signal) to 1 (only the sidechain, a new device's). Values between blend the two.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `mix` | number | yes | The mix, from 0 to 1. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_state`

**Set Device State**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces a device's whole state at once, as loading a preset does: `params` lists every parameter value to set, as `[parameter, value]` pairs (any parameter not listed goes back to its default), and `name` is what its title bar shows while Show Preset Name is on (empty for the device's own name). One undo step. To load a preset file, use `device.load_preset`; to change one parameter, `device.set_param`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `params` | array of pair of [`ParamId`](#paramid) and number | yes | The parameter values, as `[parameter, value]` pairs, each finite and each parameter once. |
| `name` | string | yes | The name the title bar shows while Show Preset Name is on, such as the preset's; empty for the device's own name. |
| `articulations` | array or null | no | An Articulation Map's articulations (the articulation map spec, R16), which a preset of one holds; `null` to keep the ones the device has. |
| `shape` | array or null | no | A Shaper's breakpoint shape (the modulation spec, R23), which a preset of one holds; `null` for the default shape. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_warp`

**Device Warp On/Off**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a device's Warp on or off (WP-5.15b). On, the sample plays through its warp map at the set's tempo; off, it plays at its own speed.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `warp` | boolean | yes | Whether Warp is on. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_warp_mode`

**Set Device Warp Mode**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets how a warped device's audio is fitted to the speed its warp map sets: `beats`, `tones`, `texture`, `re_pitch`, `complex` or `complex_pro` (WP-5.15b). Until the other modes are built, they play as `re_pitch` does.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `mode` | [`WarpMode`](#warpmode) | yes | The mode: Beats, Tones, Texture, Re-Pitch, Complex or Complex Pro. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_warp_settings`

**Set Device Warp Settings**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets controls of a device's warp modes, named by mode, any of them in one undo step (WP-5.15b). `beats`: `preserve` (`transients`, `1_bar`, `half`, `quarter`, `eighth`, `sixteenth`, `thirty_second`), `transient_loop_mode` (`loop_off`, `loop_forward`, `loop_back_and_forth`), `transient_envelope` (0 to 100, default 100). `tones`: `grain_size` (10 to 100 ms, default 30). `texture`: `grain_size` (10 to 500 ms, default 65), `flux` (0 to 100 %, default 25). `complex_pro`: `formants` (0 to 100 %, default 100), `envelope` (8 to 512, default 128).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `beats` | [`BeatsUpdate`](#beatsupdate) or null | no | Beats' controls to change. |
| `complex_pro` | [`ComplexProUpdate`](#complexproupdate) or null | no | Complex Pro's controls to change. |
| `texture` | [`TextureUpdate`](#textureupdate) or null | no | Texture's controls to change. |
| `tones` | [`TonesUpdate`](#tonesupdate) or null | no | Tones' controls to change. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.set_window`

**Move Device Window**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves or resizes a floating device's window, as dragging it does: `frame` is its outer top-left corner and the size of its contents, in points. A size is kept within the window's smallest (the device's docked size) and, for a device that doesn't grow, held at it. The frame is saved with the set but isn't an undo step, so undo never moves a window instead of undoing an edit.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The floating device. |
| `frame` | [`WindowFrame`](#windowframe) | yes | Where its window sits and how big its contents are, in points. |

Result: [`FloatingWindows`](#floatingwindows).

#### `device.show_sidechain`

**Show Sidechain**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Shows or hides a device's sidechain section, as the toggle at the top of the device's left strip does; switches unless `shown` says which. Only devices with a sidechain input or a MIDI sidechain input have one. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step. The section's settings are the set's: `device.set_sidechain_input`, `device.set_sidechain_enabled`, `device.set_sidechain_mix`, `device.set_sidechain_gain`, and `device.set_sidechain_listen`; the MIDI sidechain's, `device.set_midi_sidechain_source`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `shown` | boolean or null | no | Show (true) or hide (false); switches if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `device.snap_layer_markers`

**Snap Markers**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Snaps a loop's two markers (the sustain loop's Loop Start and Loop End, or the release loop's point) to the nearest zero crossings of the layers' left channel once, whatever Snap says, as the loop brace's context menu does. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The multisampler; the selected device if left out. |
| `layers` | array or null | no | The layers; the selected layers if left out. |
| `loop` | [`LoopKind`](#loopkind) | no | Which loop's markers; the sustain loop's if left out. |

Result: [`LayersChanged`](#layerschanged).

#### `device.sort_layers`

**Sort Samples**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sorts a multisampler's layers by name, key, velocity or selector (the lowest value of that zone), ascending or `descending`, as the layer list's sorting items do. Layers that tie keep their order.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `by` | [`LayerSort`](#layersort) | yes | What to sort by. |
| `descending` | boolean | yes | Whether the largest comes first. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.swap_to_snapshot`

**Swap to Simpler**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces a Drum Sampler with Simpler in One-Shot mode, as Drum Sampler's context menu does: the new device takes the old one's place, sample, and on or off state, and keeps its sample's Start and Length; every other setting is Simpler's default. One undo step, named Swap to Simpler, and the new device is selected. A device that isn't a Drum Sampler is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceAdded`](#deviceadded).

#### `device.ungroup`

**Ungroup**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Takes the selected rack (or `device`) apart, as Ungroup does: the devices of its one chain take the rack's place in order and the first is selected; the rack, its chain's mixer and its Macro Controls go. A rack with no chains is just removed; a rack of several chains can't be taken apart. One undo step (Ungroup).

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-002 | `Cmd+Shift+G` | `Ctrl+Shift+G` | `device-view` | Ungroup the selected rack | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`Ungrouped`](#ungrouped).

#### `device.unwrap_rack`

**Take a Rack Apart**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Takes a rack with one chain, or none, apart: the chain's devices take the rack's place in order, keeping their settings and running state; the rack, its chain and its mixer are gone. A rack of several chains can't be taken apart. One undo step. To ungroup the selected rack as a person does, use `device.ungroup`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.update_layers`

**Change Sample Settings**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Changes settings of the listed layers exactly as given, without snapping markers to zero crossings (`device.set_layer` does that while Snap is on): `root_key`, `detune`, `volume` (a linear gain, up to +24 dB), `pan`, `start`, `end`, `link`, `sustain` and `release` modes, `loop_start`, `loop_end`, `release_loop` (frames of the sample at its own rate), `crossfade_ms`, `loop_detune` and `one_shot` (the layer's voices play on to Sample End whatever the note does, as an SFZ `one_shot` region's do). Settings left out stay as they were. The markers must stay ordered: Start, Loop Start, Loop End, Release Loop and End, inside the sample. One setting out of range refuses the whole command.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `layers` | array of [`LayerId`](#layerid) | yes | The layers to change. |
| `settings` | [`LayerSettings`](#layersettings) | yes | The settings to set. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `device.windows`

**Floating Device Windows**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports every floating device's window (IMP-14), on any track: the device and its track, the window's title, where it sits and how big it is (`frame`, in points, `null` until the app has placed it), its smallest size (the device's docked size under its title bar), whether it can grow (only a device with a display that grows can), and the device as its window draws it. `device.set_floating` floats and docks devices. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`FloatingWindows`](#floatingwindows).

#### `device.wrap_in_rack`

**Wrap Devices in a Rack**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Wraps devices of one chain in a new rack, which takes the first device's place: the rack holds one chain that holds the devices in their order, each keeping its settings and running state. `devices` are in one chain of a track or a rack; `rack` is a new rack device (its kind `rack` of `instrument`, `audio_effect`, `midi_effect` or `drum`, and the role of its kind) with new IDs and exactly one empty chain. The rack's kind must be one that can hold them: an audio effect rack for audio effects alone, a MIDI effect rack for MIDI effects alone, an instrument rack for any other mix. A grouping that would break the chain's order is refused. One undo step. To group the selection as a person does, use `device.group`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `devices` | array of [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The devices, all in one chain of a track or a rack. Not empty. |
| `rack` | [`Device`](#device) | yes | The new rack, with a new ID, of a kind that can hold the devices, with exactly one chain, with a new ID and no devices. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `device_view`

#### `device_view.state`

**Device View State**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports what the Device View shows: the selected track and its devices in signal order, each with its title, its own name, its kind and role, whether it's on, folded, selected, or being hot-swapped, and whether it has an expanded part (`expandable`) and shows it (`expanded`); the selected device; hot-swapping; and whether there's a device to paste. A native device also lists its parameters' descriptors, its layout, and its values (`panel`); `device.parameters` reports any device's. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

### Area `edit`

#### `edit.go_to_step`

**Go to Step**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Returns the set to the state just after the step at `index`, counted up from the set's start: 0 is the set's start, before any step, and the newest step is the number of steps there are. The steps above that row are undone and stay listed, greyed, until a new change replaces them. The jump is no step of its own.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The row, counted up from the set's start: 0 is the set's start, before any step, and the newest step is the number of steps there are. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `edit.redo`

**Redo**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Redoes the step most recently undone. It fails if nothing has been undone since the last new change, because a new change discards the steps that could have been redone.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-007 | `Cmd+Shift+Z` | `Ctrl+Y` | `global` | Redo | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `edit.undo`

**Undo**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Undoes the newest step in the undo history: the last command or gesture, however many changes it made. Use it to reverse a mistake; `edit.redo` puts the step back. It fails if there's nothing to undo.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-006 | `Cmd+Z` | `Ctrl+Z` | `global` | Undo | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-A11Y-025 | `Delete` | `Delete` | `envelope` | Delete the selected breakpoint | runs it |

#### `envelope.enter`

**Envelope Enter**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `envelope`.

With no breakpoint selected, selects the breakpoint at the insert marker of the envelope that has the keyboard, or makes one there at the envelope's value at that point (the parameter's value when there is no envelope) and selects it. With one selected, keeps the changes made since it was selected and deselects it. All of it is one undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-A11Y-019 | `Enter` | `Enter` | `envelope` | Create or select a breakpoint at the insert marker, or confirm an edit | runs it |

#### `envelope.move_marker`

**Move Insert Marker Along Envelope**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `clip-view`, `envelope`.

Moves the insert marker along the envelope that has the keyboard, one grid step to the `left` or `right` with `by` `grid`, or to the previous or next breakpoint with `by` `breakpoint`; it stays at the end if there is none further. The result says the envelope's value at the marker. Does nothing while a breakpoint is selected: `envelope.move_selected` moves that. Changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [`ArrowKey`](#arrowkey) | yes | `left` for earlier, `right` for later. |
| `by` | [`MarkerStep`](#markerstep) | yes | `grid` for one grid step, or `breakpoint` for the previous or next breakpoint. |

Result: [`EnvelopeKeyState`](#envelopekeystate).

#### `envelope.move_selected`

**Move Selected Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `clip-view`, `envelope`.

Moves the selected breakpoint of the envelope that has the keyboard: `left` and `right` one grid step in time, not past its neighbours, and `up` and `down` by one step of the parameter's control (1% of its travel, or one step of a stepped value), within its range. The insert marker goes with it. It is part of the edit that began when the breakpoint was selected.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [`ArrowKey`](#arrowkey) | yes | `left` and `right` move it one grid step in time, `up` and `down` change its value by the step its parameter's control takes for an arrow key. |

Result: [`EnvelopeKeyState`](#envelopekeystate).

#### `envelope.select_adjacent`

**Select Adjacent Breakpoint**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `envelope`.

While a breakpoint of the envelope that has the keyboard is selected, selects the next one (the previous one with `reverse`) and moves the insert marker to it; it stays on the last or first. Part of the edit that began when the first breakpoint was selected. Does nothing with none selected.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-A11Y-022 | `Tab`, `Shift+Tab` | `Tab`, `Shift+Tab` | `envelope` | Select the next or previous breakpoint | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reverse` | boolean | no | Select the previous breakpoint instead of the next. |

Result: [`EnvelopeKeyState`](#envelopekeystate).

#### `envelope.set_value`

**Set Breakpoint Value**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `clip-view`, `envelope`.

Types a value for the selected breakpoint of the envelope that has the keyboard, as its parameter's control reads it (`-6 dB`, `25L`, `50%`); the other selected breakpoints of a lane move by the same share of the travel. With `at`, makes a new breakpoint there with the value instead. A value the parameter doesn't read is refused. Part of the edit that began when the breakpoint was selected, or one undo step on its own.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes | The value, as the parameter's control shows it: `-6` or `-6 dB` for a volume, `25L` for a pan, `50%` for a clip envelope. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | Where to make a new breakpoint with the value. Left out, the value goes to the selected breakpoint. |

Result: [`EnvelopeKeyState`](#envelopekeystate).

### Area `export`

#### `export.audio`

**Export Audio**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Renders the set's Main output (what you hear) or individual tracks to audio files, offline and faster than real time, as the File menu's Export Audio/Video does. `path` is the file to write. `bit_depth` (16, 24, or 32) is 24 and `sample_rate` the engine's rate when left out. `rendered_track` chooses `main` (the default), `all_tracks`, `selected_tracks`, or a single track `{ "track": <id> }`. With an individual track, `include_return_and_main_effects` includes return tracks and Main devices (unavailable for `main`). Multi-track exports write one file per track beside `path`. The file type follows the extension (`.wav`, `.aif`/`.aiff`, `.flac`, `.mp3`; FLAC holds 16 or 24 bits only) or `file_type`. MP3 writes 320 kbps CBR at one of MP3's sample rates, and ignores `bit_depth` and `dither`; `encode_mp3` also writes an MP3 of the same render beside a PCM file. `convert_to_mono` makes each file one channel, the average of left and right, before `normalize` and dither. `create_analysis_file` builds each written file's peaks and analysis into the caches, by the file's content hash, so importing it needs no analysis. The call returns when the export ends; only one export runs at a time, and `export.status` and `export.cancel` read and stop it. `render_as_loop` adds the tail the song leaves after the range's end onto the file's start, so the file loops without a cut tail. The range is `start` and `length` if given, otherwise the Arrangement's time selection, otherwise the whole set from 1.1.1 to the end of the last clip; it plays straight through, without the Arrangement loop. Below 32 bits, `dither` adds `triangular` noise unless told `rectangular` or `none`. `normalize` brings the highest peak to 0 dBFS. A rate below the engine's is rendered at the engine's and converted down. Files are written under temporary names and appear only when complete. Existing files are refused unless `replace` is true. Playback stops first, and plug-in devices render through the plug-ins the engine plays, lent to the export and handed back afterwards. An export whose path runs through external hardware renders in real time, on the running engine, after waiting `wait_seconds` seconds (10 unless given) so the hardware's sound dies away; `auto_restart` (on unless told otherwise) starts it again when a dropout spoils it, up to `max_attempts` times, and with it off the dropouts are listed. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The file to write, absolute or relative to the app's working directory, such as `/Music/Mix.wav`. Its folder must exist. |
| `auto_restart` | boolean or null | no | Whether the render starts again when a dropout spoils it: on unless told otherwise. With it off, the render carries on and the dropouts are listed. |
| `bit_depth` | one of `16`, `24`, `32` | no | Bits per sample: 16 or 24 (integers), or 32 (floating point; WAV and AIFF only). Left out, 24. MP3 has no bit depth, so it ignores this. |
| `convert_to_mono` | boolean | no | Convert to Mono: each file holds one channel, the average of the render's left and right, taken before Normalize and dither. An MP3 is written mono too. |
| `create_analysis_file` | boolean | no | Create Analysis File: once a file is written, build its peaks and its analysis (transients, tempo and beats) and keep them by the file's content hash, where an imported file's are kept, so the file brought into a set needs no analysis. Nothing is written beside the file. |
| `dither` | [`Dither`](#dither) or null | no | The dither below 32 bits. Left out, `triangular`. MP3 ignores it. |
| `encode_mp3` | boolean | no | Encode MP3: also write an MP3 of the same render, 320 kbps, beside each PCM file with its name and `.mp3`. With `file_type` `mp3` the MP3 is the only file. |
| `file_type` | [`FileType`](#filetype) or null | no | The file type. Left out, the path's extension decides: `.wav`; `.aif` or `.aiff`; `.flac`; `.mp3`. Given, it must agree with the extension. |
| `include_return_and_main_effects` | boolean | no | Include return and Main effects when rendering individual tracks. Unavailable (refused) when `rendered_track` is `main`. |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | How long the range is, in ticks (705,600 to the quarter note). Left out, to the end of the time selection, or without one to the end of the set's last clip. |
| `max_attempts` | integer or null | no | The most times the render may start again after a dropout: no limit when left out. |
| `normalize` | boolean | no | Normalize: raise or lower the whole export so its highest peak is at full scale (0 dBFS). |
| `render_as_loop` | boolean | no | Render as Loop: the song goes on past the range's end as if Stop were pressed there, until the output has stayed below -120 dBFS for 100 ms or 60 s have passed, and that tail is added onto the file's start, wrapping round if it's longer than the range. The file is still exactly the range long. Off unless given. |
| `rendered_track` | [`RenderedTrack`](#renderedtrack) or null | no | Which track(s) to render: `main` (the default), `all_tracks`, `selected_tracks`, or a single track `{ "track": <id> }`. |
| `replace` | boolean | no | Replace a file already at `path`. Without it, an existing file is left alone and the export refused. |
| `sample_rate` | integer or null | no | The file's sample rate in hertz, from 8,000 to 384,000, such as 44100 or 48000. Left out, the engine's rate. MP3 holds 8,000, 11,025, 12,000, 16,000, 22,050, 24,000, 32,000, 44,100, or 48,000 Hz. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the range starts. Left out, the start of the Arrangement's time selection, or 1.1.1 without one. |
| `wait_seconds` | integer or null | no | How long the render waits before it starts, in seconds, so the hardware's last sound dies away: 10 unless given, and longer if the seconds are given. |

Result: [`ExportResult`](#exportresult).

#### `export.start`

**Export**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Exports with the open dialog's choices, as its Export button does. It returns at once, and the export goes on in the background: read its share with `export.status` and stop it with `export.cancel`. One export runs at a time. The files are written outside the project. Changes nothing in the set.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

**Clip View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves the keyboard focus to the Clip View's editor, so the Clip View's shortcuts apply, showing the Clip View first if it is hidden. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step. The result is the detail area's state. With the second window open it acts on the window `window` names, `main` or `second`, and on the window with the focus without it.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FOCUS-004 | `Option+3` | `Alt+3` | `global` | Move focus to the Clip View's editor | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | [`WindowName`](#windowname) or null | no | The window to act on, `main` or `second`. Left out, the window with the focus. |

Result: [`DetailState`](#detailstate).

#### `focus.control_bar`

**Control Bar**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves the keyboard focus to the Control Bar at the top of the main window, onto the control focused there last. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FOCUS-001 | `Option+0` | `Alt+0` | `global` | Move focus to the Control Bar | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `focus.device_view`

**Device View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves the keyboard focus to the Device View, so its shortcuts apply, showing the Device View first if it is hidden. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step. The result is the detail area's state. With the second window open it acts on the window `window` names, `main` or `second`, and on the window with the focus without it.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FOCUS-005 | `Option+4` | `Alt+4` | `global` | Move focus to the Device View | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | [`WindowName`](#windowname) or null | no | The window to act on, `main` or `second`. Left out, the window with the focus. |

Result: [`DetailState`](#detailstate).

#### `focus.next`

**Next**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `tab-focus`, `settings`.

Moves the keyboard focus to the next control in the focused area or window. Tab does this in the Settings window, and in the main window while Use Tab Key to Move Focus is on.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FOCUS-011 | `Tab` | `Tab` | `tab-focus` | Move to the next focusable control | runs it |
| S-SET-001 | `Tab` | `Tab` | `settings` | Move to the next option | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `focus.next_neighbor`

**Next Neighbor**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `tab-focus`.

Moves the keyboard focus from a track's control to the same control on the next track, such as from one track's volume to the next track's volume, in the mixers and the Arrangement's track headers, without changing the selected track. Navigate > Next Neighbor runs it whenever there's a next track; Option-Tab (Ctrl-Tab) does while Use Tab Key to Move Focus is on. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FOCUS-013 | `Option+Tab` | `Ctrl+Tab` | `tab-focus` | Move to the same control on the next track (next neighbour) | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `focus.previous`

**Previous**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `tab-focus`, `settings`.

Moves the keyboard focus to the previous control in the focused area or window, the reverse of `focus.next`.

Default keys:

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FOCUS-012 | `Shift+Tab` | `Shift+Tab` | `tab-focus` | Move to the previous focusable control | runs it |
| S-SET-002 | `Shift+Tab` | `Shift+Tab` | `settings` | Move to the previous option, or back to the page list from the first option | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

#### `focus.previous_neighbor`

**Previous Neighbor**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `tab-focus`.

Moves the keyboard focus from a track's control to the same control on the previous track, the reverse of `focus.next_neighbor`. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FOCUS-014 | `Option+Shift+Tab` | `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | `tab-focus` | Move to the same control on the previous track (previous neighbour) | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

#### `focus.toggle_tab_navigation`

**Use Tab Key to Move Focus**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches whether Tab and Shift-Tab move the keyboard focus between controls in the main window. While it's off, as it is by default, Tab switches between the Session and Arrangement Views. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `focus.toggle_wrap_navigation`

**Wrap Keyboard Navigation**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches whether Tab and Shift-Tab wrap round at the ends of the focused area or track: from its last control to its first, and from its first to its last. It's on in a new install, as Live's is; while it's off, they stop at the ends. The Settings window calls it Wrap Tab Navigation. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).
