### Area `groove`

#### `groove.add`

**Add Groove**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Adds a groove to the end of the set's Groove Pool: a `groove` with a new ID, a name, a `length` in ticks, its `notes` (each a `position` from 0 to before the length and a `velocity` from 1 to 127, none two at one position) and its parameters, which are Base `1/16`, Quantize 0, Timing 100, Random 0 and Velocity 0 where left out. It changes no clip: use `clip.set_groove` to give a clip the groove. A groove that breaks those limits is refused. One undo step, `Add Groove`. To make a groove from a clip, use `groove.extract`; from a file, `groove.load`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `groove` | [`Groove`](#groove) | yes | The groove, with a new ID. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `groove.commit`

**Commit Groove**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `clip-view`.

Writes a clip's groove into the clip and sets its groove to none. A MIDI clip's notes move to where they play with the groove and take the velocities they play at, Random drawn once from `seed` (a new seed if left out). A warped audio clip gets a warp marker at each grid line and moved transient where the groove puts it, over the part of its contents that plays, and, while the groove's Velocity is above 0, a Volume clip envelope stepping through the gains it gives, replacing any Volume envelope the clip had (a Volume envelope only lowers a level, so the steps are shares of the loudest and the clip's gain rises by that gain). `clips` names the clips; left out, the selected ones; with `groove` and no clips, every clip that uses the groove. A clip with no groove is left as it is. One undo step, `Commit Groove`, however many clips it commits. An audio clip needs its file's analysis to be ready. Returns the clips committed.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips to commit. Left out, the selected ones. |
| `groove` | [`GrooveId`](#grooveid) or null | no | A groove: with it and no `clips`, every clip that uses the groove is committed. |
| `seed` | integer or null | no | The seed Random's one draw comes from. Left out, a new one. |

Result: [`GrooveCommitted`](#groovecommitted).

#### `groove.delete`

**Delete Groove**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Takes a groove out of the Groove Pool, as the Delete key does in the pool: every clip that used it is set to no groove, and if it was the auto-load groove nothing is auto-loaded any more. One undo step, `Delete Groove`. Because it removes the person's work, an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `groove` | [`GrooveId`](#grooveid) | yes | The groove. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `groove.extract`

**Extract Groove**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `clip-view`.

Makes a groove of each clip it names (`clips`, or the selected clips) at the end of the Groove Pool, from the part of the clip that plays: its loop brace while its loop is on, otherwise its Start to its End marker, the groove as long as that part. From a MIDI clip, a groove note at each note's start with its velocity, the loudest where notes start together. From an audio clip, a groove note at each of its transients, in its beats through its warp map (an unwarped clip's at the set's tempo where it starts), with a velocity from the audio's peak level in the 20 ms after it: the loudest peak 127, and 48 dB below it 1. The groove is named after the clip (`Groove` if it has no name) and has Base 1/16, Quantize 0, Timing 100, Random 0 and Velocity 0. An audio clip needs its file's analysis to be ready. One undo step, `Extract Groove`. Returns the grooves' IDs.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips to make grooves of. Left out, the selected ones. |

Result: [`GrooveExtracted`](#grooveextracted).

#### `groove.load`

**Load Groove**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Reads a groove file (`.blgroove`, Beatlayer's own JSON format) and adds the groove it holds to the end of the Groove Pool, with the parameters it holds, as double-clicking a groove in the browser does. With `clips`, those clips are given the groove too. One undo step, `Load Groove`. A file that is damaged, was saved by a newer Beatlayer or breaks a groove's limits is refused and changes nothing; loading the same file twice adds two grooves. Reads a file outside the project. Returns the groove's ID and name.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The groove file, a `.blgroove`, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. |
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | no | Clips to give the groove to as well, in the same undo step. |

Result: [`GrooveLoaded`](#grooveloaded).

#### `groove.pool`

**Groove Pool**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports the set's grooves: each with its ID, name, length, notes and its Base, Quantize, Timing, Random and Velocity, whether it is active (some clip uses it) and which clips use it; the Global Amount; and Auto Load Groove with its groove. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`GroovePoolState`](#groovepoolstate).

#### `groove.rename`

**Rename Groove**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Renames a groove in the Groove Pool. One undo step, `Rename Groove`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `groove` | [`GrooveId`](#grooveid) | yes | The groove. |
| `name` | string | yes | The new name. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `groove.save`

**Save Groove**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Writes a groove of the pool, with its current parameters, to a groove file: at `path`, or as `<name>.blgroove` in the User Library's Grooves folder, where the browser's Grooves label finds it. The file is written whole or not at all, and a file already there is left alone and the save refused unless `replace` is true. Changes nothing in the set and is no undo step; writes a file outside the project. Returns the path written.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `groove` | [`GrooveId`](#grooveid) | yes | The groove, one of the pool's. |
| `path` | string or null | no | The file to write. Left out, `<name>.blgroove` in the User Library's Grooves folder. |
| `replace` | boolean | no | Replace a file already there. Without it, an existing file is left alone and the save refused. |

Result: [`GrooveSaved`](#groovesaved).

#### `groove.set`

**Set Groove**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets any of a groove's parameters, as its row in the Groove Pool does, and keeps those left out: `base` (`1/4`, `1/8`, `1/8T`, `1/16`, `1/16T` or `1/32`), `quantize` (0 to 100 percent), `timing` (0 to 100), `random` (0 to 100) and `velocity` (-100 to +100). A value out of range refuses them all. A change reaches every clip playing the groove from the next block. One undo step, named for the parameter when one is set: `Change Base`, `Change Quantize`, `Change Timing`, `Change Random` or `Change Velocity`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `groove` | [`GrooveId`](#grooveid) | yes | The groove. |
| `base` | [`GrooveBase`](#groovebase) or null | no | The grid its notes are measured against. |
| `quantize` | number or null | no | Quantize, from 0 to 100 percent. |
| `random` | number or null | no | Random, from 0 to 100 percent. |
| `timing` | number or null | no | Timing, from 0 to 100 percent. |
| `velocity` | number or null | no | Velocity, from -100 to +100 percent. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `groove.set_auto_load`

**Set Auto Load Groove**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the Auto Load Groove switch (`enabled`) and the groove a new MIDI clip takes while it is on (`groove`, one of the pool's), and keeps what is left out. A MIDI clip made new, empty or by recording takes that groove; a clip made by copying, pasting or importing keeps its own. One undo step, `Change Auto Load Groove`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean or null | no | Whether a new MIDI clip takes the auto-load groove. |
| `groove` | [`GrooveId`](#grooveid) or null | no | The auto-load groove, one of the pool's. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `groove.set_global_amount`

**Set Global Groove Amount**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the Global Amount, from 0 to 130 percent: it scales Timing, Random and Velocity for every groove in the set at once, and not Quantize; 100 plays each groove as set. The set holds one. It reaches every clip playing a groove from the next block. One undo step, `Change Global Amount`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | number | yes | The amount, in percent. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `groove.to_clip`

**Groove to Clip**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Makes a MIDI clip of a groove of the pool on a MIDI track at a position, as dragging the groove onto the track does: a note on C3 (key 60) at each groove note with its velocity, each a sixteenth long or as long as the gap to the next note, whichever is shorter; the clip one groove long, looping, and named after the groove. A clip made so takes no auto-load groove. A clip already there is replaced where the new one covers it. One undo step, `Groove to Clip`. Returns the clip's ID.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `groove` | [`GrooveId`](#grooveid) | yes | The groove, one of the pool's. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The MIDI track to put the clip on. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the clip starts, in ticks. |

Result: [`GrooveClip`](#grooveclip).

### Area `keymap`

#### `keymap.bind`

**Bind Keys**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Gives a command the keys, which run it in the context (the command's default shortcut's, or `global` when it has none). The keys are written as the shortcut reference writes them, such as `Cmd+Option+D`. The keys are taken at once, and the file is written at once; nothing is part of the set and nothing is an undo step. Refuses the contexts that take no user shortcut, and the keys that run another command where the Shortcuts page would ask, unless `replace` is true.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | string | yes | The command to bind, by its ID. |
| `keys` | array of string | yes | The keys, as the shortcut reference writes them. |
| `platform` | [`Platform`](#platform) | yes | The platform the keys are for. |
| `args` | object | no | The arguments the binding fixes, as the default keymap's entries fix them. |
| `context` | string or null | no | The context the keys run in; without one, the command's default shortcut's, or `global` when the command has none. |
| `replace` | boolean | no | Whether to take the keys from the command they already run, which the page asks about (R9). |

Result: [`KeymapResult`](#keymapresult).

#### `keymap.reset`

**Reset Keys**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Gives a command Live 12's own keys back, or every command's when no command is named, emptying the person's keymap file. The file is written at once; nothing is part of the set and nothing is an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | string or null | no | The command to give Live's keys back; without one, every command. |

Result: [`KeymapResult`](#keymapresult).

#### `keymap.state`

**Keymap State**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports the keymap in use on each platform: every shortcut with its keys, context, trigger and commands, and whether its keys are Live's, the person's own, or a default their keymap file unbinds; and every entry the file holds that can't be used, with why. The person's own shortcuts are in `keymap.toml`, beside the preferences, layered over Live 12's. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`KeymapState`](#keymapstate).

#### `keymap.unbind`

**Unbind Keys**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Takes a shortcut's keys away: the default shortcut by its ID, such as `S-EDIT-004`, or a command with the keys themselves. The keys go on one platform, or on both without a platform. The file is written at once; nothing is part of the set and nothing is an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | string or null | no | The command whose keys go, with the keys themselves. |
| `keys` | array of string | no | The keys, as the shortcut reference writes them. |
| `platform` | [`Platform`](#platform) or null | no | The platform whose keys go; without one, both. |
| `shortcut` | string or null | no | The default shortcut's ID, such as `S-EDIT-004`. |

Result: [`KeymapResult`](#keymapresult).

### Area `locator`

#### `locator.add`

**Add Locator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Adds a locator at `at`, as the Set Locator button and Add Locator do. Left out, it goes where the button puts one: on the line of the global launch quantisation nearest the playhead while the song plays, and at the time selection's start, or the insert marker, while it is stopped. A locator is named with the next whole number, one more than the highest any locator is named with, and becomes the only selected locator. Two locators never share a position: adding one where another is leaves that one as it is. The locators are saved with the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the locator goes. Left out, it goes where the Set Locator button puts one: on the line of the global launch quantisation nearest the playhead while the song plays, and at the time selection's start, or the insert marker, while it is stopped. |

Result: [`LocatorResult`](#locatorresult).

#### `locator.delete`

**Delete Locator**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Deletes the locators (`locators`, or the selected ones), as the Delete Locator button and the Delete key do. A song start time on one of them goes with it. Because it removes the person's work, an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `locators` | array or null | no | The locators to delete. Left out, the selected ones. |

Result: [`LocatorResult`](#locatorresult).

#### `locator.jump`

**Jump to Locator**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Jumps to a locator (`locator`, or the selected one), as clicking it does: while the song plays, playback jumps there on the next line of the global launch quantisation; while it is stopped, the insert marker moves there. It changes nothing in the set, and it is refused while the audio engine is off.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `locator` | [`LocatorId`](#locatorid) or null | no | The locator. Left out, the selected one. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `locator.jump_next`

**Jump to Next Locator**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Jumps to the locator after the current position: the playhead while the song plays, the insert marker while it is stopped. With no locator after it, it jumps to the end of the arrangement. It selects no locator, changes nothing in the set, and is refused while the audio engine is off.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `locator.jump_previous`

**Jump to Previous Locator**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Jumps to the locator before the current position: the playhead while the song plays, the insert marker while it is stopped. With no locator before it, it jumps to 1.1.1. It selects no locator, changes nothing in the set, and is refused while the audio engine is off.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `locator.loop_to_next`

**Loop to Next Locator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Sets the Arrangement's loop brace from a locator (`locator`, or the selected one) to the next one and switches the loop on, as the locator's context menu does. The last locator has none after it, and is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `locator` | [`LocatorId`](#locatorid) or null | no | The locator. Left out, the selected one. |

Result: [`LocatorResult`](#locatorresult).

#### `locator.move`

**Move Locator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves a locator (`locator`, or the selected ones) to `to`, the position it goes to, and moves every other selected locator by the same distance. The keys pass the grid step Left and Right move, and a drag passes the position the pointer is at, snapped to the editing grid as a clip's start does. A locator can't go before 1.1.1, and a move that would put two locators at one position changes nothing. Dragging a locator runs this, and the whole drag is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | [`Position`](#position) | yes | Where it goes: the position the locator moves to. The keys pass the grid step Left and Right move. |
| `locator` | [`LocatorId`](#locatorid) or null | no | The locator to move. Left out, the selected ones. |

Result: [`LocatorResult`](#locatorresult).

#### `locator.rename`

**Rename Locator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Renames the locators (`locators`, or the selected ones), as Cmd-R (Ctrl-R) and Edit > Rename do. The new name is `name`; an empty name keeps the old one. Left out, the name is typed in place, as Cmd-R does.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `locators` | array or null | no | The locators to rename. Left out, the selected ones. |
| `name` | string or null | no | The new name. An empty name keeps the old one. Left out, the name is typed in place, as Cmd-R does. |

Result: [`LocatorResult`](#locatorresult).

#### `locator.select`

**Select Locators**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Selects locators in the Arrangement, as clicking one does: `replace` selects only these, `toggle` adds or removes each, `add` adds them, and `extend` adds them and every locator between them and the first selected locator. Selecting is never an undo step and changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `locators` | array of [`LocatorId`](#locatorid) | yes | The locators. |
| `mode` | [`SelectMode`](#selectmode) | no | How to change the selection; `replace` if left out. |

Result: [`ArrangementState`](#arrangementstate).

#### `locator.set_info_text`

**Set Locator Info Text**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Sets the info text of a locator (`locator`, or the selected one), which the Info View shows while the pointer is over it. The person's own way of typing it comes later.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `info_text` | string | yes | The info text, which the Info View shows while the pointer is over the locator. |
| `locator` | [`LocatorId`](#locatorid) or null | no | The locator. Left out, the selected one. |

Result: [`LocatorResult`](#locatorresult).

### Area `midi`

#### `midi.capture`

**Capture MIDI**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Capture MIDI (Create ▸ Capture MIDI; the Control Bar's button). Brings back the notes played on the MIDI tracks that monitor their input, since the last capture or recording, as one clip on each track that was played, with their velocities and timing. A track with a clip playing while the transport runs gets the notes added to that clip: it grows to the loop pass the last note falls in and its loop moves there, keeping its length. Any other track gets a new clip in the selected scene's slot if it is empty, else the next empty slot below, else a scene added at the end; the clip's loop is the whole bars that cover its last phrase, from the first note-on to the last. With the transport stopped the first note is on 1.1.1 and the song's tempo may change to the played tempo; with it running the tempo stays. Control changes, pitch bend and pressure are not captured yet. Refused when no note was played; `transport.state` shows `capture_midi_ready`. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`Captured`](#captured).

#### `midi.computer_keyboard_key`

**Computer Keyboard Key**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Presses or releases one of the computer MIDI keyboard's note keys, as typing it does: a press sends a note-on at the keyboard's velocity on MIDI channel 1, a release the note-off of the note that key started, even if the octave moved meanwhile. The notes reach the tracks whose MIDI From is Computer Keyboard or All Ins. A press fails while the keyboard is off. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | The note key's letter: A W S E D F T G Y H U J K O L P, from the lowest note up. |
| `pressed` | boolean | yes | Whether the key goes down (the note starts) or comes up (it ends). |

Result: [`KeyboardKeyResult`](#keyboardkeyresult).

#### `midi.computer_keyboard_octave`

**Computer Keyboard Octave**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves the computer MIDI keyboard's octave by `steps`, as Z (down) and X (up) do: 12 semitones a step, from C-2 to C8 for the A key, stopping at the ends. Notes already held keep sounding until their keys come up. Works whether or not the keyboard is on. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `steps` | integer from -16 to 16 | yes | The steps to move: -1 for down (Z, C), 1 for up (X, V). Any number of steps is allowed; it stops at the ends of the range. |

Result: [`KeyboardInfo`](#keyboardinfo).

#### `midi.computer_keyboard_velocity`

**Computer Keyboard Velocity**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Steps the computer MIDI keyboard's velocity by `steps` through 1, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, and 127, as C (lower) and V (raise) do, stopping at the ends. It starts at 100. Works whether or not the keyboard is on. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `steps` | integer from -16 to 16 | yes | The steps to move: -1 for down (Z, C), 1 for up (X, V). Any number of steps is allowed; it stops at the ends of the range. |

Result: [`KeyboardInfo`](#keyboardinfo).

#### `midi.export_clip`

**Export MIDI Clip**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Writes a MIDI clip's notes as a type 1 Standard MIDI File at `path`, as the File menu's Export MIDI Clip does: its notes' pitches, starts, lengths and velocities, its tempo (the song's tempo where the clip starts) and its time signature. Fails for an audio clip, or for a file already at `path` unless `replace` is true. Writes a file outside the project; changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The MIDI clip to write. |
| `path` | string | yes | The file to write, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. Its folder must exist. `.mid` or `.midi` by convention. |
| `replace` | boolean | no | Replace a file already at `path`. Without it, an existing file is left alone and the export refused. |

Result: [`MidiExportResult`](#midiexportresult).

#### `midi.import_file`

**Import MIDI File**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Reads a Standard MIDI File (type 0 or type 1) into the Arrangement, as dragging it in or the Create menu's Import MIDI File does: each of the file's tracks that has notes becomes a MIDI clip. With no `track`, each becomes a new MIDI track below the last one, named as a new track is; with a `track`, the file's one track with notes goes on that MIDI track. Clips start at `at`, or the insert marker. Each clip keeps the file's leading silence, is named after its track's name (or `Track N`), carries the file's time signature, loops its whole length, and lasts from its first note to its last note-off rounded up to a whole bar. With `import_tempo`, the file's tempo and time signature come into the song as Live's "Import tempo and time signature data into Arrangement?" answer Yes does: a single-tempo file sets the song's tempo, a file whose tempo changes writes Song Tempo automation over the clip and restores the tempo at its end, and a time-signature marker is written at the clip's start and one restoring the previous signature at its end. Off (the default), the song's tempo, automation and markers are left alone. A clip placed over part of another replaces that part, so a track never plays two clips at once; when a clip on `track` ends after `at`, it's destructive as well as external. One undo step. Reads a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The Standard MIDI File to read, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. Its type 0 or type 1 tracks become clips. |
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | Where the first clip starts, in ticks (705,600 to the quarter note). Left out, the Arrangement's insert marker. |
| `import_tempo` | boolean | no | Whether to bring the file's tempo and time signature into the song, as Live's "Import tempo and time signature data into Arrangement?" asks. Off unless given, so an agent never changes the song's tempo by accident. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The MIDI track to put the file's clips on. Left out, each track of the file with notes gets a new MIDI track below the last one. |

Result: [`MidiImportResult`](#midiimportresult).

#### `midi.ports`

**MIDI Ports**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Lists every MIDI input and output port the computer offers, each with its Track, Sync, Remote and MPE switches as the Settings window's Tempo & MIDI page shows them, and the computer MIDI keyboard's state. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`MidiPortsResult`](#midiportsresult).

#### `midi.set_port`

**Set MIDI Port**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Changes a MIDI port's Track, Sync, Remote and MPE switches, as the Settings window's MIDI ports table does; switches left out stay as they are. A port is open while its Track, Sync or Remote switch is on and closed when all three are off; MPE opens nothing by itself. An input's notes and controllers reach tracks only while its Track switch is on, and as MPE, each note on a channel of its own with its own pitch, slide and pressure, while its MPE switch is on too; Sync and Remote are kept and act when sync and MIDI mapping are built. Output ports have no MPE switch, and `mpe` on one is refused. The port's switches are kept for the next start, and aren't part of the set or an undo step. Opens or closes a device outside Beatlayer. Fails if the computer doesn't offer the port now.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [`PortDirection`](#portdirection) | yes | Input or output. |
| `name` | string | yes | The port's name, as `midi.ports` lists it. |
| `mpe` | boolean or null | no | MPE on or off, for an input. Left out, it stays as it is. |
| `remote` | boolean or null | no | Remote on or off. Left out, it stays as it is. |
| `sync` | boolean or null | no | Sync on or off. Left out, it stays as it is. |
| `track` | boolean or null | no | Track on or off. Left out, it stays as it is. |

Result: [`PortInfo`](#portinfo).

#### `midi.toggle_computer_keyboard`

**Computer MIDI Keyboard**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches the computer MIDI keyboard, as the Control Bar's switch and M do, to `on`, or to the other state if it's left out. While it's on, the letter keys play notes (A W S E D F T G Y H U J K O L P) to the tracks whose MIDI From is Computer Keyboard or All Ins; Z and X move its octave, C and V its velocity, and the letters it uses don't run their shortcuts unless Shift is held. Switching it off ends every note it holds. Whether it's on is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-MAP-003 | `M` | `M` | `global` | Turn the computer MIDI keyboard on or off | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Switch it on or off. Left out, it switches to the other state. |

Result: [`KeyboardInfo`](#keyboardinfo).

### Area `midi_tool`

#### `midi_tool.apply`

**Apply MIDI Tool**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `clip-view`.

Applies a MIDI Tool once, with its settings, whether Auto is on or off. A transformation replaces its input (the given `notes`, the selected notes, the notes that start in the time selection, or the notes that start in the clip's loop); a generator writes notes into the range, replacing the notes at the same key that overlap them. `values` replace the tool's settings for those parameters and are kept. `seed` (0 to 4294967295) makes the random choices repeatable; left out, a new one is drawn. The notes written are selected afterwards. One undo step named after the tool, even when the notes come out unchanged. Cmd+Enter (S-NOTE-033) and Edit ▸ Apply Transformation/Generator run it. A transformation with no input is refused, and so is a run that would write more than 65536 notes. A call that would leave the clip fewer notes asks first. Read the notes in the query tool's `clip` (`data.midi.notes`).

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-033 | `Cmd+Enter` | `Ctrl+Enter` | `note-editor` | Apply the current MIDI tool's settings | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes a transformation takes as input, by their place in the clip's notes in order. Left out, the Clip View's selection. |
| `range` | [`RangeArgs`](#rangeargs) or null | no | The range to act on. Left out, the note editor's time selection or the clip's loop. |
| `seed` | integer or null | no | The seed, from 0 to 4294967295. Left out, a new one is drawn. |
| `tool` | string or null | no | The tool's ID. Left out, the chosen tool of the panel shown last. |
| `values` | object or null | no | Parameters to set before applying, by ID. They replace the tool's settings for those parameters and are kept as its settings. |

Result: [`MidiToolState`](#miditoolstate).

#### `midi_tool.choose`

**Choose MIDI Tool**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `clip-view`.

Chooses the tool the Transform or Generate panel shows for the track of a MIDI clip, as the Transformation or Generator Selector does: a transformation or a generator, by its ID from `midi_tool.list`. Each track remembers its choice, saved with the set. Changes no notes and is no undo step; read it back in `midi_tool.state`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tool` | string | yes | The tool's ID, from `midi_tool.list`. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip whose track's panel shows the tool. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |

Result: [`MidiToolState`](#miditoolstate).

#### `midi_tool.close`

**Close MIDI Tool Application**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `clip-view`.

Closes the open MIDI Tool application, so the next change of a tool's parameters starts a new one on the notes as they are then. Leaves the notes as they are. View state: no undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |

Result: [`MidiToolState`](#miditoolstate).

#### `midi_tool.list`

**List MIDI Tools**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `clip-view`.

Lists the MIDI Tools: every transformation, then every generator, in the order the Transformation and Generator Selectors list them. Each has its ID, name and kind, and its parameters: ID, name, kind (number, whole, choice, switch, pitch, pitch_range, division, breakpoints, levels, toggles or structured), range, default, unit, whether it counts scale degrees, and what it does. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ToolList`](#toollist).

#### `midi_tool.reseed`

**Reseed MIDI Tool**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `clip-view`.

Gives the open MIDI Tool application a new seed, or the one it is given, and runs the tool again on the notes it started from, as a tool's Reseed button does. Refused while no application is open. A call that would leave the clip fewer notes asks first. Read the seed in `midi_tool.state`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |
| `seed` | integer or null | no | The seed, from 0 to 4294967295. Left out, a new one is drawn. |

Result: [`MidiToolState`](#miditoolstate).

#### `midi_tool.reset`

**Reset MIDI Tool**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `clip-view`.

Puts every parameter of a MIDI Tool back to its default and leaves its Auto switch as it is. Changes no notes and is no undo step. Closes the open application. Read it back in `midi_tool.state`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |
| `tool` | string or null | no | The tool's ID. Left out, the chosen tool of the panel shown last. |

Result: [`MidiToolState`](#miditoolstate).

#### `midi_tool.set`

**Set MIDI Tool Parameters**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `clip-view`.

Sets one or more parameters of a MIDI Tool, by ID. The settings are one set for the whole set, saved with it, and changing them is no undo step. With the tool's Auto switch on, the change applies the tool at once (a transformation only while notes or a time selection are selected): the first change opens an application on the notes as they are, and each further change runs the tool again on the notes it started from, with the same seed. The application is one undo step named after the tool. A change that would leave the clip fewer notes asks first. Read the settings back in `midi_tool.state` and the notes in the query tool's `clip`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `values` | object | yes | The parameters to set, by ID, each in the form `midi_tool.list` gives its default. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |
| `tool` | string or null | no | The tool's ID. Left out, the chosen tool of the panel shown last. |

Result: [`MidiToolState`](#miditoolstate).

#### `midi_tool.set_auto`

**Set MIDI Tool Auto**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `clip-view`.

Switches a MIDI Tool's Auto switch. Switching it off while the tool's application is open puts the notes back as they were before it and closes the application, as one undo step; switching it on applies nothing until a parameter changes. Read it back in `midi_tool.state`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` | boolean | yes | Whether Auto is on. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |
| `tool` | string or null | no | The tool's ID. Left out, the chosen tool of the panel shown last. |

Result: [`MidiToolState`](#miditoolstate).

#### `midi_tool.state`

**MIDI Tool State**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `clip-view`.

Reports the MIDI Tools: the Clip View's right group's shown panel, the transformation and generator the clip's track shows, every tool's settings (its Auto switch, its parameters' values, whether they are all at their defaults), what a tool would act on now (the range, the time selection, the selected notes and the notes a transformation would take), and the open application with its tool, how many input notes it keeps, its range and its seed. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |

Result: [`MidiToolState`](#miditoolstate).

### Area `mixer`

#### `mixer.arm_exclusive`

**Arm Track Exclusively**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Arms one track and disarms every other track, in one undo step, as a click on an Arm switch does while Exclusive Arm is on (Live's default). Only audio and MIDI tracks can be armed.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_arm`

**Arm Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Arms or disarms one track for recording, leaving other tracks' arm switches as they are, so it records its input when recording starts (recording arrives in Phase 2; until then the switch is only saved). Only audio and MIDI tracks can be armed.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-013 | `C` | `C` | `track-headers` | Arm the selected tracks for recording | toggles `arm` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `arm` | boolean | yes | Whether it's armed. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_crossfade_assign`

**Assign Crossfade**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Assigns a track to a side of the crossfader, as its A and B buttons under the mixer's Crossfader section do: `a`, `b`, or `none` (neither, where every track starts). A track's sides are exclusive, so assigning one releases the other; a track assigned to neither plays through at every crossfader position. Every track but Main can be assigned, and Main carries the crossfader itself (`mixer.set_crossfader`). The assignment is saved with the set, and undo releases it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track; every track but Main. |
| `assign` | [`CrossfadeAssign`](#crossfadeassign) | yes | `a`, `b`, or `none`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_crossfader`

**Set Crossfader**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets the Main track's crossfader, as the Crossfader section's fader does. `position` runs from 0 (the A end) through 0.5 (the centre, where a new set starts) to 1 (the B end). Tracks assigned to A and B fade between the two ends on the default Constant Power curve: at the centre each side plays at -3 dB, at either end the near side plays at 0 dB, the far side is silent, and a track assigned to neither plays through at every position. The engine glides to the new position over 20 ms, so a move never clicks. The position is saved with the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | number from 0 to 1 | yes | The position: 0 is the A end, 0.5 the centre, 1 the B end. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_cue_mode`

**Cue Switches**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Cue mode, as the Main strip's Solo/Cue button and the Options menu's Solo Switches and Cue Switches do: with `enabled` true, every track's Solo switch becomes a Cue switch (`mixer.set_solo` sets it) that feeds the Cue Out at the Cue Volume (`mixer.set_cue_volume`) instead of silencing the other tracks, and Main plays what the activators leave. A cue-switched track is heard on the Cue Out after its devices and before its volume, pan and activator. It needs a Cue Out that shares no output channel with Main Out (`routing.set_cue_out`, `routing.set_main_out`): turning it on with an overlap is refused, and an overlap made later switches it off in effect. A new set is in Solo mode. The mode is saved with the set and is no undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether the Solo switches are Cue switches. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_cue_volume`

**Set Cue Volume**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the Preview/Cue Volume knob on Main's strip, which scales the Cue Out in Cue mode, as a linear gain from 0 (-inf dB) to 1.995 (+6 dB); 1 (0 dB) is where a new set starts. The engine glides to the new value over 20 ms. The volume is saved with the set, and each change is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `volume` | number from 0 to 1.9952623149688795 | yes | The gain: 1 is unity (0 dB, where a new set starts) and 0 silence, up to 1.995 (+6 dB). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_delay_compensation`

**Delay Compensation**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Delay Compensation, the Options menu item. On in a new set, it holds every path back so signals through high-latency devices reach the Main output aligned. While it's off, nothing is held back, no device's latency counts, and a track's Track Delay has no effect; the Track Delay and Hardware Latency controls are disabled, keeping their values. The setting is saved with the set, and each change is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether compensation is on. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_keep_monitoring_latency`

**Keep Monitoring Latency**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets a track's Keep Monitoring Latency, as its Track Options do. With monitoring In or Auto, it decides whether a monitored track keeps its delay compensation while Reduced Latency When Monitoring is on: with `enabled` true (a new track's), the track is compensated with the rest of the set; off, it is given the lowest possible latency. The setting is saved only where it's off, and each change is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether it keeps its compensation. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_mute`

**Activate/Deactivate Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Switches a track's activator: `mute` true deactivates the track, so its output and its post-fader sends are silent (its pre-fader sends still carry it), and false activates it again. Use it to silence a track without deleting it. Every track but Main has an activator.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-016 | `0` | `0` | `track-headers` | Deactivate the selected track | toggles `mute` |
| S-TRANS-010 | `F1..F8` | `F1..F8` | `global` | Turn track 1 to 8 on or off | toggles `mute` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `mute` | boolean | yes | Whether it's muted. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_pan`

**Set Track Pan**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets a track's pan from -1 (fully left) through 0 (centre) to 1 (fully right). Use it to place a track in the stereo field. Panning keeps the power constant: at the centre both channels pass at 0 dB, and fully to one side that side is 3 dB louder and the other silent.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `pan` | number from -1 to 1 | yes | The pan position, from −1 (left) through 0 (centre) to 1 (right). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_pan_mode`

**Set Split Pan Mode**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets a track's pan mode: `stereo` (the default) balances both channels with the one Pan control, and `split` gives each input channel its own control (`mixer.set_split_pan_left` and `mixer.set_split_pan_right`). Use it as the Pan control's context menu does. The mode is saved only where it isn't the default, and each change is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `mode` | [`PanMode`](#panmode) | yes | `stereo` or `split`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_reduced_latency_monitoring`

**Reduced Latency When Monitoring**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Reduced Latency When Monitoring, the Options menu item, which is available only while Delay Compensation is on; the command refuses `enabled` true while compensation is off. With it on, a track whose input is monitored (Monitor In, or Auto while armed and not playing a clip) is given the lowest possible latency: its input isn't held back with the rest of the set, so it may be out of sync with tracks such as the returns, which stay compensated. A monitored track that keeps its monitoring latency (`mixer.set_keep_monitoring_latency`) is compensated as usual. The setting is saved with the set, and each change is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether a monitored track is given the lowest possible latency. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_send`

**Set Send Level**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets how much of a track's signal its send feeds to the return track `to`, as a linear gain from 0 (-inf dB, where every send starts) to 1 (0 dB). Use it to put a track through a return's effects, such as a shared reverb. Audio, MIDI, and group tracks have a send to every return; the return's Pre/Post switch (`mixer.set_send_tap`) decides whether the send takes the track's signal before or after its pan, volume, and activator.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The sending track. |
| `to` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The return track the send feeds. |
| `level` | number from 0 to 1 | yes | The level: 1 is 0 dB, 0.5 about −6 dB, and 0 sends nothing. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_send_tap`

**Set Sends Pre/Post**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets a return track's Pre/Post switch, which decides where every send to that return takes its signal from each sending track: `post` (the default) after the track's pan, volume, and activator, so the send follows the fader; `pre` before them, straight after the track's devices, for a mix that ignores the faders, such as a monitor mix. Only return tracks have it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The return track. |
| `tap` | [`SendTap`](#sendtap) | yes | `pre` or `post`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_solo`

**Solo Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Solos or unsolos one track, leaving other tracks' solo switches as they are, as a Cmd-click (Ctrl-click) on a Solo switch does; to solo one track alone, use `mixer.solo_exclusive`. While any track is soloed, only soloed tracks, the groups that hold them, and the tracks inside soloed groups are heard. Return tracks stay audible if Solo in Place is on (`mixer.set_solo_in_place`); soloing a return silences every other track's output but keeps their sends to it. In Cue mode (`mixer.set_cue_mode`) the switch is the track's Cue switch and silences nothing. Every track but Main can be soloed.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-014 | `S` | `S` | `track-headers` | Solo the selected tracks | toggles `solo` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `solo` | boolean | yes | Whether it's soloed. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_solo_in_place`

**Solo in Place**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Solo in Place, the Options menu item. On (the default in a new set), soloing an audio, MIDI, or group track keeps the return tracks audible, so the soloed track is heard with its sends' effects; off, soloing such a track silences the returns too. It doesn't change what soloing a return does. The setting is saved with the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether soloing a track keeps the return tracks audible. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_split_pan_left`

**Set Split Pan Left**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

In Split Stereo Pan Mode, sets the left input channel's position, from -1 (fully left) through 0 (centre) to 1 (fully right). Each channel is placed on the constant-power pan law, so a control fully to one side puts that channel on that side 3 dB louder. The position is an automation and modulation target, glides over 20 ms, and is saved only where it isn't the centre; each change is one undo step. It does nothing outside split mode.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `pan` | number from -1 to 1 | yes | The position, from −1 (left) through 0 (centre) to 1 (right). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_split_pan_right`

**Set Split Pan Right**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

In Split Stereo Pan Mode, sets the right input channel's position, as `mixer.set_split_pan_left` sets the left.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `pan` | number from -1 to 1 | yes | The position, from −1 (left) through 0 (centre) to 1 (right). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_track_delay`

**Set Track Delay**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets a track's Track Delay, which shifts the track's whole output in time: positive delays the track, negative plays it early (the other paths then wait for it). `delay` names its unit, as Hardware Latency does: `{"unit": "milliseconds", "value": 10.0}` from -1000 to 1000 (kept in milliseconds when the sample rate changes) or `{"unit": "samples", "value": 480}` from -192000 to 192000 (kept in samples). The delay is saved with the set, and each change is one undo step. It is refused while Delay Compensation is off (`mixer.set_delay_compensation`), keeping its value.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `delay` | [`TrackDelay`](#trackdelay) | yes | The delay and the unit it is in. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.set_volume`

**Set Track Volume**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets a track's volume as a linear gain: 1 is unity (0 dB), 0.5 is about -6 dB (10^(dB/20) converts decibels), 2 is about +6 dB, and 0 is silence (-inf dB). Use it to balance tracks; the Main track's volume sets the song's output level. The engine glides to the new level over 20 ms, so a change never clicks. The value must be finite and at least 0.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `volume` | number, at least 0 | yes | The gain: 1 is unity (0 dB), 0.5 about −6 dB, and 0 silence. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer.solo_exclusive`

**Solo Track Exclusively**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `session`, `arrangement`.

Solos one track and unsolos every other track, in one undo step, as a click on a Solo switch does while Exclusive Solo is on (Live's default). Use it to hear one track on its own. To unsolo, use `mixer.set_solo` with `solo` false. Every track but Main can be soloed.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `mixer_view.fold_chains`

Folds a rack's chains out in the mixers as strips after the track's, as the fold button in the track's title bar does, or folds them back in. `rack` is the rack: a rack of more than one chain, on a track or inside another rack's chain. A track's fold button is for the instrument or drum rack it holds; a chain's is for the rack inside it. A rack of one chain has no chains to fold out. Switches unless `shown` says which. Changes only the view, and isn't saved with the set; the chains it shows read back in `mixer_view.state`.

### Area `modulation`

#### `modulation.state`

**Modulation State**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports the parameters a track's clips and the modulators act on (all tracks' when `track` is left out): for each, the track and the parameter (a mixer control, a send, or a device's parameter), its base (what its automation, a modulator in Remote Control or its control sets), the value it played in the last block, the clip envelopes modulating it, each with its value at the play position and what it contributes, as a share of the parameter's travel, the modulator slots mapping it (`modulators`), and the modulator that holds it in Remote Control (`held_by`). A clip envelope modulates by a share: 0 to 1 for a volume or a send, which brings its level down to that share, and −1 to 1 for the rest. It reads back `clip.set_envelope_breakpoint` and the other clip envelope commands, and `modulator.map`. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track, or every track when left out. |

Result: [`ModulationState`](#modulationstate).

### Area `modulator`

#### `modulator.arm_map`

**Map**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Lights or puts out a modulator slot's Map button, as clicking it does. While one is lit, every parameter in the set that can be mapped is tinted, and clicking one maps it to the slot (`modulator.map`); Esc, or the button again (`armed`: false), puts it out and changes nothing. Lighting a button puts out the one that was lit. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and `device_view.state` reports the lit button in `armed_map`. Only a modulator has slots.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `slot` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The slot, from 0 to 7. |
| `armed` | boolean or null | no | Arm (true) or disarm (false); switches if left out. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The modulator; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `modulator.map`

**Map Modulator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Maps one of a modulator's slots (`slot`, 0 to 7; the Expression Control's are 0 to 4) to a parameter, as the slot's Map button and a click on the parameter's control do. `target` is a mixer control (`volume`, `pan` or `mute`) or a send of any track, or a parameter of any device on any track, but not a parameter of the modulator itself. The slot's earlier mapping is replaced; one modulator doesn't map one parameter twice. A modulator in Remote Control can't map a parameter another modulator in Remote Control holds. A modulator driven by audio, notes or MIDI (the Envelope Follower, Envelope MIDI, Shaper MIDI and Expression Control) doesn't map another modulator's parameters, nor one on a track that feeds its own track, which would make the two tracks wait on each other. The mapping is saved with the set, goes with its target when that is deleted, and shows in the `mappings` field of the query tool's `device`. One undo step (Map Modulator).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The modulator device. |
| `slot` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The slot, from 0 to 7. |
| `target` | [`ModTarget`](#modtarget) | yes | The parameter to map: a mixer control or send of any track, or a parameter of any device but the modulator's own. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `modulator.set_shape`

**Edit Shape**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces the breakpoint shape of a Shaper or a Shaper MIDI, as every edit of its display does (adding, moving, bending or deleting a breakpoint, making one the sustain breakpoint, Clear and the six presets). `points` lists up to 64 breakpoints in order along the cycle, each with `x` (its place, 0 to 1), `y` (the output there, 0 to 1), `bend` (of the segment starting there, from -1 to 1, 0 straight) and `sustain` (true on the Shaper MIDI's sustain breakpoint, at most one in a shape). An empty list outputs 0. One undo step (Edit Shape).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The Shaper device. |
| `points` | array of [`ShapePoint`](#shapepoint) | yes | The breakpoints, in order along the cycle (at most 64), each with its place and output from 0 to 1 and the bend of the segment starting there, from −1 to 1. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `modulator.unmap`

**Unmap Modulator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Removes the mapping of a modulator's slot (`slot`, 0 to 7; the Expression Control's are 0 to 4), as its Unmap button does: the parameter plays its own value again from the next frame. A slot with no mapping stays as it is. One undo step (Unmap Modulator).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The modulator device. |
| `slot` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The slot, from 0 to 7. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `note`

#### `note.add`

**Add Note**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Adds a note to a MIDI clip: pitch `key` (0 to 127; 60 is middle C), starting `start` ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents, lasting `length` ticks, with `velocity` (1 to 127; 100 unless given). With Draw Mode on, clicking the note area runs this for a note one grid step long. The new note is selected afterwards, and the edit is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pitch, a MIDI key from 0 to 127; 60 is middle C. |
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the note starts, in ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents. Never negative. |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How long the note lasts, in ticks. Always positive. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `velocity` | integer or null | no | The velocity, from 1 to 127; 100 unless given. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.adjust_value`

**Adjust Note Values**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Changes one value of notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) by `by`, as the value keys and dragging a marker in an expression lane do: `field` is `velocity` or `release_velocity` (whole numbers, 1 to 127), `chance` (0 to 1; 0.1 is 10 %), or `velocity_deviation` (whole numbers, held to the room each note's velocity leaves: at most 127 less its velocity and at least 1 less). Each note is held within its range, so a change past an end brings it to that end, and a call that changes no note records no undo step. The edited notes stay selected, and the whole drag is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | [`NoteField`](#notefield) | yes | Which value to change. |
| `by` | number | yes | How much to add to each note's value; negative lowers it. Whole numbers for the whole-number fields; for `chance`, a fraction (0.1 is 10 %). |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips, each with its notes, in place of `clip` and `notes` (Spec: multi-clip-editing R18). Left out with `clip` and `notes`, the selected notes of every clip shown, or of the active clip alone in Focus Mode. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.chop`

**Chop Note(s) on Grid**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-selection`.

Chops notes (`notes`, or the selected notes), as Cmd-E (Ctrl-E) with notes selected does: each is cut at every line of `grid` (ticks apart; the editing grid if left out) that falls strictly inside it, or with `parts`, into that many equal parts, from 1 to 64. `steps` then change each note's number of parts, one part more or fewer or the next or previous power of two, as Cmd with Up and Down does while Cmd is held; the number stays from 1 to 64, and a note keeps parts of at least a tick. The parts keep what Split keeps, and stay selected. The edit is one undo step, `Chop Notes`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `grid` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | Cut at every line of a grid this many ticks apart. Left out (and without `parts`), the editing grid. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order. Left out, the selected notes. |
| `parts` | integer or null | no | Instead of the grid: cut every note into this many equal parts, from 1 to 64. |
| `steps` | array of [`ChopStep`](#chopstep) | no | Changes to make to each note's parts after the first cut, in order, as Cmd with Up and Down does. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.copy`

**Copy Notes**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Copies notes (`notes`, or the selected notes, or with none selected the notes that start inside the time selection) to the note clipboard, keeping their pitches, values and their places in time from the earliest of them. The note clipboard is apart from the Arrangement's clip clipboard. Copy changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-002 | `Cmd+C` | `Ctrl+C` | `global` | Copy | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips, each with its notes, in place of `clip` and `notes` (Spec: multi-clip-editing R18). Left out with `clip` and `notes`, the selected notes of every clip shown, or of the active clip alone in Focus Mode. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes, or with none selected the notes that start inside the time selection. |

Result: [`NoteClipboardState`](#noteclipboardstate).

#### `note.cut`

**Cut Notes**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Copies notes to the note clipboard, as `note.copy` does, then deletes them, as `note.delete` does. Cmd-X (Ctrl-X) runs this on the selected notes, or with none selected the notes in the time selection. Because it removes the person's work, an agent asks first.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-001 | `Cmd+X` | `Ctrl+X` | `global` | Cut | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

**Deactivate Note(s)**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Deactivates notes (`notes`, or the selected notes), as 0 does: a deactivated note keeps its place and values, is drawn grey and never plays. With `active` left out the notes are deactivated, or activated again when every one of them is deactivated already (the menu item then reads Activate Note(s)); `active` `true` or `false` sets them. The edit is one undo step, and the notes stay selected.

#### `note.group`

**Group Notes**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Puts notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) in a new probability group of `kind`: `play_all` plays all of its notes or none, `play_one` plays one of them, chosen evenly. Left out, `kind` is the one made last in this session, `play_all` until one is chosen. Notes leave the group they were in, a group left with fewer than two notes ends, and the new group's chance is that of its first note in the clip's order, which every note of it takes. Naming every note of one group changes its kind. Refused with fewer than two notes. One undo step, named Group Notes, or Change Group when it changes one group's kind; the notes stay selected. Read the groups back from the clip's `data.midi.groups` and each note's `group`.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-031 | `Cmd+G` | `Ctrl+G` | `note-selection` | Group the selected notes (play all) | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `kind` | [`GroupKind`](#groupkind) or null | no | How the group plays. Left out, the kind made last in this session, `play_all` until one is chosen. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.join`

**Join Notes**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Joins notes (`notes`, or the selected notes), as Cmd-J (Ctrl-J) does: the notes of each pitch that has two or more become one note from the earliest start among them to the latest end, with the values of the earliest of them. Every joined note's pressure points stay at their places in time, and where two overlap the later note's win. A pitch with one note is left alone, and the command is refused when there is nothing to join. The joined notes are selected afterwards. The edit is one undo step, `Join Notes`.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-007 | `Cmd+J` | `Ctrl+J` | `note-editor` | Join the selected notes | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order. Left out, the selected notes. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.move`

**Move Notes**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Moves notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) in time by `by` ticks and in pitch by `semitones`, as dragging them in the note editor does; dragging right and left runs it with `semitones` 0, and up and down snap the pitch. Nothing moves if any note would start before the clip's contents or leave the range of MIDI keys 0 to 127. With `copy` the notes are copied where they would have gone and the originals stay, as Option-dragging a note does. The moved notes stay selected, and the whole drag is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `by` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | How far to move them in time, in ticks; negative is earlier. Give `by` or `semitones`, or both. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips, each with its notes, in place of `clip` and `notes` (Spec: multi-clip-editing R18). Left out with `clip` and `notes`, the selected notes of every clip shown, or of the active clip alone in Focus Mode. |
| `copy` | boolean or null | no | Copy them instead of moving them, as Option-dragging a note does: the copies land where the notes would have gone and the originals stay. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |
| `semitones` | integer or null | no | How far to move them in pitch, in semitones; negative is lower. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

Puts the note clipboard's notes into the clip at `at`, in ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents, or at the insert marker, or at the time selection's start, with their pitches, values and spacing, and selects them. It fails, changing nothing, if there is nothing on the clipboard. Cmd-V (Ctrl-V) runs this.

| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |

#### `note.preview`

**Preview Note**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `clip-view`, `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Plays a note on the track of a MIDI clip (`clip`, or the one the Clip View shows), through its devices and mixer, whether or not the song plays and whether or not the track is armed or monitoring: `on` presses it (`velocity`, 100 unless given) and a later call with `on` false releases it. A press with no release plays until the release, so an agent that presses must release. Needs the Preview switch on. It changes nothing in the set and is never an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pitch, a MIDI key from 0 to 127; 60 is middle C. |
| `on` | boolean | yes | Press (true) or release (false) the note. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip whose track plays the note. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |
| `velocity` | integer or null | no | The velocity, from 1 to 127; 100 unless given. Used when `on`. |

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `note.quantize`

**Quantize**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Quantises notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) to `grid`: each note moves `amount` percent of the way from its start (or its end, with `target` `note_end`) to the nearest grid line, so 100 percent lands it on the line and 50 percent halves its distance to it. The lines are laid out from each bar's start, as the note editor's grid is, and a spacing of whole bars counts bars from 1.1.1. `grid`, `target`, and `amount` left out use the Clip View's Quantize settings (`clip_view.quantize_settings`), which follow the note editor's editing grid until a grid is set. Quantising is one undo step, and the quantised notes stay selected.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-011 | `Cmd+U` | `Ctrl+U` | `note-editor` | Quantise the selected notes | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | integer or null | no | How far each note moves toward its grid line, from 0 to 100 percent. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips, each with its notes, in place of `clip` and `notes` (Spec: multi-clip-editing R18). Left out with `clip` and `notes`, the selected notes of every clip shown, or of the active clip alone in Focus Mode. |
| `grid` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The grid line spacing in ticks, over the Quantize settings. Lines are laid out from each bar's start, as the editing grid's are; a spacing of whole bars counts bars from 1.1.1. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |
| `target` | [`QuantizeTarget`](#quantizetarget) or null | no | What to move toward the grid. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.ramp_value`

**Ramp Note Values**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Sets one value of notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) as a ramp, as the footer's Ramp Start and Ramp End do: the first note by start takes `from`, the last takes `to`, and those between take values on a straight line between them by their start times, notes that start together taking the same value (whole numbers for the whole-number fields). `field` takes the same fields and ranges as `note.set_value`; nothing changes if `from` or `to` is out of range. One note takes `from`, and so do notes that all start together. The edited notes stay selected, and the whole edit is one undo step.

Default keys: none.
