| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | [`NoteField`](#notefield) | yes | Which value to ramp. |
| `from` | number | yes | The value the first note takes. |
| `to` | number | yes | The value the last note takes. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips, each with its notes, in place of `clip` and `notes` (Spec: multi-clip-editing R18). Left out with `clip` and `notes`, the selected notes of every clip shown, or of the active clip alone in Focus Mode. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.randomize`

**Randomize Note Values**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Moves one value of notes (`notes`, or the selected notes, or with none selected every note in the clip's span) at random, as the footer's Randomize does: each note takes a value drawn evenly from its value less `amount` to its value plus `amount`, held within the field's range and whole for the velocities. `field` is `velocity`, `release_velocity` or `chance`; `amount` is in the field's own units, 0 to 127 or 0 to 1 for `chance`. The same `seed` with the same notes gives the same values, each note keeping its own draw so a larger `amount` moves it further the same way; left out, each call draws afresh. An `amount` of 0 changes nothing. The edit is one undo step, and the notes stay selected.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | [`NoteField`](#notefield) | yes | Which value to randomise: `velocity`, `release_velocity` or `chance`. |
| `amount` | number | yes | How far from its value each note may move, in the field's own units: 0 to 127 for the velocities, 0 to 1 for `chance` (0.25 is 25 %). |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips, each with its notes, in place of `clip` and `notes` (Spec: multi-clip-editing R18). Left out with `clip` and `notes`, the selected notes of every clip shown, or of the active clip alone in Focus Mode. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes, or with none selected every note in the clip's span. |
| `seed` | integer or null | no | Seeds the draw: the same seed with the same notes gives the same values. Left out, each call draws afresh. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.resize`

**Resize Notes**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Moves notes' ends (`notes`, or the selected notes) by `by` ticks, as dragging a note's end in the note editor does: a positive `by` makes them longer, a negative one shorter, and every note keeps at least one tick of length. A note's start doesn't move. The resized notes stay selected, and the whole drag is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `by` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How far each note's end moves, in ticks; negative is shorter. A note keeps at least one tick of length. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips, each with its notes, in place of `clip` and `notes` (Spec: multi-clip-editing R18). Left out with `clip` and `notes`, the selected notes of every clip shown, or of the active clip alone in Focus Mode. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.set_expression`

**Set Note Expression**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Replaces one expression envelope of notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) with `breakpoints`, as editing the Clip View's MPE tab does: `envelope` is `pitch` (the note's own pitch bend in semitones from its key, -48 to 48), `slide` (0 to 127) or `pressure` (0 to 127). Each breakpoint is an `at` in ticks counted from the note's start, from 0 to the note's length, a `value` in the envelope's range, and a `bend` from -1 to 1 for the segment starting there (0 is straight); they go in order of `at`, none twice. An empty list clears the envelope. Nothing changes if a value, a position or a bend is out of range, two breakpoints share a position, or the clip isn't a MIDI clip. One undo step, Set Note Expression; the notes stay selected. The clip query's notes read each envelope back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `envelope` | [`Expression`](#expression) | yes | Which envelope to replace: `pitch` (semitones from the note's key, −48 to 48), `slide` or `pressure` (0 to 127). |
| `breakpoints` | array of [`Breakpoint`](#breakpoint) | yes | The breakpoints every one of the notes gets, each at a position in ticks counted from the note's start (0 to its length, in order, none twice), with a value in the envelope's range and an optional `bend` from −1 to 1 for the segment starting there. An empty list clears the envelope. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.set_value`

**Set Note Value**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Sets one value of notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) to `value`, or to each note's own entry of `values` (one for each note, in the order named), as typing a value or drawing across an expression lane does: `field` is `velocity` (whole numbers 1 to 127), `release_velocity` (whole numbers 1 to 127), `chance` (0 to 1), or `velocity_deviation` (whole numbers -127 to 127). Nothing changes if `value` is outside the field's range. A velocity deviation is held within the room each note's velocity leaves: at most 127 less its velocity and at least 1 less. The edited notes stay selected, and the whole drag is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field` | [`NoteField`](#notefield) | yes | Which value to set. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips, each with its notes, in place of `clip` and `notes` (Spec: multi-clip-editing R18). Left out with `clip` and `notes`, the selected notes of every clip shown, or of the active clip alone in Focus Mode. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. |
| `value` | number or null | no | The value, within the field's range, for every one of the notes. Give this or `values`. |
| `values` | array or null | no | One value for each of the notes, in the order they're named, each within the field's range: what drawing across a lane gives. Give this or `value`. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.split`

**Split Note(s)**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`.

Splits notes at ticks, as holding E and clicking a note, or Cmd-E (Ctrl-E) with no notes selected, does. `notes` (or the selected notes, or with none selected every note) are each split at every tick of `at` (or of the time selection's start and end, or the insert marker) that falls strictly inside them; `cuts` instead names a tick for each note. A note split becomes parts that together cover it: the first keeps its start, the last its end, each keeps the note's pitch, velocity, release velocity, chance, deviation and deactivation, and its pressure points go with the part they fall in. A tick at or outside a note's start or end splits nothing, and when no note splits nothing changes and no undo step is recorded. The parts of the notes that were selected stay selected. The edit is one undo step, `Split Notes`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | array or null | no | The ticks to split them at, from the beginning of the clip's contents. Left out, the time selection's start and end, or the insert marker. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `cuts` | array or null | no | Instead of `notes` and `at`: each note with its own tick, as dragging E across several notes splits each where the drag crosses it. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes to split, by their place in the clip's notes in order. Left out, the selected notes, or with none selected every note. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.split_clip`

**Split Clip**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Splits the Arrangement clip the Clip View shows at the start and end of the editor's time selection, each that falls strictly inside the clip, as `arrangement.split` does, and selects the part inside. Cmd-Shift-E (Ctrl-Shift-E) runs it. Refused for a Session clip, or with no time selection.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-036 | `Cmd+Shift+E` | `Ctrl+Shift+E` | `note-editor` | Split an Arrangement clip at the time selection | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`EditResult`](#editresult).

#### `note.step_record`

**Step Record**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Step-records at the insert marker of a MIDI clip while its track is armed, Preview is on and the transport is stopped. Forward (Right): each held key (`held`, or the keys held on the track's MIDI input) is added at the insert marker, one grid step long at its velocity, and the marker moves one step on; held keys that this stepping just added are made one step longer instead, and a key let go is left as it is. Back (`back`, Left): the held notes just added are made one step shorter, a note left with no length is removed, and the marker moves one step back. With nothing held, the marker moves a step and leaves a rest. No record quantisation applies. One undo step, `Step Record`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `back` | boolean | no | Step back, as Left does, instead of forward, as Right does. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows. |
| `held` | array or null | no | The keys held, each with its velocity. Left out, the keys held on the track's MIDI input now; an empty list means no key is held. |

Result: [`StepRecordResult`](#steprecordresult).

#### `note.stretch`

**Stretch Notes**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Scales notes in time from the range `from` (or the time selection) to the range `to`, as dragging a note stretch marker does: `from`'s start goes to `to`'s start and its end to `to`'s end, and each note's start and end keep their place in proportion, so starts and lengths scale together. The notes are `notes`, or the selected notes, or with none selected those that start inside `from`. With `point`, what lies between the start and the point is scaled to end at the point's new place, and what lies between the point and the end to start there, as dragging the pseudo marker does. A `to` that ends before it starts mirrors the notes' order in time. A note's pressure points scale with it, and the breakpoints of the clip's linked envelopes inside `from` move by the same mapping, replacing any breakpoint they land on; unlinked envelopes stay. Refused, changing nothing, if a note would be shorter than a tick or start before the clip's contents. The time selection becomes `to`. The edit is one undo step, `Stretch Notes`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | [`TickRange`](#tickrange) | yes | The range it becomes: its start is where `from`'s start goes, and its end where `from`'s end goes. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `from` | [`TickRange`](#tickrange) or null | no | The range being stretched. Left out, the time selection. |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order. Left out, the selected notes, or with none selected the notes that start inside `from`. |
| `point` | [`StretchPoint`](#stretchpoint) or null | no | A point inside `from` that goes somewhere else: what lies on either side of it is scaled to meet it there. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

#### `note.ungroup`

**Ungroup Notes**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `note-editor`, `note-selection`.

Takes notes (`notes`, or the selected notes) out of their probability groups, each keeping its group's chance as its own; a group left with fewer than two notes ends, and naming every note of a group ends it. One undo step, named Ungroup Notes; the notes stay selected. Read the groups back from the clip's `data.midi.groups` and each note's `group`.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-032 | `Cmd+Shift+G` | `Ctrl+Shift+G` | `note-selection` | Ungroup the selected notes | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `notes` | array or null | no | The notes, by their place in the clip's notes in order (by start, then pitch). Left out, the selected notes. Naming every note of a group ends it. |

Result: [`NoteEditResult`](#noteeditresult).

### Area `pad`

#### `pad.delete`

**Delete Pad**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Deletes the chains on a pad, with their devices and automation: one undo step (Delete Chain). Undo restores them, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note, 0 to 127. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.drop`

**Drop on Pad**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Drops what the browser drags onto a pad. One audio file in `samples` on an empty pad makes a chain on its note holding the sampler with the file loaded (or a chain made from the pad default that Save as Default Pad saved), named after the file; on a pad with a chain it replaces the chain's sampler and sample and keeps its effects. Several files go one to a pad, rising a note each from `note` (those past note 127 are left out), or with `layer` onto that one pad as an instrument rack with a chain per file. A `device` or `preset` goes at the end of the pad's chain if it is an audio effect, at the end of its MIDI effects if it is a MIDI effect, and in place of its instrument if it is an instrument; on an empty pad each makes a chain holding it. A pad of several chains takes no drop. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note; with several samples, the first of the pads they rise from. |
| `device` | [`NewDevice`](#newdevice) or null | no | A device to drop, as `device.add` describes one. |
| `layer` | boolean | no | With several samples, layer them on this one pad (Cmd, or Alt on Windows and Linux) rather than spread them over pads. |
| `move_device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | A device to move onto the pad from where it is. |
| `preset` | string or null | no | A preset file to drop. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |
| `samples` | array of string | no | Audio files: one goes on the pad, several on pads rising from it. |

Result: [`PadDropped`](#paddropped).

#### `pad.hot_swap`

**Hot-Swap Pad**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Makes a pad the target of hot-swap, as its Hot-Swap button does, or ends it: loading an item from the browser then lands on the pad as dropping it would (`pad.drop`). It ends the hot-swap of a device or a chain. Only a pad of one chain, or an empty one, can be the target. It changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Start (true) or end (false) hot-swapping the pad; switches if left out. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.hot_swap_sample`

**Hot-Swap Sample**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

A pad's Hot-Swap Sample button: it makes the pad the hot-swap target and opens the folder of the sample its chain plays in the browser, so loading a sample replaces the pad's (one undo step each). Pressing it again, the hot-swap bar's close button, Esc, Q, or going from the browser to another view ends it. Only a pad whose chain plays a sample has one.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Start (true) or end (false) hot-swapping the pad; switches if left out. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.preview`

**Preview Pad**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Holds a pad's Preview button, or lets it go: while it is held each of the pad's chains plays its Receive note into itself alone at velocity 100 (C3 for a chain on All Notes), through the rest of the track's chain and its mixer, whether or not the song plays. A press with no release plays until the release, so an agent that presses must release. It changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note. |
| `on` | boolean | yes | Press (true) or release (false) the Preview button. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.rename`

**Rename Pad**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Renames the chain of a pad that holds one chain: an empty name gives it the name a chain has without one. A pad of several chains can't be renamed. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note. |
| `name` | string | yes | The new name; empty gives the name a chain has without one. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.save_default`

**Save as Default Pad**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Saves the pad's chain as the default pad: a sample dropped on an empty pad afterwards makes its chain from that default, with the sample in the first sampler. The one saved last is used. A pad of one chain only. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note, 0 to 127. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.select`

**Select Pad**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Selects a pad, as clicking it does, and its chains in the chain list, so the devices view shows them. The selected pad is the one D switches hot-swap to. It changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note, 0 to 127. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.set_mute`

**Mute Pad**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Mutes a pad, or unmutes it: it switches off the Chain Activator of each of the pad's chains (a pad of several chains mutes them all, and a mixed pad mutes the rest). One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Turn it on (true) or off (false); switches if left out, a mixed pad turning on. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.set_solo`

**Solo Pad**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Solos a pad, or unsolos it: it sets the Solo of each of the pad's chains, and leaves every other chain's as it is. While any drum chain is soloed the rack's return chains stay audible carrying only the soloed chains' sends. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad's note. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Turn it on (true) or off (false); switches if left out, a mixed pad turning on. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `pad.swap`

**Swap Pads**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Drags one pad onto another: each pad's chains take the other pad's note as their Receive, so the set's clips play the other sound. With `layer` (Cmd, or Alt on Windows and Linux) both pads' chains are layered on `to` as one chain holding an instrument rack of them, and `from` is left empty. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad dragged. |
| `to` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The pad it's dropped on. |
| `layer` | boolean | no | Layer both pads' chains on `to` instead (Cmd, or Alt on Windows and Linux). |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

### Area `perception`

#### `perception.analyze`

**Analyze Audio**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Measures audio and reports numbers with units: loudness (integrated, momentary and short-term LUFS, loudness range in LU, true peak in dBTP, as ITU-R BS.1770-4 and EBU R 128 define them), sample peak and RMS in dBFS, the level in each octave band from 31.5 Hz to 16 kHz, the tempo in BPM, the key, and when transients start. Give `preview` to measure a preview, or a range (`start`, `length`, and `track`, as for `perception.preview`) to render one for the analysis, up to ten minutes. `measure` picks what to measure; left out, everything. Tempo and key are estimates from the audio, not the set's settings. A range renders as `perception.preview` does, refused likewise while the transport plays a set with a CLAP plug-in. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | How long the range is, in ticks (705,600 to the quarter note, so a 4/4 bar is 2,822,400). Left out, to the end of the time selection, or without one to the end of the set's last clip. |
| `measure` | array or null | no | What to measure. Left out, everything. |
| `preview` | integer or null | no | A preview to analyse, by the ID `perception.preview` gave. Left out, the range below is rendered for the analysis (up to ten minutes). |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Without `preview`: where the range starts, as ticks from 1.1.1 or bar.beat.sixteenth text such as `"9.1.1"`. Left out, the start of the Arrangement's time selection, or 1.1.1 without one. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | One track to hear on its own, as it sounds soloed: through its group tracks and the Main track, with the returns its sends reach while Solo in Place is on. Left out, the whole mix: the Main output. |

Result: [`AnalyzeResult`](#analyzeresult).

#### `perception.capture_view`

**Capture View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Captures one of the app's views as a PNG image, as the person sees it, for a model that reads images: the whole `window`, the `arrangement` or `session` view, the `mixer`, the `browser`, the `detail` area (Clip or Device View), or the `settings` window. The view must be on screen. The image is scaled to fit `max_size` pixels. Only the agent API's `capture_view` tool returns the image, and only while the app's window is open: headless (`bl-cli mcp`) there's no window to capture. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | [`View`](#view) | yes | The view to capture. It must be on screen: the main window shows the Arrangement or the Session View, and the browser, the mixer, and the Settings window only while they're open. |
| `max_size` | integer or null | no | The longest side of the image, in pixels, from 256 to 4,096: a larger capture is scaled down to fit. Left out, 1,568. |

Result: [`CaptureResult`](#captureresult).

#### `perception.preview`

**Preview Audio**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Renders a short audio preview of a range of the set, offline, through the engine that exports, and keeps it as a WAV file for you to listen to: the agent API's `preview` tool returns it as audio, and `uri` reads it as a resource. The range is `start` and `length` if given, otherwise the Arrangement's time selection, otherwise the whole set; it plays straight through, without the loop, and is cut to its first 30 seconds. `track` previews one track as it sounds soloed; left out, the whole mix. 16-bit stereo at 48 kHz is about 190 KB a second: a lower `sample_rate` makes it smaller. Plug-in devices render through the plug-ins the engine plays, lent to the render, so while the transport plays a set with a CLAP plug-in the preview is refused (run `transport.stop` first); otherwise rendering doesn't stop or disturb playback. The last 4 previews are kept, for `perception.analyze`. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bit_depth` | one of `16`, `24`, `32` | no | Bits per sample: 16 (the default, with triangular dither), 24, or 32 (floating point). |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | How long the range is, in ticks (705,600 to the quarter note, so a 4/4 bar is 2,822,400). Left out, to the end of the time selection, or without one to the end of the set's last clip. |
| `sample_rate` | integer or null | no | The preview's sample rate in hertz, from 8,000 to 192,000. Left out, the engine's rate. A lower rate makes a smaller file. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the range starts: ticks from 1.1.1, or bar.beat.sixteenth text such as `"9.1.1"`. Left out, the start of the Arrangement's time selection, or 1.1.1 without one. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | One track to hear on its own, as it sounds soloed: through its group tracks and the Main track, with the returns its sends reach while Solo in Place is on. Left out, the whole mix: the Main output. |

Result: [`PreviewResult`](#previewresult).

### Area `plugin`

#### `plugin.configure`

**Configure Plug-In**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Opens or closes a plug-in device's Plug-In Configure Mode (manual 24.1.2): while it is on, a parameter moved in the plug-in's own window joins the device's list of configured parameters, the ones its panel knobs and the automation and clip-envelope choosers show. `on` sets it, or switches it if left out. Configure mode itself is view state: it isn't an undo step and isn't saved with the set (the list is). Returns the Device View's state.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Turn configure mode on (true) or off (false); switches if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `plugin.configure_param`

**Configure Plug-In Parameter**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Adds one of a plug-in's parameters to the device's list of configured parameters, the ones its panel knobs and the automation and clip-envelope choosers show (manual 24.1.2). `index` places it in the list, or the end if left out; one already in the list moves there. One undo step, and the list is saved with the set. Returns `device.parameters`, each marked configured or not.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `param` | [`ParamId`](#paramid) | yes | The parameter to add. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where it goes in the list; at the end if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceParameters`](#deviceparameters).

#### `plugin.export_list`

**Export the Set's Plug-In List**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Writes the set's plug-in list to a text file, as the list's Export… button does: the set's name and the date, a header line, and one line per plug-in with its name, format, vendor, version, preset names, tracks, and `Missing` where this computer doesn't have it, separated by tabs. `path` is the file to write it to; left out, the app asks where to save it. The file is written outside the set, so an agent asks first. Returns the file written.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string or null | no | The file to write the list to. Left out, the app asks where to save it, as the list's Export… button does. |

Result: [`ExportedList`](#exportedlist).

#### `plugin.info`

**Plug-In Info**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Reports what a plug-in device's plug-in is doing: its ID and file, whether it's running, the latency it reports in frames, what went wrong if anything, whether its editor window can open, is open, and is shown (a hidden window stays open), and its parameters' values as it reports them. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`PluginInfo`](#plugininfo).

#### `plugin.list`

**List Plug-Ins in the Set**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Lists every plug-in the set uses, grouped by plug-in: its format, its identifier, name, the file the set says it came from, its vendor and version when the scanner knows them, the devices and tracks that use it, the preset names its devices hold, and whether this machine has it (missing when the scanner hasn't seen it, or says why it is blocklisted). Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SetPluginList`](#setpluginlist).

#### `plugin.load`

**Load Plug-In**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `device-view`.

Loads a plug-in from its file or bundle (`path`: a `.clap` file, or a `.vst3` bundle or module) and adds it as a device, as `device.add` adds one: to the selected track (or `track`), at `index` or where its role goes, selected, one undo step (Insert Device). `plugin` picks one of the file's plug-ins by its ID (CLAP's, or a VST3 class ID); the first if left out. Its parameters become the device's, which `device.parameters` lists and `device.set_param` and automation change. The plug-in's code runs inside Beatlayer, so load only plug-ins you trust. The scanner (`plugin.scan`) lists the plug-ins on this machine; this command still loads one by its path.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The plug-in's file or bundle (`.clap`, or `.vst3` for VST3). |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where it goes in the chain; as `device.add` places it if left out. |
| `plugin` | string or null | no | Which of the file's plug-ins, by its ID; the first if left out. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track; the selected track if left out. |

Result: [`PluginLoaded`](#pluginloaded).

#### `plugin.load_au`

**Load Audio Unit**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `device-view`.

Loads the Audio Unit with the given component description — its `type`, `subtype`, and `manufacturer`, four characters each, such as Apple's `aufx`, `dely`, `appl` for AUDelay — and adds it as a device, as `device.add` adds one: to the selected track (or `track`), at `index` or where its role goes, selected, one undo step (Insert Device). Its parameters become the device's, which `device.parameters` lists and `device.set_param` and automation change; its own state is saved with the set. Audio Units are macOS only: on Windows and Linux this fails with that reason. Its own editor window opens from `plugin.show_window`, as a CLAP plug-in's does, and a change made in it is one undo step. The unit's code runs inside Beatlayer, so load only units you trust.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | yes | The component's type, four characters: `aufx` for an effect, `aumu` or `augn` for an instrument, `aumi` for a MIDI effect. |
| `subtype` | string | yes | The component's subtype, four characters, such as `dely` for Apple's AUDelay. |
| `manufacturer` | string | yes | The component's manufacturer, four characters, such as `appl` for Apple's units. |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where it goes in the chain; as `device.add` places it if left out. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track; the selected track if left out. |

Result: [`PluginLoaded`](#pluginloaded).

#### `plugin.move_configured_param`

**Move Plug-In Parameter**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Moves one entry of a plug-in device's configured list from `from` to `to` (manual 24.1.2), the order its panel knobs and the choosers show. One undo step. Returns `device.parameters`, each marked configured or not.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where the parameter is now, 0 for the first. |
| `to` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes, 0 for the first. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceParameters`](#deviceparameters).

#### `plugin.rescan`

**Rescan Plug-Ins**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `device-view`.

Scans the plug-ins in `paths` (or each format's system plug-in folders) again, ignoring the cache and clearing the blocklist for them, as the Rescan button does. Returns `plugin.scan`'s report; with `background`, returns at once and the browser lists what was found when the scan is done.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `background` | boolean | no | Scan the system folders in the background and return at once, with an empty report, as the Settings window's Rescan button does; the browser lists what was found when it's done. |
| `paths` | array or null | no | The files or folders to scan; each format's system plug-in folders if left out. |

Result: [`PluginScan`](#pluginscan).

#### `plugin.scan`

**Scan Plug-Ins**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `device-view`.

Finds the plug-ins installed on this machine and describes each one: its format, its file, its identifier, name, vendor, version, and role in a chain. Scans the files or folders in `paths` for every hosted format, or, when `paths` is left out, the system plug-in folders of CLAP and of the formats the Plug-Ins settings switch on (`plugin.settings`: `vst3_system_folders`, and on macOS `use_audio_units_v2`). The app also runs this at start, in the background, and when one of those switches turns on. Each one is loaded in a separate process with a timeout, so a plug-in that crashes or hangs is put on a blocklist with the reason instead of taking Beatlayer down; a file whose size and modification time are unchanged is answered from the cache. Reads plug-in files outside the project, so an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `background` | boolean | no | Scan the system folders in the background and return at once, with an empty report, as the Settings window's Rescan button does; the browser lists what was found when it's done. |
| `paths` | array or null | no | The files or folders to scan; each format's system plug-in folders if left out. |

Result: [`PluginScan`](#pluginscan).

#### `plugin.set_panel_param`

**Set Plug-In Panel Parameter**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets which of a plug-in device's own parameters a panel knob shows (D19): `index` is the knob, 0 for the first and up to seven, and `param` the parameter, or null to restore the knob to the plug-in's parameter at that place. The mapping is remembered per plug-in, so another device of the same plug-in keeps it, and it changes only the view: it isn't an undo step. Returns the Device View's state.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The knob, 0 for the first (leftmost) and up to [`PANEL_KNOBS`] − 1. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `param` | [`ParamId`](#paramid) or null | no | The parameter it shows, from the plug-in's own; `null` restores the knob to the plug-in's parameter at that place. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `plugin.set_window`

**Set Plug-In Window Place**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Records where a plug-in device's editor window sits and how big it is, in points (`frame`): its place is saved with the set beside the document, so moving or resizing a window is never an undo step. A plug-in window reopens where it was left. Returns `plugin.info`'s report.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frame` | [`WindowFrame`](#windowframe) | yes | Where its window sits and how big it is, in points. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |

Result: [`PluginInfo`](#plugininfo).

#### `plugin.settings`

**Plug-In Settings**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Reads or changes how the browser shows plug-ins (IMP-07): `hidden` is the plug-ins to hide, as `format/plugin_id` keys; `show_hidden` whether hidden plug-ins still show; and `format_preference` the format to prefer when a plug-in exists in several. Also the Plug-In Sources switches of Settings ▸ Plug-Ins: `use_audio_units_v2`, `use_audio_units_v3` and `vst3_system_folders`, all off in a new install; the browser lists a format's plug-ins only while its switch is on (CLAP has none and is always listed), and turning one on scans that format in the background. Fields left out are unchanged. Returns the settings. A set that uses a hidden plug-in still loads it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format_preference` | [`PluginFormat`](#pluginformat) or null | no | The format to prefer when a plug-in exists in several. |
| `hidden` | array or null | no | The hidden plug-ins to remember, as `format/plugin_id` keys (IMP-07); empty hides none. |
| `show_hidden` | boolean or null | no | Whether the browser shows hidden plug-ins. |
| `use_audio_units_v2` | boolean or null | no | Use Audio Units v2 (Settings ▸ Plug-Ins): scan and list Audio Units on macOS. Turning it on scans them. |
| `use_audio_units_v3` | boolean or null | no | Use Audio Units v3 (Settings ▸ Plug-Ins). Kept; app-extension Audio Units aren't scanned yet. |
| `vst3_system_folders` | boolean or null | no | Use VST3 Plug-In System Folders (Settings ▸ Plug-Ins): scan and list the VST3 plug-ins in the format's system folders. Turning it on scans them. |

Result: [`PluginSettings`](#pluginsettings).

#### `plugin.show_window`

**Show Plug-In Window**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Opens or closes a plug-in device's editor, as the device's title bar button does; switches unless `shown` says which. On Windows and Linux the editor opens in a window Beatlayer owns, with the plug-in's own view embedded into it; on macOS, and for a plug-in that won't embed, in a floating window of the plug-in's own. An open window follows View ▸ Plug-In Windows and Auto-Hide Plug-In Windows, which hide and show it without closing it. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step. Returns `plugin.info`'s report.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `shown` | boolean or null | no | Open (true) or close (false) the window; switches if left out. |

Result: [`PluginInfo`](#plugininfo).

#### `plugin.unconfigure_param`

**Unconfigure Plug-In Parameter**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Removes one parameter from a plug-in device's configured list (manual 24.1.2). A parameter that has automation, a clip envelope, or a MIDI, key or Macro mapping is refused, naming what it has, as Live warns before deleting one; `force` removes it anyway. One undo step. Returns `device.parameters`, each marked configured or not.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `param` | [`ParamId`](#paramid) | yes | The parameter to remove. |
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The device; the selected one if left out. |
| `force` | boolean | no | Remove it even when it has automation, a clip envelope, or a mapping (the warning accepted). |

Result: [`DeviceParameters`](#deviceparameters).

### Area `rack`

#### `rack.delete_variation`

**Delete Macro Variation**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Deletes the variation at `index`. One undo step, `Delete Macro Variation`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The variation's place in the rack's list, from 0. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.duplicate_variation`

**Duplicate Macro Variation**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Puts a copy of the variation at `index`, with the same name and values, straight after it. One undo step, `Duplicate Macro Variation`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The variation's place in the rack's list, from 0. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.invert_mapping`

**Invert Macro Mapping**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Swaps a mapping's Min and Max, as Invert Range does. The mapped parameter takes the value the macro gives it now. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `target` | [`MacroTarget`](#macrotarget) | yes | The mapped parameter. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.launch_variation`

**Launch Macro Variation**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets every macro of a rack that isn't excluded from variations to the value the variation at `index` holds, at once and on one frame, as the Launch Macro Variation button does. Excluded macros keep their values. Each macro moved is a hand move on it, so its automation envelope is overridden and, while Automation Arm records, the move is written as its envelope. Continuous mapped parameters glide to their new values. One undo step, `Launch Macro Variation`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The variation's place in the rack's list, from 0. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.macros`

**Rack Macros**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Reports a rack's macros and mappings: each macro's number, name, colour, value from 0 to 1, how it reads, and whether Randomize leaves it alone, with each mapping's target, device and parameter names and its range in the parameter's units and as positions on its travel, and how many macros show. The query tool's `device` reports the same in its `macros` field.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack; the selected device if left out, which must be a rack. |

Result: [`MacroState`](#macrostate).

#### `rack.map_macro`

**Map to Macro**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Maps a parameter inside a rack to one of its macros, numbered 1 to 16, as Map mode's Map button does: `target` is `{"type": "device", "device": d, "param": p}` for a device inside the rack at any depth (or the rack's own chain selector), or `{"type": "chain", "chain": c, "param": "volume" | "pan" | "mute"}` for a chain's mixer. A parameter is mapped to one macro of a rack: mapping it to another moves its mapping there. A new mapping runs the whole of the parameter's travel. One undo step, `Map to Macro`. What it maps reads back in `rack.macros`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `macro_number` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The macro, numbered from 1. |
| `target` | [`MacroTarget`](#macrotarget) | yes | The parameter to map. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.map_mode`

**Map Mode**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Turns a rack's Map mode on or off, the selected device's or `rack`'s: with it on, every parameter the rack can map is tinted, a Map button shows under each shown macro, and the mappings list takes the browser's place. Turning on another rack's Map mode turns this one's off. Map mode is view state: it isn't an undo step and the set doesn't keep it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Turn Map mode on (true) or off (false); switches if left out. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack; the selected device if left out, which must be a rack. |

Result: [`MacroState`](#macrostate).

#### `rack.move_pads`

**Move the Pads**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Moves the sixteen notes a drum rack's pad view shows (the rack in focus, or `rack`): to `first` (a note, rounded down to a row), or by `groups` of sixteen notes and `rows` of four from where it is, as dragging the overview's selector, or Up and Down with Cmd (Alt on Windows and Linux) for a row, do. The view stays within notes 0 to 127. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and the set keeps which notes show (`device_view.state`, the rack's `pads.first`).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `first` | integer or null | no | Show the sixteen notes from here (rounded down to a row); the view moves by `groups` and `rows` from where it is if left out. |
| `groups` | integer or null | no | How many groups of sixteen notes to move up (positive) or down. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The drum rack; the selected device if left out. |
| `rows` | integer or null | no | How many rows of four notes to move up or down. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `rack.overwrite_variation`

**Overwrite Macro Variation**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Replaces every value the variation at `index` holds with the macros' values now, keeping its name and place, as the Overwrite Macro Variation button does. One undo step, `Overwrite Macro Variation`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The variation's place in the rack's list, from 0. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.randomize_macros`

**Randomize Macros**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets every macro of a rack that has a mapping and isn't excluded from Randomization to a random position from 0 to 1, as the rack's Rand button does. Macros with no mapping, and excluded ones, keep their values. `seed` makes the values repeatable: the same seed gives the same values, and without one a new seed is picked. Each macro moved is a hand move on it, so its automation envelope is overridden. One undo step, `Randomize Macros`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `seed` | integer or null | no | The seed; without one a new seed is picked. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.rename_macro`

**Rename Macro**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Gives macro `macro_number` a `name` of its own; an empty name gives it its default name: its one parameter's name, or "Macro N". One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `macro_number` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The macro, numbered from 1. |
| `name` | string | yes | The name, or empty. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.rename_variation`

**Rename Macro Variation**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Gives the variation at `index` the `name` of its own. One undo step, `Rename Macro Variation`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The variation's place in the rack's list, from 0. |
| `name` | string | yes | The name. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.select_macro`

**Select Macro**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Selects a macro in a rack's Macro Controls, or none, so Rename names it. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step and the set doesn't keep it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `macro_number` | integer or null | no | The macro, numbered from 1; null, or left out, selects none. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack; the selected device if left out, which must be a rack. |

Result: [`MacroState`](#macrostate).

#### `rack.select_variation`

**Select Macro Variation**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Selects a variation in a rack's Macro Variations view, or none, so Rename, Duplicate and Delete act on it. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step and the set doesn't keep it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `index` | integer or null | no | The variation's place in the rack's list, from 0; null, or left out, selects none. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack; the selected device if left out, which must be a rack. |

Result: [`MacroState`](#macrostate).

#### `rack.set_auto_select`

**Auto Select**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Switches a rack's Auto Select, the selected device's or `rack`'s: while it is on, the chain list selects every chain that is processing, which the engine publishes after each block: in an instrument or MIDI effect rack each chain a held note reached, in an audio effect rack each chain whose chain select zone holds the chain selector's value. The devices view follows. It changes only the view: neither the switch nor the selections it makes are undo steps, and the set keeps the switch.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Switch on (true) or off (false); switches if left out. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack; the selected device if left out, which must be a rack. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `rack.set_macro_colour`

**Change Macro Color**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Colours macro `macro_number` with swatch `colour` of the palette of 5 rows of 14 (0 to 69), or clears its colour with null. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `macro_number` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The macro, numbered from 1. |
| `colour` | integer or null | no | The swatch, or `null` for none. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.set_macro_count`

**Show More or Fewer Macros**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets how many of a rack's 16 macros its Macro Controls show, from 1 to 16, always the lowest-numbered ones, as Show More and Show Fewer do. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and the set keeps the count.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | How many macros show, from 1 to 16. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack; the selected device if left out, which must be a rack. |

Result: [`MacroState`](#macrostate).

#### `rack.set_macro_info_text`

**Change Macro Info Text**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the info text of macro `macro_number`, which the Info View shows while the pointer is over it. Empty clears it. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `macro_number` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The macro, numbered from 1. |
| `info` | string | yes | The text. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.set_macro_randomize_excluded`

**Exclude Macro from Randomization**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Leaves macro `macro_number` out of Randomize (`excluded` true), or puts it back (false). A new rack's macros aren't excluded. One undo step, saved with the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `macro_number` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The macro, numbered from 1. |
| `excluded` | boolean | yes | Whether it's left out. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.set_macro_style`

**Change Macro Style**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets how macro `macro_number` is drawn and which positions it takes: `style` is `knob`, Live's continuous control, `stepped`, a knob that takes `steps` steps, or `radio_buttons`, a stepped macro drawn as its steps' buttons. A stepped macro takes from 2 to 16 steps, 8 by default, and only the positions `k / (steps - 1)`: a drag, an arrow key and `device.set_param` all move it a step at a time. A macro that becomes stepped moves to its nearest step. One undo step, saved with the set and with the rack in a preset.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `macro_number` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The macro, numbered from 1. |
| `style` | [`MacroStyle`](#macrostyle) | yes | The style. |
| `steps` | integer or null | no | How many steps a stepped macro takes, from 2 to 16; the macro's own number of steps when left out. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.set_macro_variation_excluded`

**Exclude Macro from Variations**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Leaves macro `macro_number` out of variations (`excluded` true), so no launch changes it, or puts it back (false). Storing and overwriting still record its value, so switching the exclusion off lets the next launch set it. One undo step, saved with the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `macro_number` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The macro, numbered from 1. |
| `excluded` | boolean | yes | Whether it's left out. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.set_mapped_value`

**Change parameter**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets a parameter a rack's macro drives to `value`, in the parameter's own units, without overriding its own automation envelope, which waits while the macro drives it. The macro commands run it inside their own undo step; run it directly only to correct a mapped value.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | [`MacroTarget`](#macrotarget) | yes | The mapped parameter. |
| `value` | number | yes | The value, in the parameter's own units. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.set_mapping_range`

**Change Macro Mapping**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Sets the range of a mapping to `min` and `max`, each a position from 0 (the bottom of the parameter's travel) to 1 (its top); Min above Max inverts the mapping, so the parameter falls as the macro rises. The mapped parameter takes the value the macro gives it now. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `target` | [`MacroTarget`](#macrotarget) | yes | The mapped parameter. |
| `min` | number | yes | The bottom of the range. |
| `max` | number | yes | The top of the range. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.set_view`

**Show or Hide a Rack's View**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Shows or hides one of the views of a rack, the selected device or `rack`: the Macro Controls, the chain list (View > Show Chains and Hide Chains) or the selected chain's devices. With every view hidden the rack folds into its view column. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and the set keeps which views each rack shows.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-DEV-012 | `Plus` | `Plus` | `device-view` | Show the selected rack's chain list | fixes `shown` = `true`; fixes `view` = `"chain_list"` |
| S-DEV-013 | `Minus` | `Minus` | `device-view` | Hide the selected rack's chain list | fixes `shown` = `false`; fixes `view` = `"chain_list"` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | [`RackView`](#rackview) | yes | The view. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack; the selected device if left out, which must be a rack. |
| `shown` | boolean or null | no | Show (true) or hide (false); switches if left out. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `rack.set_zone_editor`

**Show a Rack's Zone Editor**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Shows the zone editor of a rack, the selected device or `rack`, beside its chain list: `editor` is `key` (the Key button), `velocity` (Vel) or `select` (Chain); an audio effect rack has only `select`, and a drum rack none. Leaving `editor` out, or null, hides it (Hide). It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and the set keeps which editor each rack shows.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `editor` | [`ZoneKind`](#zonekind) or null | no | The editor to show: `key`, `velocity` (the Vel button) or `select` (the Chain button). None, or left out, is Hide. |
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack; the selected device if left out, which must be a rack. |

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `rack.show_variations`

**Show or Hide Macro Variations**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Shows or hides a rack's Macro Variations view, the selected device's or `rack`'s, as the Show/Hide Macro Variations view selector does. It changes only the view: it isn't an undo step, and the set keeps which views each rack shows. `rack.set_view` with the `variations` view does the same.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) or null | no | The rack; the selected device if left out, which must be a rack. |
| `shown` | boolean or null | no | Show the Macro Variations view (true) or hide it (false); switches if left out. |

Result: [`MacroState`](#macrostate).

#### `rack.store_variation`

**Store Macro Variation**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Stores every one of a rack's 16 macros' values as a new variation at the end of its list, named "Variation N", N one more than the highest number among the rack's variations named that way. A rack holds any number of variations. One undo step, `Store Macro Variation`. `rack.macros` reports the variations.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `rack.switch_hot_swap_target`

**Switch Hot-Swap Target**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

While a drum rack is being hot-swapped, switches the target between the rack and the rack's last selected pad, as D does; with a pad the target an item loaded from the browser lands on the pad. It changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-VIEW-007 | `D` | `D` | `global` | Switch between a Drum Rack and its last selected pad | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`DeviceViewState`](#deviceviewstate).

#### `rack.unmap_macro`

**Unmap Macro**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `device-view`.

Unmaps `target` from its rack's macro, as the mappings list's Delete does. The parameter keeps the value it has then and refuses no more. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rack` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The rack. |
| `target` | [`MacroTarget`](#macrotarget) | yes | The parameter to unmap. |

### Area `routing`

#### `routing.set_cue_out`

**Set Cue Out**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets Main's Cue Out, the audio interface's output channels the cue mix goes to, as Main's In/Out section does: `channel` is a stereo pair of the interface's outputs, counted from 1; the default is the first pair, 1/2. It carries the cue mix once cue mode is built (a later package); the choice is kept and saved with the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channel` | [`Channel`](#channel) | yes | The pair: its first channel, counted from 1. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `routing.set_input`

**Set Input**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets where an audio or MIDI track takes its input from, as the In/Out section's Audio From or MIDI From chooser and its channel do. An audio track can take `external` (Ext. In, the audio interface's inputs, with a `channel`: a single channel (`{ "type": "mono", "channel": 3 }`) or a stereo pair (`{ "type": "pair", "channel": 3 }`, the pair 3/4), counted from 1), `resampling` (the Main output, for recording the mix; the track's own output and sends are then silent so it can't feed back), `none`, or `track` with another audio track, a group, a return track, or Main and a `tap`: `pre_fx` (before its devices), `post_fx` (after its devices, before its mixer), or `post_mixer` (its output, the default). A MIDI track can take `all_ins` (every MIDI input whose Track switch is on in the settings, and the computer MIDI keyboard), `computer_keyboard`, `port` with the port's `name` as the MIDI settings list it, `none`, or another MIDI track (which carries MIDI once MIDI playback is built). `channel` is 1 to 16 to take only that channel, or null (the default) for All Channels; only a port input has one. The input is heard only while the track monitors it (`routing.set_monitor`). A routing may make a loop, as in Live; the engine plays the routing that closes it as silence.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `input` | [`Input`](#input) | yes | The input. |
| `channel` | integer or null | no | The MIDI channel to take, 1 to 16, or `null` (or nothing) for All Channels. Only a MIDI port input has a channel. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `routing.set_main_out`

**Set Main Out**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets Main's Main Out, the audio interface's output channels the Main mix goes to, as Main's In/Out section does: `channel` is a stereo pair of the interface's outputs (`{ "type": "pair", "channel": 3 }` is the pair 3/4), counted from 1. The default is the first pair, 1/2.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channel` | [`Channel`](#channel) | yes | The pair: its first channel, counted from 1 (`{ "type": "pair", "channel": 3 }` is 3/4). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `routing.set_midi_output`

**Set MIDI Output**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets where a MIDI track's MIDI goes, as its MIDI To chooser does: another MIDI track (give its ID; it arrives at its Track In), an output port (`{ "name": "Synth", "channel": 1 }`: the port's name as `midi.ports` lists it, with its Track switch on, and the channel to send on, 1 to 16), or `null` for No Output (a new MIDI track's). A track sends to a port the notes and controller, pitch bend and pressure messages that reach the end of its device chain (a track with an instrument sends none, the instrument playing them), at the moment their frame is heard at the audio interface's output; it keeps a missing port's name and sends again when the port returns. Choosing a port takes channel 1.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The MIDI track. |
| `to` | [`MidiTo`](#midito) or null | no | Another MIDI track (its ID), an output port with its channel (`{ "name": "Synth", "channel": 1 }`), or `null` (or nothing) for No Output. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `routing.set_monitor`

**Set Monitor**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets an audio or MIDI track's Monitor switch: `in` always plays the track's input through its devices and silences its clips, `auto` plays the input while the track is armed, and `off` never plays it. A new track is `auto`. Use `in` to hear another track routed into this one.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `monitor` | [`Monitor`](#monitor) | yes | `in`, `auto`, or `off`. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `routing.set_output`

**Set Output**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`, `arrangement`.

Sets where a track's audio goes, as the In/Out section's Audio To chooser does: `default` (Main, or the group the track is in), `main` (Main, even from inside a group), `track` with another audio track (its input, heard while that track monitors it) or the track's own group, `sends_only` (only through its sends to the return tracks), or `external` (Ext. Out: the track plays on the audio interface's output channels, a single channel or a stereo pair, the first pair by default, and not into Main). Audio, group, and return tracks take any of these. A routing may make a loop, as in Live; the engine then plays the routing that closes the loop as silence.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `output` | [`Output`](#output) | yes | The output. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `scene`

#### `scene.create`

**Insert Scene**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Inserts a new empty scene at `index` among the scenes, as Create ▸ Insert Scene (Cmd+I) does: it holds an empty slot in every audio and MIDI track. A new set opens with eight scenes. `id` must be a new ID the project has issued for it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The new scene's ID. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes among the scenes, from 0 to the number of scenes. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.delete`

**Delete Scene**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `session`.

Deletes a scene, and the clips in its slots with it; the clips in the other scenes stay. Undo restores everything it deleted, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.duplicate`

**Duplicate Scene**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Copies a scene and the clips in its slots into a new scene directly after it, as Edit ▸ Duplicate does. `clips` lists every track that holds a clip in the scene, each with the new ID its copy takes; each copy is an independent clip. A scene whose slots are all empty copies no clips. `id` must be a new ID the project has issued for it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |
| `id` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The new scene's ID. |
| `clips` | array of pair of [`TrackId`](#trackid) and [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | Each track that holds a clip in the scene, with the new ID its copy takes, each track once. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.move`

**Move Scene**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Moves a scene to `index` among the scenes, with the clips in its slots, as dragging a scene does. The index counts positions after the scene is taken out of its current place, so moving a scene down past its neighbour is its current index plus one.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes among the scenes. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.rename`

**Rename Scene**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Renames a scene. A name may be empty: a scene without a name shows its number, which is its position.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |
| `name` | string | yes | The new name. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.set_follow_actions`

**Set Scene Follow Actions**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Changes a scene's follow actions, as the Scene View does: what the scene does after it was launched, over the scenes as a clip's do over its track's slots. `enabled` is the Follow Action switch; `action_a` and `action_b` are one of `no_action`, `stop`, `play_again`, `previous`, `next`, `first`, `last`, `any`, `other` and `jump`; `chance_a` is action A's chance in whole percent, 0 to 100, and action B has the rest; `jump_a` and `jump_b` are the slot (scene) numbers Jump goes to, 1 up to the number of scenes, and 0 for none, where Jump stops the scene; `linked` is Longest (on by default): the follow time is the multiplier times the scene's longest clip; off: `time`; `multiplier` is the Linked multiplier, a whole number from 1; and `time` is the Unlinked follow time in ticks, from a sixteenth (a bar is 2822400 ticks in 4/4). Fields left out stay as they are, and a number past its limit is held at the limit. One undo step. The defaults are off, A Next, B No Action, 100 %, Linked, 1x, one bar. While the song plays the action runs when the follow time has passed after the scene started, and the global switch (`session.set_follow_actions_enabled`) must be on.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |
| `action_a` | [`FollowAction`](#followaction) or null | no | Action A. |
| `action_b` | [`FollowAction`](#followaction) or null | no | Action B. |
| `chance_a` | integer or null | no | The chance of action A in whole percent, 0 to 100; B has the rest. |
| `enabled` | boolean or null | no | The Follow Action switch. |
| `jump_a` | integer or null | no | The slot (scene) number action A's Jump goes to: 1 up to the number of scenes, and 0 for none. |
| `jump_b` | integer or null | no | The slot (scene) number action B's Jump goes to. |
| `linked` | boolean or null | no | Linked (on a scene, Longest) or Unlinked. |
| `multiplier` | integer or null | no | The Linked multiplier, a whole number from 1. |
| `time` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The Unlinked follow time in ticks, from a sixteenth. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.set_tempo`

**Set Scene Tempo**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Gives a scene a tempo, from 20 to 999 BPM, that launching the scene sets for the set, as the Tempo field in the Main column and the Scene View does. `tempo` left out or null switches the scene's tempo off, as double-clicking the field or Return to Default does, so launching it leaves the set's tempo as it is. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |
| `tempo` | [`Bpm`](#bpm) or null | no | The tempo, or `None` for none of its own. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `scene.set_time_signature`

**Set Scene Time Signature**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Gives a scene a time signature that launching the scene sets for the set, as the Signature field in the Main column and the Scene View does: a numerator from 1 to 99 over a denominator of 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16. `signature` left out or null switches the scene's signature off, so launching it leaves the set's signature as it is. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |
| `signature` | [`TimeSignature`](#timesignature) or null | no | The signature, or `None` for none of its own. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `search`

#### `search.close`

**Close Search**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `text-field`.

Closes the search field, removes the track outlines and shows every track again. Changes nothing in the set.

#### `search.commands`

**Find Commands**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

The rows the Commands scope lists for `text`, in the order it lists them: every command a menu item, a context-menu item or a shortcut runs, once, with the arguments that item fixes, its label, the menu or context it belongs to, the keys bound to it now and whether it can run now. A word matches when it starts a word of the label or the menu, or appears in the command's description; rows that can't run now come last. Works with the field closed, and runs nothing: run a row by running its `command` with its `args`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes | What was typed. |

#### `search.next`

**Search Next**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `text-field`.

In the Tracks scope, selects the next matching track after the selected one in display order (the first when none is selected, wrapping from the last), as clicking its title bar would, and scrolls the view in front to it, unfolding any group that holds it: Return in the field. In the Commands scope, moves the highlight down a row, wrapping. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SearchState`](#searchstate).

#### `search.open`

Opens the search field over the main view with the text empty, on the Commands scope (`commands`: the commands a menu item, a context-menu item or a shortcut runs) or the Tracks scope (`tracks`: tracks found by their name or by the name of a device on them). Help > Search Commands... and Cmd-Shift-P (Ctrl-Shift-P) open the first; Navigate > Find Track and Cmd-Shift-O (Ctrl-Shift-O) the second. With the field open it switches the scope and keeps the text. The field is view state: it isn't saved in the set and it isn't an undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-MENU-007 | `Cmd+Shift+P` | `Ctrl+Shift+P` | `global` | Open the command search | fixes `scope` = `"commands"` |
| S-FOCUS-015 | `Cmd+Shift+O` | `Ctrl+Shift+O` | `global` | Open the track search | fixes `scope` = `"tracks"` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scope` | [`SearchScope`](#searchscope) | yes | `commands` or `tracks`. |

Result: [`SearchState`](#searchstate).

#### `search.previous`

**Search Previous**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `text-field`.

The reverse of `search.next`: in the Tracks scope, selects the previous matching track (Shift-Return in the field); in the Commands scope, moves the highlight up a row, wrapping. Changes nothing in the set.

Switches Show Only Matches in the Tracks scope. The other tracks play, record and take edits as before. It's view state that ends with the search: it is off each time the field opens.

Switches the open search field to the Commands or the Tracks scope and keeps its text. Changes nothing in the set.
