**Type in Search**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `text-field`.

Sets the text of the open search field, as typing does. The Commands scope then lists the rows `search.commands` gives for it, with the first highlighted; the Tracks scope outlines the tracks `search.tracks` gives. Changes nothing in the set.

What the search field shows: whether it is open, its scope, its text, the highlighted row, whether Show Only Matches is on, and the rows it lists, each with its command ID and the arguments it fixes, or its track ID.

**Find Tracks**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

The tracks the Tracks scope lists for `text`, in display order: those with the text, ignoring case, in their name or in the name or own name of a device on them at any depth, plug-ins included. Each row says whether the track's name matched and which device did. Works with the field closed, and changes nothing.

### Area `session`

#### `session.back_to_arrangement`

**Back to Arrangement**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Returns every track to the Arrangement, as the Back to Arrangement button and F10 do. A Session clip that started has taken its track over from the Arrangement, and stays so after it stops, until this runs. It stops every track's Session clips at once, not on the launch quantisation grid, and drops launches and stops still queued; the Arrangement plays again from the playhead and the transport keeps running. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRANS-009 | `F10` | `F10` | `global` | Return every track to the Arrangement (Back to Arrangement) | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.back_to_arrangement_track`

**Back to Arrangement (Track)**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Returns one track to the Arrangement, as the button in the track's Arrangement header does: its Session clip stops at once, a launch or a stop still queued on it is dropped, and its Arrangement clips play again from the playhead. Other tracks are not touched, and the transport keeps running. A track nothing took over just keeps playing its Arrangement. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.capture_and_insert_scene`

**Capture and Insert Scene**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Inserts a new scene holding copies of the clips that are playing, each in its own track's slot, as Create > Capture and Insert Scene (Cmd-Shift-I, Ctrl-Shift-I) does, and the playing clips carry on in the copies without a break. The scene goes after the scene launched last, or after the selected scene when none has been launched since the set opened, and its tempo and time signature are set to the ones in force now. With nothing playing it inserts an empty scene with the same tempo and signature, and launches nothing. One undo step. The playing clips are the engine's, so it needs an engine that runs.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-009 | `Cmd+Shift+I` | `Ctrl+Shift+I` | `session` | Capture the playing clips into a new scene | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `session.copy_clip_to_slot`

**Copy Clip to Slot**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Copies a clip into a track's Session slot at `scene`, as Option-dragging (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) a clip between slots does. The target slot must be empty and the clip's data must match the track. The copy gets its own ID. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip to copy. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track whose slot it goes in. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it goes in. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `session.create_follow_action_chain`

**Create Follow Action Chain**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Chains the selected slots' clips, as the clip menu's Create Follow Action Chain (Cmd+Shift+Enter) does, a chain for each track in scene order: every clip gets Follow Action on, A Next at 100 %, B No Action and Linked 1x, so each launches the one after it when it ends. Where the next clip of the selection isn't the next slot, the clip gets A Jump to its slot instead, and the last clip jumps to the first, so the chain loops within the selection. Loop switches don't change. One undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-014 | `Cmd+Shift+Enter` | `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` | `session` | Create a follow action chain from the selected clips | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `session.deactivate`

**Deactivate Clips**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Switches the selected slots' clips off, or back on when they're all off, as pressing 0 does: a deactivated clip stays in place but doesn't play. One undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-018 | `0` | `0` | `session` | Deactivate the selected clip | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `session.delete`

**Delete in the Session View**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `session`.

Deletes the Session View's selection: the clips in the selected slots, or the selected scenes with the clips in their slots. Destructive, so an agent asks first. One undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `session.drop_files`

**Drop Files into a Slot**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `session`.

Puts audio files dropped from the browser, Finder, or Explorer into the Session slot at `track` and `scene`, as dropping them on a slot does: one after another down that track's scenes, or, with `spread` (Cmd, Ctrl on Windows and Linux, held while dropping), across the tracks at `scene`. Each target slot must be empty. Each file becomes a Session clip of its length, starting at the clip's beginning. One undo step. Reads the files, outside the project, and registers them so the set keeps them. Clip files (`.blclip`) are placed as clips: in an empty slot on a track of their kind, bringing the track's devices when it has no clips and no devices; with no `track` (the Session's drop area), each on a new track of its kind in the scene, named after the file, with its devices; with `spread`, each on a track of its own across the tracks at `scene`. A track of the other kind, a group, return or Main track, and a slot holding a clip take none, and the command is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paths` | array of string | yes | The files' paths, in the order dropped. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot the first one goes in. |
| `spread` | boolean | no | With the command modifier (Cmd, Ctrl on Windows and Linux) held, spread them across the tracks instead of down the scenes. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track whose slot they go in. Left out, the Session's drop area: clip files make a new track of their kind each, in the scene (audio files need a track). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

**Duplicate Scene**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Copies the selected scene and the clips in its slots into a new scene directly after it, as Edit > Duplicate does. Each copied clip is independent. One undo step.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) or null | no | The scene; the selected one when left out. |

Moves the global launch quantisation one step larger up the Quantization Menu's list: none, 8 bars, 4 bars, 2 bars, 1 bar, 1/2, 1/2T, 1/4, 1/4T, 1/8, 1/8T, 1/16, 1/16T, 1/32. #### `session.launch`

**Launch Clip**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Launches the clip in a track's Session slot at `scene`, as clicking the slot's launch button does. While the song plays the clip starts on the next line of the global launch quantisation grid, and until then the slot reads `queued`; while it's stopped the transport starts at once from the Arrangement position and the clip starts with it. A clip already playing on that track stops where the new one starts. The clip's launch mode (`clip.set_launch_mode`) says what the press does next: a Trigger, Gate or Repeat clip that already plays restarts on the grid, and a Toggle clip that plays is queued to stop. A Gate or Repeat clip stops when `session.release` follows. The engine publishes the slots' states with the playhead, so the UI can draw them. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track whose slot it is. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it is. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.launch_scene`

**Launch Scene**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Launches every clip of the scene at `scene`, as clicking the scene's launch button does: all of them start on one line of the launch quantisation grid, as one launch, so a scene's clips play together. While the song is stopped the transport starts at once. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.launch_selected`

**Launch the Selected Clips and Scenes**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Launches every selected slot that holds a clip and every selected scene, as Enter does in the Session View: each runs `session.launch` or `session.launch_scene`, so it waits for the launch quantisation grid while the song plays and starts the transport at once while it's stopped. A selected empty slot is skipped. Select a slot or a scene first. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-001 | `Enter` | `Enter` | `session` | Launch the selected clip, slot or scene | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.overdub`

**Overdub Slot**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `session`.

Records the notes an armed MIDI track plays into the MIDI clip that is playing in the slot (`track`, `scene`), a loop pass at a time: each pass adds its notes to the clip and is one undo step. A clip that does not loop overdubs until it ends. Launch the clip first; audio clips are never overdubbed. Ends like any recording: `session.stop_recording`, or `session.record` again, which pauses the overdub while the clip plays on. Recording captures input devices, so the person is asked first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track whose slot it is. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it is. |

Result: [`RecordingStarted`](#recordingstarted).

#### `session.record`

**Record to Session**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`, `session`.

The Session Record button (Playback ▸ Record to Session, Cmd+Shift+F9; Ctrl+Shift+F9 on Windows and Linux). Records every armed track into the Session View: a MIDI track whose clip is playing overdubs it, one note pass at a time; any other armed track records a new clip into the selected scene's slot if it is empty, else into the next empty slot below it on that track, and a scene is inserted at the end when there is none. The recording starts on the next line of the launch quantisation grid while the song plays, and from the playhead, after any count-in, while it is stopped, which starts the transport. The clip exists from the start and grows as it records. While a recording is under way the command ends it instead, as pressing the button again does: the new clips play on as loops from the next grid line. Audio goes to the project's Samples/Recorded/; the set must have been saved. Recording captures input devices, including a microphone, so the person is asked first. To end a recording without asking, run `session.stop_recording`.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-012 | `Cmd+Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+Shift+F9` | `session` | Record into the Session View | runs it |
| S-TRANS-008 | `Cmd+Shift+F9` | `Ctrl+Shift+F9` | `global` | Record into the Session View | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`RecordingStarted`](#recordingstarted).

#### `session.record_slot`

**Record into Slot**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `session`.

The Clip Record button in an empty slot of an armed track: records a new clip into that slot (`track`, `scene`), starting on the next grid line, or from the playhead with the transport stopped. The track must be armed and the slot empty: a slot with a clip has a launch button instead, which `session.launch` presses. The clip exists from the start and grows as it records; `session.launch` on the recording slot, or `session.stop_recording`, ends the recording and loops the clip, and `session.stop_track` ends it without looping. Audio goes to the project's Samples/Recorded/. Recording captures input devices, including a microphone, so the person is asked first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track whose slot it is. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it is. |

Result: [`RecordingStarted`](#recordingstarted).

#### `session.release`

**Release Clip Launch Button**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Ends the press that `session.launch` began on the slot at `track` and `scene`, as letting go of the slot's launch button does. A clip in Gate mode stops on the next line of its launch quantisation grid, or at once with quantisation off, and a Repeat clip stops the same way after the quantum it is playing; a release never cancels a launch still queued, so the clip plays one quantum before it stops. A Trigger or Toggle clip ignores the release, and so does a slot that isn't playing. The clip's mode is read at the release. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track whose slot it is. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it is. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.scroll`

**Scroll the Session View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Scrolls the Session View's scenes by `y` points (positive towards later scenes), as the wheel over the grid does. The returns and Main stay pinned. It can't scroll before the first scene or past the last. Changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `y` | number | no | Points to scroll the scenes down: positive towards later scenes. |

Result: [`SessionViewState`](#sessionviewstate).

#### `session.select`

**Select in the Session View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Selects a slot, a scene, or a track's title bar, as clicking the grid does. `track` and `scene` together name a slot, `scene` alone a scene, and `track` alone a title bar. `mode` is `replace` for a plain click, `add` for Cmd-click (Ctrl on Windows and Linux), which adds the item or removes it when it's already selected, and `range` for Shift-click, which selects from the last item clicked to this one. Changes only the view.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | [`SessionSelectMode`](#sessionselectmode) | no | How the click changes the selection. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) or null | no | The scene, for a slot or a scene. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track, for a slot or a title bar. |

Result: [`SessionViewState`](#sessionviewstate).

#### `session.select_all`

**Select All Slots**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Selects every clip slot in the Session View, as Edit > Select All (Cmd-A, Ctrl-A) does in it. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-003 | `Cmd+A` | `Ctrl+A` | `session` | Select all clips and slots | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SessionViewState`](#sessionviewstate).

#### `session.select_edge`

**Select the Scene's First or Last Track**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Selects the first (Home) or last (End) track of the current scene, as Home and End do in the Session View. On the last track, End selects the scene itself. Changes only the view.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-020 | `Home`, `Fn+Left` | `Home` | `session` | Jump to the first track of the current scene | fixes `edge` = `"first"` |
| S-SES-021 | `End`, `Fn+Right` | `End` | `session` | Jump to the last track of the current scene | fixes `edge` = `"last"` |
| S-SES-022 | `End`, `Fn+Right` | `End` | `session` | From the last track, jump to the current scene | fixes `edge` = `"last"` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `edge` | [`SelectEdge`](#selectedge) | no | Which edge to select. |

Result: [`SessionViewState`](#sessionviewstate).

#### `session.set_follow_actions_enabled`

**Enable Follow Actions Globally**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Turns every clip's and scene's follow actions on or off (`enabled`; left out, the switch goes to the other state), as the Enable Follow Actions Globally switch in Main's status row does. Off, no follow action runs, whatever a clip's or scene's own Follow Action switch says; a clip that started while it was off follows nothing until it starts again. On by default. Saved with the set beside the launch quantisation, and no undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean or null | no | Whether follow actions run; left out, the switch goes to the other state. |

Result: [`LaunchSettings`](#launchsettings).

#### `session.set_quantization`

**Set Global Launch Quantization**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the global launch quantisation: the grid line a clip or a scene launch, or a stop, waits for while the song plays (`quantization`: `none`, a bar count like `2_bars`, or a note value from `half` to `thirty_second`, with `_triplet` forms). The Control Bar's Quantization Menu shows it, and Cmd+6 to Cmd+9 and Cmd+0 (Ctrl+6 to Ctrl+9 and Ctrl+0 on Windows and Linux) set the common ones. It's saved with the set beside the song and changing it is no undo step. A launch or a stop already queued keeps the frame it was queued for.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-GQ-001 | `Cmd+6` | `Ctrl+6` | `global` | Set global launch quantisation to a sixteenth note | fixes `quantization` = `"sixteenth"` |
| S-GQ-002 | `Cmd+7` | `Ctrl+7` | `global` | Set global launch quantisation to an eighth note | fixes `quantization` = `"eighth"` |
| S-GQ-003 | `Cmd+8` | `Ctrl+8` | `global` | Set global launch quantisation to a quarter note | fixes `quantization` = `"quarter"` |
| S-GQ-004 | `Cmd+9` | `Ctrl+9` | `global` | Set global launch quantisation to one bar | fixes `quantization` = `"1_bar"` |
| S-GQ-005 | `Cmd+0` | `Ctrl+0` | `global` | Turn global launch quantisation off | fixes `quantization` = `"none"` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quantization` | [`LaunchQuantization`](#launchquantization) | yes | The step launches and stops wait for. |

Result: [`LaunchSettings`](#launchsettings).

#### `session.set_quantization_enabled`

**Launch Quantization Enabled**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Turns quantised launching on or off (`enabled`; left out, the switch goes to the other state): off, a launch or a stop takes effect at once whatever the quantisation says. Cmd+4 with the Session View focused, and Options ▸ Launch Quantization Enabled, which shows a check mark while it's on. Saved with the set, and no undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-027 | `Cmd+4` | `Ctrl+4` | `session` | Turn launch quantisation on or off | toggles `enabled` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean or null | no | Whether launches and stops are quantised; left out, the switch goes to the other state. |

Result: [`LaunchSettings`](#launchsettings).

#### `session.smaller_quantization`

**Smaller Launch Quantization**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Moves the global launch quantisation one step smaller down the Quantization Menu's list: none, 8 bars, 4 bars, 2 bars, 1 bar, 1/2, 1/2T, 1/4, 1/4T, 1/8, 1/8T, 1/16, 1/16T, 1/32. Cmd+1 with the Session View focused, and Options ▸ Smaller Launch Quantization. The smallest step stays. Saved with the set, and no undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-024 | `Cmd+1` | `Ctrl+1` | `session` | Make launch quantisation smaller | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`LaunchSettings`](#launchsettings).

#### `session.state`

**Session View State**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports what the Session View grid has selected: the slots, the scenes (their launch buttons or names), and the track title bars, and how far the scenes are scrolled. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SessionViewState`](#sessionviewstate).

#### `session.stop_all`

**Stop All Clips**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Stops every track's playing clip, as Stop All Clips at the Main column's left does: all of them stop on the next line of the launch quantisation grid, as one stop. Launches still queued are dropped, and the transport keeps playing. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.stop_recording`

**Stop Session Recording**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `session`.

Ends the Session recording on the next grid line, without asking the person: the new clips it made play on as loops from there, and an overdubbed clip plays on as it was. A clip that is still being recorded is a clip of the length so far, even when nothing was played. Does nothing when no Session recording is under way.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.stop_selected`

**Stop the Selected Tracks' Clips**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Stops the clip of every track that has a selected slot in the Session View, as Cmd+Enter (Ctrl+Enter on Windows and Linux) does: each stops on the next line of the launch quantisation grid, and launches still queued on those tracks are dropped. The transport keeps playing, and nothing in the set changes. Select a slot first.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-006 | `Cmd+Enter` | `Ctrl+Enter` | `session` | Stop the clips in the tracks that have a selected slot | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.stop_track`

**Stop Track**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Stops the clip the track plays, as the track's stop button in the status row does: it stops on the next line of the launch quantisation grid, and until then the slot reads `queued to stop`. A launch still queued on the track is dropped, and the transport keeps playing. It changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `session.toggle_follow_actions`

**Toggle Follow Actions**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Switches the Follow Action switch of the selected slots' clips on, or off when they are all on already, as Shift+Enter does: with some on and some off, they all go on. One undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-013 | `Shift+Enter` | `Shift+Enter` | `session` | Turn follow actions on or off for the selected clips | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `session.triplet_quantization`

**Triplet Launch Quantization**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `session`.

Makes the global launch quantisation the triplet of its note value, or the plain value again: 1/2 and 1/2T, 1/4 and 1/4T, 1/8 and 1/8T, 1/16 and 1/16T. `none` and the bar counts have no triplet, so it changes nothing while one of them is set. Cmd+3 with the Session View focused, and Options ▸ Triplet Launch Quantization. Saved with the set, and no undo step.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-026 | `Cmd+3` | `Ctrl+3` | `session` | Toggle triplet launch quantisation | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`LaunchSettings`](#launchsettings).

### Area `set`

#### `set.backups`

**Beatlayer Set Backups**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

The open set's backups, in the project folder's `Backup` folder, newest first, each with the time it was made in local time. The list is empty when the set has no backups.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`Backups`](#backups).

#### `set.collect_all_and_save`

**Collect All and Save**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Copies the files the open set uses that live outside its project folder into the project's `Samples/Imported` folder, re-points the set's media table at the copies, and saves the set, as File ▸ Collect All and Save does in Live, so the set no longer depends on files elsewhere. `groups` chooses which places to collect from: "other-project", "user-library" and "elsewhere"; all of them when none are given. Fails if the set has never been saved; use `set.save_as` to give it a project folder first. The result's `files` is how many files were copied.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `groups` | array of [`ExternalGroup`](#externalgroup) | no | The groups to collect from: "other-project", "user-library" or "elsewhere". All of them when none are given. |
| `project` | string or null | no | The project folder to collect for, when it isn't the open set's: every set in it is rewritten, each keeping the version it replaces in its project's `Backup` folder (R16). |

Result: [`FileReport`](#filereport).

#### `set.discard_changes`

**Don't Save**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Throws away the open set's unsaved changes, as choosing Don't Save when asked to save does: the set goes back to how it was when it was last opened or saved (a set never saved goes back to the factory default set), and its undo history is cleared. The changes can't be brought back. Nothing on disk changes. Does nothing if there are no unsaved changes.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.discard_recovery`

**Discard Recovery**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Declines to recover a set that `set.list_recoverable` lists, the one with `id` or the newest: its unsaved edits are removed from beside the set, so it isn't offered again, and a copy of its journal is kept in the recovery folder's Discarded folder for seven days. Its set file is untouched.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string or null | no | The recoverable set's `id`, as `set.list_recoverable` gives it. Leave it out for the newest. |

Result: [`DiscardedRecovery`](#discardedrecovery).

#### `set.import_dawproject`

**Import DAWproject File**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Reads the DAWproject file at `path` and opens what it holds as a new set, in place of the open one, as opening a set does: it is refused while the open set has unsaved changes. The new set starts empty and holds what the file carries: its tracks, groups, returns and their mixer and routing, its clips with their notes, media, warping and loops, its scenes and slots, its tempo and time signature. It is unsaved, and its name is the file's name without `.dawproject` until it is first saved. The result's `report` says what the import left out or changed, and `set.import_report` gives that report again while the set the import made is open. Reads a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The DAWproject file to read, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. |

Result: [`ImportDawProjectResult`](#importdawprojectresult).

#### `set.import_report`

**DAWproject Import Report**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports what the last DAWproject import left out or changed: each thing, where it was, how many there were, and what Beatlayer did, and the application and version the file says made it. It gives the report again while the set the import made is open, and nothing after another set opens. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ImportReport`](#importreport).

#### `set.later_recovery`

**Later Recovery**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Closes the recovery prompt the app shows at launch, leaving every set it listed to be offered again at the next launch: nothing is recovered and nothing is thrown away. The prompt's Later button runs it, and Esc does the same. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`RecoveryPrompt`](#recoveryprompt).

#### `set.list_recoverable`

**List Recoverable Sets**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Lists the sets that Beatlayer, here or in an earlier run, stopped without closing (a crash, a forced quit, a power cut) while they had unsaved edits. Each has an `id` for `set.recover` or `set.discard_recovery`, its file (null if it had never been saved), how many edits followed its last save, and when the last was made. Sets open in another running instance aren't listed. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`RecoverableSets`](#recoverablesets).

#### `set.new`

**New Beatlayer Set**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Replaces the open set with the factory default set: four tracks (two MIDI, two audio) and two return tracks, shown in the Arrangement View. Unsaved changes to the open set are lost, and its undo history is cleared, so save first if they matter.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FILE-001 | `Cmd+N` | `Ctrl+N` | `global` | Create a new set | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.open`

**Open Beatlayer Set...**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Opens the set file at `path` (or the only set in the project folder at `path`), replacing the open set and clearing its undo history. It refuses while the open set has unsaved changes: save them first with `set.save` or `set.save_as`, or throw them away with `set.discard_changes`, so losing work is always its own step. A person choosing the menu item or pressing the shortcut is asked whether to save, then picks the file in a dialog.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FILE-002 | `Cmd+O` | `Ctrl+O` | `global` | Open a set | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The set file's path, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. |

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.open_backup`

**Open Beatlayer Set Backup**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Opens the backup at `path` as the set itself, as File ▸ Open Beatlayer Set Backups does: the set keeps its own file and name, its song is the backup's, and it opens unsaved with an empty undo history, so `set.save` makes the backup the set's current version. Refuses while the set has unsaved changes, as `set.open` does.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The backup to open, by its path. |

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.recover`

**Recover Set**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Opens a set that `set.list_recoverable` lists, the one with `id` or the newest, exactly as it was after its last journalled edit. It replaces the open set, whose undo history is cleared; if the open set had unsaved edits they're kept for recovery in turn. The recovered set is unsaved: use `set.save` to keep it in its file, or `set.save_as`. Use it when the user wants back the work a crash interrupted.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string or null | no | The recoverable set's `id`, as `set.list_recoverable` gives it. Leave it out for the newest. |

Result: [`RecoveredSet`](#recoveredset).

#### `set.relink_missing`

**Relink Missing Files**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Searches for the files the open set uses that are missing or changed, and relinks each one to the file found with the same content, as Live's automatic search does. The search covers the set's project folder, the User Library, the folders the files were last in, and any `folders` given, each with its subfolders; `project` and `library` switch the first two off, and `folder` names the folder the Automatic Search's Search Folder chooses. A file with one candidate is relinked to it; a file with several keeps its row, and the candidates are in the result's `candidates`, so the person chooses. The result's `files` is how many files were relinked. It also runs by itself when a set is opened.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string or null | no | The folder the Automatic Search's Search Folder names. |
| `folders` | array of string | no | Folders to search, each with its subfolders, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. May be empty. |
| `library` | boolean or null | no | Whether the User Library is searched. On unless asked otherwise. |
| `project` | boolean or null | no | Whether the set's project folder is searched. On unless asked otherwise. |

Result: [`FileReport`](#filereport).

#### `set.restore`

**Restore**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Replaces the whole song with the one a row of `set.save_history` holds, as one undo step named `Restore Save Point` or `Restore Saved Version` that undo takes back. The set keeps its file and name, and the transport keeps playing. With Save Continuously on the restore is a new save point; every row stays listed. A row that can't be read changes nothing. Read the result back with the query tool's `song` (`undo.next_undo`).

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | The row's `id`, as `set.save_history` gives it. |

Result: [`Restored`](#restored).

#### `set.save`

**Save Beatlayer Set**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Saves the set to its file, replacing the file's previous contents, which are kept in the `Backup` folder of the set's project folder (the last 10 saves). Fails if the set has never been saved; use `set.save_as` to give it a file and a project folder first.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FILE-003 | `Cmd+S` | `Ctrl+S` | `global` | Save the set | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.save_as`

**Save Beatlayer Set As...**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Saves the set under a new name or in a new place, always inside a project folder, and that file becomes the set's. `path` gives a folder and the set's name, such as `/Music/Tango.blset` (`.blset` is added if it's missing). If the folder is a project folder, one that already holds a `.blset` set, the set joins that project as `<name>.blset` there; a set of that name there is replaced, and the replaced version kept in that project's `Backup` folder. Otherwise a new project folder, `<name> Project`, is made in the folder (or `<name> Project 2` and so on if that name is taken, so nothing is overwritten), and the set is saved inside it, as `/Music/Tango Project/Tango.blset`. The result's `path` is where the set was saved. Moving to another project folder keeps the set using the same media files. A person choosing the menu item or pressing the shortcut picks the path in a dialog that opens in the set's project folder.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-FILE-004 | `Cmd+Shift+S` | `Ctrl+Shift+S` | `global` | Save the set under a new name | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | A folder and the set's name, as a set file's path such as `/Music/Tango.blset`, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. The set goes in that folder if it's a project folder (it holds a set already), and otherwise in a new `<name> Project` folder inside it; the result says where. |

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.save_as_default`

**Save Beatlayer Set As Default Set...**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Saves the open set as the default set, which every new set starts from, as File ▸ Save Beatlayer Set As Default Set does in Live. `path` names the default set's file; left out it goes in the User Library's `Templates` folder, or beside the app's preferences when there is no User Library. The open set itself doesn't change and keeps its own file. The result's `path` is the default set's file.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string or null | no | The file to save the default set as, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. Left out, it goes in the User Library's `Templates` folder, or beside the app's preferences when there is no User Library. `.blset` is added if it's missing. |

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.save_as_template`

**Save Beatlayer Set As Template...**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Saves the open set as a template in the User Library's `Templates` folder, making that folder if it isn't there, as File ▸ Save Beatlayer Set As Template does in Live. `name` names the template; left out it takes the open set's name. The open set itself doesn't change and keeps its own file. The result's `path` is the template's file.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string or null | no | The template's name, without the `.blset` extension; left out uses the open set's name. |

Result: [`SetResult`](#setresult).

#### `set.save_copy`

**Save a Copy...**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Saves a copy of the open set at `path`, as File ▸ Save a Copy... does: in the folder when it is a project folder, otherwise in a new "<name> Project" folder. The copy names the same media files. The open set keeps its file, its name, its undo history and whether it has unsaved changes.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Where to save the copy, as a save dialog gives it: a folder and the set's name, such as `/Music/Tango.blset`. |

Result: [`SavedCopy`](#savedcopy).

#### `set.save_history`

**Save History**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Lists the open set's save history, newest first: the save points Save Continuously kept since the last save (none while it is off), then the set as last saved, then its backups. Each row has an `id` for `set.restore`, its kind (`save_point`, `saved` or `backup`), its time in UTC and its label, which is the edit's name for a save point. A set never saved has no rows. Changes nothing.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SaveHistory`](#savehistory).

### Area `settings`

#### `settings.next_page`

**Next Settings Page**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `settings`.

Shows the next page of the Settings window, wrapping from the last to the first. Changes no setting.

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SET-005 | `Option+Tab` | `Ctrl+Tab` | `settings` | Show the next settings page | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

#### `settings.previous_page`

**Previous Settings Page**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `settings`.

Shows the previous page of the Settings window, wrapping from the first to the last. Changes no setting.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SET-006 | `Option+Shift+Tab` | `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` | `settings` | Show the previous settings page | runs it |

#### `settings.set_appearance`

**Appearance**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Draws the theme in its light or dark colours, or follows the operating system's mode while Beatlayer runs (`follow-system`); a new install draws dark. Kept for the next start; changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appearance` | [`Appearance`](#appearance) | yes | `light`, `dark` or `follow-system`. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_auto_hide_plug_in_windows`

**Auto-Hide Plug-In Windows**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Auto-Hide Plug-In Windows, on the Settings window's Plug-Ins page; it's on in a new install, as Live's is. While it's on, a floating device's window or a plug-in's editor window hides while another track is selected and comes back when its own track is selected again, as Live's plug-in windows do. A hidden window's device still floats, and a hidden editor stays open: hiding isn't docking or closing, isn't an undo step, and the set saves the device as floating. `device.windows` and `plugin.info` say which windows show. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.set_auto_warp_long_samples`

**Auto-Warp Long Samples**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Auto-Warp Long Samples on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page; it's on in a new install, as Live's is. While it's on, a new audio clip of a long sample, one of 60 seconds or more, is warped with a warp marker on the first beat of every bar its analysis finds, and its 1.1.1 on the first beat; off, it is left unwarped. Clips already in the set keep their settings. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.set_automation_record_mode`

**Automation Record Mode**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses the mode an Arrangement recording writes control moves in, the one the Control Bar's Automation Arm button's context menu chooses: `touch` (the default, Live's) writes a control's values while it is held, `latch` holds the last value a control was moved to until the recording stops, and `write` writes a moved control's envelope from where the recording started. A Session recording is unaffected. The mode is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | [`AutomationRecordMode`](#automationrecordmode) | yes | `touch`, `latch` or `write`. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_brightness`

**Brightness**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Adds points of lightness to every background colour, from -50 to 50; 0 is the default. Chromatic colours and the track palette don't change. Kept for the next start; changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | integer from -50 to 50 | yes | Points of lightness added to the backgrounds, from -50 to 50. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_collect_files_on_export`

**Collect Files on Export**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses Collect Files on Export on the Settings window's Library page: what happens to the audio files a clip or a set uses when it is saved to the browser as a clip file or a set. `always` (a new install's choice) copies every such file that isn't already in the saved file's project into its `Samples/Imported` folder; `never` copies none, and the saved file names each file where it is; `ask` asks first, with Copy, Don't Copy and Cancel, and the commands that save to the browser refuse to run under it without their `copy` argument, so an agent asks the person first. Collect All and Save and device presets don't follow it. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | [`CollectFiles`](#collectfiles) | yes | `always`, `never` or `ask`. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_color_hue`

**Color Hue**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Turns the hue of the interface's chromatic colours by this many degrees, from -180 to 180 in steps of 5; 0 is the default. Backgrounds and the track palette don't change. Kept for the next start; changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `degrees` | integer from -180 to 180 | yes | Degrees the interface's colours are turned, from -180 to 180. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_color_intensity`

**Color Intensity**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Multiplies the chroma of the interface's chromatic colours, from 0 to 200 percent in steps of 5; 100 is the default. Backgrounds and the track palette don't change. Kept for the next start; changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `percent` | integer from 0 to 200 | yes | A whole percentage from 0 to 200, in steps of 5. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_continuous_save`

**Save Continuously**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Turns Save Continuously on or off (it starts off). When on, every finished edit of a set that has a file is saved within a second, so reopening the set shows it without asking, and each edit is a save point in the set's history since its last normal save. Turning it on saves the open set's unsaved edits that way. When off, edits are still journalled for crash recovery, and only Save keeps them. Save still writes the set file either way.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether Save Continuously is on. |

Result: [`ContinuousSave`](#continuoussave).

#### `settings.set_create_fades_on_clip_edges`

**Create Fades on Clip Edges**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Create Fades on Clip Edges, on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page; it's on in a new install, as Live's is. While it's on, each audio clip added to the Arrangement from now on gets fades of 4 ms (0.004 s) at both edges, so a clip that starts or ends mid-waveform doesn't click; clips already in the set keep their fades, which `clip.set_fades` changes. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.set_default_launch_mode`

**Default Launch Mode**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses Default Launch Mode on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page: the launch mode (`trigger`, `gate`, `toggle` or `repeat`) a new Session clip starts with. It's `trigger` in a new install, as Live's is. Clips made so far keep their modes, and launch modes aren't built into clips yet, so for now it only keeps the choice. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | [`LaunchMode`](#launchmode) | yes | The launch mode new clips start with. |

#### `settings.set_default_launch_quantization`

**Default Launch Quantization**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses Default Launch Quantization on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page: the launch quantisation a new Session clip starts with, one of the global quantisation's steps (see `clip.set_launch_quantization`), or `null` to follow the global quantisation (the default, Live's "Global"). Clips already in the set keep theirs. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quantization` | [`LaunchQuantization`](#launchquantization) or null | no | The quantisation new clips start with; `null` (or nothing) follows the global one, Live's "Global". |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_default_warp_mode`

**Default Warp Mode**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses Default Warp Mode on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page: the warp mode (`beats`, `tones`, `texture`, `re_pitch`, `complex` or `complex_pro`) a new warped clip takes. It's `beats` in a new install, as Live's is. Clips already in the set keep their modes. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | [`DefaultWarpMode`](#defaultwarpmode) | yes | The warp mode a new warped clip takes. |

#### `settings.set_grid_line_intensity`

**Grid Line Intensity**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Sets how strong the grid lines of the Arrangement, the Clip View's editors and the automation lanes are, from 0 to 200 percent in steps of 5; 100, the default, draws the theme's grid colour, 0 shows no line. Kept for the next start; changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `percent` | integer from 0 to 200 | yes | A whole percentage from 0 to 200, in steps of 5. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_high_contrast`

**High Contrast**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches High Contrast, off in a new install. On, text stands at a contrast ratio of at least 7:1 against its background, dimmed text at 4.5:1, and separators, outlines and the focus ring at 3:1, whatever the other Theme & Colors settings are. Kept for the next start; changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_loop_warp_short_samples`

**Loop/Warp Short Samples**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses Loop/Warp Short Samples on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page: what a new audio clip of a short sample, one under 60 seconds, gets when it is dropped from the browser, loaded with Enter or imported. `unwarped_one_shot` leaves Warp and the loop off; `warped_one_shot` warps it as a loop of whole bars, the loop off; `warped_loop` does the same with the loop on; `auto`, what a new install has, makes a warped loop when the file's analysis finds a steady beat that fits 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 bars, and an unwarped one-shot otherwise. Clips already in the set keep their settings. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | [`LoopWarpShortSamples`](#loopwarpshortsamples) | yes | What a new clip of a short sample gets. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_outline_view_in_focus`

**Outline View in Focus**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Outline View in Focus, on the Settings window's Display & Input page: while it's on, as it is in a new install (as Live's is), a border is drawn round the part of the main window that has the keyboard focus and an outline round the focused control; while it's off, nothing shows where the focus is. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

#### `settings.set_record_session_automation_in`

**Record Session Automation in**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses Record Session automation in on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page: `armed_tracks` (the default, Live's) records the control moves of a Session recording into the clips of the armed tracks, `all_tracks` into the playing clip of every track. Moves are recorded only while Automation Arm is on (`arrangement.automation_arm`). The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracks` | [`SessionAutomationTracks`](#sessionautomationtracks) | yes | `armed_tracks` or `all_tracks`. |

#### `settings.set_retune_on_tuning_load`

**Retune Set On Loading Tuning Systems**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Retune Set On Loading Tuning Systems, the Options menu's item; it's off in a new install. With it off, loading, changing or removing a tuning leaves every note on its key. With it on, `tuning.load` and `tuning.remove` called without `retune` move every note of the MIDI clips on tracks that play the tuning to the key whose new pitch is nearest the pitch it had, and a person who loads or removes a tuning is asked first (Retune, or Cancel to change nothing). The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

**Sample Editor**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses the sample editor on the Settings window's File & Folder page: the command the Edit button in the Clip View's Audio Utilities panel opens a clip's file in. `path` is the command: the program, its arguments, and the clip's file as the last one, or `null` for none, when Edit opens the File & Folder page instead. Run by a person from the Browse button without a `path`, it asks for a program. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `path` is the editor in use afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string or null | no | The editor's command: the program, its arguments, and the clip's file as the last one. `null` for none, when Edit opens the File & Folder page instead. |

Result: [`SampleEditorResult`](#sampleeditorresult).

#### `settings.set_select_next_scene_on_launch`

**Select Next Scene on Launch**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Select Next Scene on Launch on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page; it's on in a new install, as Live's is. While it's on, launching a scene (`session.launch_scene`) selects the scene after it, when there is one. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.set_select_on_launch`

**Select on Launch**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Select on Launch on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page; it's on in a new install, as Live's is. While it's on, launching a clip that sits in a slot (`session.launch`) selects that slot. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.set_start_recording_on_scene_launch`

**Start Recording on Scene Launch**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Start Recording on Scene Launch on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page; it's off in a new install, as Live's is. Session recording isn't built yet, so for now it only keeps the choice. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

#### `settings.set_temporary_folder`

**Temporary Folder**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses the Temporary Folder on the Settings window's File & Folder page: where the files Reverse, Crop, Consolidate, Freeze and Bounce write go while the set has never been saved (the first save moves them into the project's `Samples/Processed` folders). `path` is an absolute path, made when it is first needed, or `null` for the default, a `Temporary` folder in Beatlayer's application-data folder. Files already written stay where they are. Run by a person from the Browse button without a `path`, it asks for a folder. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `path` is the folder in use afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string or null | no | The folder's absolute path, or `null` for the default: a `Temporary` folder in Beatlayer's application-data folder. |
