#### `settings.set_theme`

**Theme**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses the theme every window draws, by its name: Beatlayer, or a theme from the User Library's Themes folder; `settings.state` lists them in `theme_colors.themes`. `dark` and `light`, which earlier versions took, set the Appearance instead. The choice is kept for the next start, and a theme that can't be read is drawn as Beatlayer. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `theme` | string | yes | A theme's name, as `settings.state`'s `theme_colors.themes` lists it. `dark` and `light`, which earlier versions took, set the Appearance instead. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_tone`

**Tone**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Tints the theme's neutral colours warm or cool, or leaves them as the theme gives them (`neutral`, the default); the chromatic colours aren't toned. Kept for the next start; changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tone` | [`Tone`](#tone) | yes | `neutral`, `warm` or `cool`. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `settings.set_user_library`

**User Library**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Chooses the User Library's folder on the Settings window's Library page. `path` is an absolute path, or `null` for the default. The folder becomes the User Library at once: its starting folders (Clips, Defaults, Grooves, Presets, Samples, Tunings) are made in it if it has none, and it is indexed in the background. Nothing is moved from the folder before. Run by a person from the Browse button without a `path`, it asks for a folder. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `path` is the User Library in use afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string or null | no | The folder's absolute path, or `null` for the default: a `User Library` folder in a Beatlayer folder in the Music folder (the Documents folder on Windows). |

Result: [`UserLibraryResult`](#userlibraryresult).

#### `settings.set_warp_recorded_audio`

**Warp Recorded Audio**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `settings`.

Switches Warp recorded audio, on the Settings window's Record, Warp & Launch page, a Beatlayer addition (IMP-02); it's on in a new install, as Live warps its recordings. Clips have no warp settings yet, so for now recorded clips play at their file's own speed whether it's on or off; warping will read the setting for the clips a recording makes. The setting is kept for the next start, and isn't part of the set or an undo step. The result's `on` is the setting afterwards.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting is on. |

Result: [`SwitchResult`](#switchresult).

#### `settings.state`

**Settings State**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports every preference the Settings window shows with a value, by page, in the form its own command takes it: Theme & Colors (`settings.set_theme`), Display & Input (zoom, Outline View in Focus, the Tab key settings), the audio device settings with Driver Error Compensation and the test tone (`audio.configure`, `audio.set_test_tone`), the MIDI ports and computer keyboard (`midi.set_port`), Create Fades on Clip Edges, Warp Recorded Audio, the Launch section, the automation recording mode (`settings.set_automation_record_mode`), the File & Folder page's Temporary Folder, sample editor and Save Continuously (`settings.set_temporary_folder`, `settings.set_sample_editor` and `settings.set_continuous_save`), Auto-Hide Plug-In Windows, the plug-ins the Browser hides and prefers (`plugin.settings`), the agent server and the assistant. The server's and the agents' tokens and the assistant's API key are never reported, only whether one is stored. Preferences aren't saved with the set. Changes nothing. Use it to check a `settings.set_*` command took effect.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`SettingsState`](#settingsstate).

### Area `slot`

#### `slot.set_stop_button`

**Add Stop Button**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `session`.

Adds or removes a Session slot's Clip Stop button, which the person reaches through Edit ▸ Remove Stop Button (Cmd+E on macOS, Ctrl+E on Windows) and the slot's and Session clip's context menus. The button stops the track's playing clip; the track's own stop button (its status row) and Stop All Clips do the same for one or every track. A slot has one until it's removed, so a set saved before this command loads with one in every slot of every audio and MIDI track. The switch is saved with the set, and undo adds or removes the button again.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-SES-005 | `Cmd+E` | `Ctrl+E` | `session` | Add or remove a clip stop button | toggles `stop_button` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track whose slot it is. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) | yes | The scene whose slot it is. |
| `stop_button` | boolean | yes | Whether the slot keeps its Clip Stop button: `true` adds it, and `false` removes it. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `song`

#### `song.add_locator`

**Add Locator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Adds a locator at a position, as the Set Locator button and Add Locator do. A locator with no name of its own is named with the next whole number. Two locators never share a position: adding one where another is leaves that one as it is. One undo step, `Add Locator`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `locator` | [`Locator`](#locator) | yes | The locator, with a new ID. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.delete_locator`

**Delete Locator**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Deletes a locator, as the Delete Locator button and the Delete key do. A song start time on it goes with it. One undo step, `Delete Locator`. Because it removes the person's work, an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `locator` | [`LocatorId`](#locatorid) | yes | The locator. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.delete_tempo_breakpoint`

**Delete Tempo Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Deletes the tempo breakpoint at `at` from the Main track's Song Tempo envelope, joining its neighbours with a straight segment. The first breakpoint, at 1.1.1, can't be deleted; `at` there is refused. A position with no breakpoint is refused too.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the breakpoint is. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.delete_time`

**Delete Time**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Removes the span from `start` to `end` on every track, whichever tracks are selected, so what follows closes up: clips inside it are deleted, a clip across an edge is cut or split there (leave out `clips` and the part after a split gets a new ID), and every Arrangement clip, take-lane clip, automation breakpoint, tempo breakpoint, time-signature marker and locator at or after `end` moves earlier by the span's length. Markers and locators inside the span are deleted. The Session View's slots and the loop brace are left as they are. One undo step, `Delete Time`. Undo restores it, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first. To delete the time selected as a person does, use `arrangement.delete_time`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the span starts: 0 (1.1.1) or later. |
| `end` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where it ends, after `start`. |
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | no | One new ID for each clip the span lies inside, which the part after the split takes, in track order; left out, the editor issues them. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.delete_time_signature_change`

**Delete Time Signature Change**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Deletes the time-signature marker at `at`, so the signature before it runs on through that position. The first marker, at 1.1.1, can't be deleted; `at` there is refused. A position with no marker is refused too.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the marker is. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.insert_time`

**Insert Silence**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Opens `length` ticks of empty time at `at` on every track, whichever tracks are selected: a clip across `at` is split there (leave out `clips` and the part after the split gets a new ID), and every Arrangement clip, take-lane clip, automation breakpoint, tempo breakpoint, time-signature marker and locator at or after `at` moves later by `length`. Each envelope, the tempo and the signature hold across the new time the value they had at `at`. The Session View's slots and the loop brace are left as they are. One undo step, `Insert Silence`. To insert silence at the time selection as a person does, use `arrangement.insert_silence`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the time opens: 0 (1.1.1) or later. |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How much time opens; more than 0. |
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | no | One new ID for each clip the time opens inside, which the part after the split takes, in track order; left out, the editor issues them. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.loop_to_next_locator`

**Loop to Next Locator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Sets the Arrangement's loop brace from a locator to the next one and switches the loop on, as the locator's context menu does. The last locator has none after it, and is refused. One undo step, `Loop to Next Locator`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `locator` | [`LocatorId`](#locatorid) | yes | The locator. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.move_locator`

**Move Locator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves a locator to a new position, as dragging it does. A locator can't go before 1.1.1, and a move that would put two locators at one position changes nothing. One undo step, `Move Locator`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `locator` | [`LocatorId`](#locatorid) | yes | The locator. |
| `to` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where it goes: 0 (1.1.1) or later, and not where another locator already is. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.move_tempo_breakpoint`

**Move Tempo Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves the tempo breakpoint at `at` to `to`, keeping its tempo, as dragging one along the Main track's Song Tempo envelope does. Both are tick positions, `to` is 0 (1.1.1) or later, and it mustn't land on another breakpoint. The first breakpoint, at 1.1.1, can't move; `at` there is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the breakpoint is now. |
| `to` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where it goes: 0 (1.1.1) or later, and not where another breakpoint already is. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.move_time_signature_change`

**Move Time Signature Change**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Moves the time-signature marker at `at` to `to`, as dragging it along the arrangement's time-signature lane does. Both are tick positions, `to` is 0 (1.1.1) or later, and it mustn't land on another marker. The first marker, at 1.1.1, can't move; `at` there is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the marker is now. |
| `to` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where it goes: 0 (1.1.1) or later, and not where another marker already is. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.rename_locator`

**Rename Locator**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Renames a locator, as Cmd-R (Ctrl-R) and Edit > Rename do. An empty name keeps the old one. One undo step, `Rename Locator`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `locator` | [`LocatorId`](#locatorid) | yes | The locator. |
| `name` | string | yes | The new name. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.scales`

**Scale List**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports the scale list: every scale a set can use, in the order the Scale Name chooser shows them, with each scale's steps above the root in semitones. The names are the ones `clip.set_scale` and `song.set_scale` take. Changes nothing. Use it to read the scales a set has before setting one.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ScaleList`](#scalelist).

#### `song.set_locator_info_text`

**Set Locator Info Text**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Sets the info text of a locator, which the Info View shows while the pointer is over it. One undo step, `Edit Info Text`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `locator` | [`LocatorId`](#locatorid) | yes | The locator. |
| `info_text` | string | yes | The new info text. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.set_lock_envelopes`

**Lock Envelopes**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Lock Envelopes, the switch above the track headers and the Options menu item. Off (the default in a new set), editing the Arrangement's clips carries their tracks' envelopes over the clips' spans with them: moving, copying, cutting, deleting, duplicating and pasting clips take the envelopes over the same spans. On, the envelopes stay where they are in the song and the clips move on their own. The setting is saved with the set, and each change is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether the envelopes stay where they are. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.set_scale`

**Set Scale**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the set's current scale: whether its Scale Mode is on (`enabled`), its root note (`root`, 0 is C and 11 is B) and its scale (`name`, one of the names `song.scales` reads). It leaves the values it isn't given as they were. The current scale is what the Control Bar's scale controls show, what the clips made next take, and what a device or a tool reads where no clip plays. It is one undo step, named "Change Scale", and the set is saved with it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean or null | no | Whether the set's Scale Mode is on. |
| `name` | string or null | no | The scale's name, from the scale list. |
| `root` | integer or null | no | The root note: 0 (C) to 11 (B). |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.set_start`

**Set Song Start Time**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Sets where the song starts: at a locator, or at the loop brace's start. Choosing it where it is set clears it, so the song starts at the insert marker again. While it is set, Play starts the song there instead of at the insert marker. One undo step, `Set Song Start Time`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | [`SongStart`](#songstart) or null | no | Where the song starts; nothing clears it. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.set_start_time`

**Set Song Start Time**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Sets where the song starts: at a locator, or at the loop brace's start, as Set Song Start Time Here does. The song start time follows its locator or the brace as they move, and deleting the locator clears it. `null` clears it, so the song starts at the insert marker again. While it is set, Play starts the song there instead of at the insert marker.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clear` | boolean | no | Whether the song start time is cleared, so the song starts at the insert marker again. |
| `locator` | [`LocatorId`](#locatorid) or null | no | The locator the song starts at. Left out, the selected one: the song starts there, or stops starting there if it already does. |
| `loop_brace` | boolean | no | Whether the song starts at the loop brace's start. |

Result: [`LocatorResult`](#locatorresult).

#### `song.set_tempo`

**Set Tempo**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Replaces the song's tempo map. To give the whole song one tempo, send a single constant segment at tick 0; add segments to change or ramp the tempo at given positions. Tempos are quarter notes per minute, from 1 to 1,000. Clips and notes keep their positions in ticks, so a new tempo changes when they sound, not where they sit in bars.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tempo` | [`TempoMap`](#tempomap) | yes | The new tempo map. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.set_tempo_breakpoint`

**Set Tempo Breakpoint**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the tempo at `at` on the Main track's Song Tempo envelope, adding a breakpoint there or replacing the one that's there, as dragging a breakpoint does. Tempos are quarter notes per minute, from 1 to 1,000, and `at` is 0 (1.1.1) or later. A breakpoint between two others splits the segment there, keeping the neighbours. Clips and notes keep their positions in ticks, so a new tempo changes when they sound, not where they sit in bars. Use `song.set_tempo` to replace the whole map at once.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the breakpoint sits: 0 (1.1.1) or later. |
| `bpm` | [`Bpm`](#bpm) | yes | The tempo there, as quarter notes per minute. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.set_time_signature_change`

**Set Time Signature Change**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Sets the time-signature marker at `at` to `signature`, adding one when there's none, as Create > Insert Time Signature Change and the marker's numerator and denominator fields do. The marker sits anywhere at 0 (1.1.1) or later and always starts a new bar there, so a change before the previous bar is full cuts it short. Numerators run 1 to 99 and denominators are 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16. Use `song.set_time_signatures` to replace the whole map.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the marker sits: 0 (1.1.1) or later. |
| `signature` | [`TimeSignature`](#timesignature) | yes | The signature from there on. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.set_time_signatures`

**Set Time Signatures**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Replaces the song's time-signature map. To give the whole song one meter, send a single change at tick 0, such as 4/4; add changes to switch meter at given positions, each of which starts a new bar. Numerators run from 1 to 99 and denominators are 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16. It changes how positions are counted in bars and beats, not where clips sit in ticks.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `time_signatures` | [`TimeSignatureMap`](#timesignaturemap) | yes | The new time-signature map. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `song.unfollow_tempo_automation`

**Unfollow Tempo Automation**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Makes every clip that leads the tempo a follower and writes the tempo they set into the Main track's Song Tempo envelope as ordinary breakpoints, so the song plays exactly as it did and the envelope becomes editable. One undo step, and changes nothing when no clip leads.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `stems`

#### `stems.cancel`

**Cancel**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Stops the package download or the separation under way. A cancelled separation changes nothing in the set; a cancelled download keeps the packages it finished.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`StemsStatus`](#stemsstatus).

#### `stems.close`

**Close Separate Stems**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Closes the Separate Stems dialog. A download or separation under way goes on; `stems.cancel` stops it. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`StemsStatus`](#stemsstatus).

#### `stems.install`

**Download Required Packages Now**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Downloads and installs the open-source packages stem separation needs, ONNX Runtime and the Demucs model (about 350 MB together), into Beatlayer's application-data folder, checking each file's SHA-256. Returns at once; `stems.status` reports the progress. Installed packages aren't downloaded again. Changes nothing in the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`StemsStatus`](#stemsstatus).

#### `stems.open`

**Separate Stems to New Audio Tracks**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Opens the Separate Stems dialog for an audio clip in the Arrangement (`clip`, or the selected clip). The first time, the dialog lists the packages stem separation needs (ONNX Runtime and the Demucs model), their sizes and where they install, with Download Required Packages Now and Cancel; once they're installed it offers Vocals, Drums, Bass and Others, High Speed or High Quality, and Separate. Changes nothing in the set: an agent calls `stems.separate` instead.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The audio clip to separate; the selected clip if left out. |

Result: [`StemsStatus`](#stemsstatus).

#### `stems.separate`

**Separate Stems**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Separates an audio clip in the Arrangement into stems on new audio tracks, with a Demucs network running on this computer. `stems` chooses the parts (`vocals`, `drums`, `bass`, `others`; all four if left out); `quality` is `high_speed` (one pass) or `high_quality` (two passes averaged, about twice as long); `merge` puts two or three parts together on one track. The audio between the clip's Start and End markers, or through its loop, is separated at 44.1 kHz and written to the project's Samples/Processed/Stems folder. Each part gets a track below the clip's track, inside a new group track when there's more than one, with a copy of the clip playing that part; the original clip is deactivated. Playback stops first. Returns at once; `stems.status` reports the progress and the new tracks, and the whole edit is one undo step. Needs the packages `stems.install` downloads.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The audio clip in the Arrangement to separate. |
| `merge` | boolean | no | Put the chosen parts together on one track: only with two or three parts. |
| `quality` | [`StemQuality`](#stemquality) | no | `high_speed` (the default) or `high_quality`. |
| `stems` | array of [`StemKind`](#stemkind) | no | Which parts to put on new tracks, one or more; all four if left out. |

Result: [`StemsStatus`](#stemsstatus).

#### `stems.status`

**Stem Separation Status**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reads stem separation's state: whether its packages are installed (and each package's name, version, project page and download size), where they install, the download's progress, the separation's progress, the tracks the last separation made, and the dialog if it's open.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`StemsStatus`](#stemsstatus).

### Area `take_lane`

#### `take_lane.audition`

**Audition Take Lane**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `take-lanes`.

Switches the audition of the take `lanes` (left out, the take lanes the selection is on: the headers, the time selection or the clips selected are on them) on or off, one lane for each track: of the lanes listed on one track, the last. Left without `on`, it switches them on, or off when each is auditioned already. While a take lane is auditioned its track plays it in place of its main lane (`take_lane.set_audition`). One undo step, `Audition Take Lane`. T runs it.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-COMP-003 | `T` | `T` | `take-lanes` | Audition the selected take lane | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lanes` | array or null | no | The take lanes to audition; of those on one track, the last listed is the one. Left out, the take lanes the selection is on. |
| `on` | boolean or null | no | Switch them on (true) or off (false). Left out, they switch on, or off when every one of them is auditioned already. |

Result: [`LanesResult`](#lanesresult).

#### `take_lane.comp_sources`

**Comp Sources**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Reports which take-lane material a track's main lane uses: a main-lane clip uses a take-lane clip over the stretch where both lie when they play the same thing there, the same data apart from the Start and End markers, the loop brace and the fades, with the same clip envelopes and the same contents at every point. A deactivated main-lane clip uses nothing. `stretches` lists each, and `unused_lanes` the take lanes none of whose material is used, which `take_lane.delete_unused` deletes.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The audio or MIDI track. |

Result: [`CompSourcesResult`](#compsourcesresult).

#### `take_lane.copy_to_main_lane`

**Copy Selection to Main Lane**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `take-lanes`.

Copies a take lane's material in `start`..`end` to its track's main lane, at the same place (with `lanes`, `start` and `end` left out, it takes them from the selection: the take lanes the headers, the time selection or the clips selected are on, and the time or the clips' span; Enter runs it so): each of the lane's clips the range reaches, cut at the range's edges as Split cuts, is copied under a new ID onto the main lane, where it replaces what it covers. Where the lane has no clip in the range, the main lane is left as it was. Of several `lanes` on one track, the last listed is copied from; lanes on several tracks each copy to their own track. The copies are independent of the take-lane clips. It is one undo step, an edit, and destructive as well when it replaces or shortens a main-lane clip. A frozen track refuses it.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-COMP-002 | `Enter` | `Enter` | `take-lanes` | Copy the selected take-lane area to the main lane | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the range ends, after `start`. Left out, the selection's end. |
| `lanes` | array or null | no | The take lanes to copy from. Of those on one track, the last listed is copied from. Left out, the take lanes the selection is on: the headers selected, the lanes the time selection covers, or the lanes of the selected clips. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the range starts, in ticks or as `bar.beat.sixteenth` text. Left out, the time selection's start, or the selected clips'. |

Result: [`CompResult`](#compresult).

#### `take_lane.create_clip`

**Create Clip on Take Lane**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Puts a new clip on a take lane, at `clip.start` for `clip.length` ticks (705,600 to the quarter note), as `clip.create` puts one on a main lane: an audio clip on an audio track's lane and a MIDI clip on a MIDI track's. `clip.id` must be a new ID the project has issued for it. It does not clear what the lane holds there. The clip is then edited by its ID with the `clip.*` commands, as a main-lane clip is.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lane` | [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) | yes | The take lane. |
| `clip` | [`Clip`](#clip) | yes | The clip, with a new ID. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `take_lane.delete`

**Delete Take Lane(s)**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Deletes take lanes with their clips. The main lane is left as it was, and a deleted lane that was auditioned stops being. Undo restores them, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lanes` | array of [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) | yes | The take lanes. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `take_lane.delete_all`

**Delete All Take Lanes**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Deletes every take lane of each of the audio or MIDI `tracks`, with their clips. The main lane is left as it was. Undo restores them, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracks` | array of [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The audio or MIDI tracks. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `take_lane.delete_unused`

**Delete All Unused Take Lanes**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Deletes each of the audio or MIDI `tracks`' take lanes none of whose material the main lane uses: a main-lane clip uses a take-lane clip over the stretch where both lie when they play the same thing there (`take_lane.comp_sources` lists what is used). The main lane is left as it was. Undo restores them, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracks` | array of [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The audio or MIDI tracks. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `take_lane.duplicate`

**Duplicate Take Lane(s)**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `take-lanes`.

Puts a copy of each of the take `lanes` (left out, the take lanes whose headers are selected) directly after it, with its name and a copy of each of its clips under a new ID, in one undo step, and selects the copies. The result's `lanes` are the copies' IDs.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-COMP-005 | `Cmd+D` | `Ctrl+D` | `take-lanes` | Duplicate the selected take lane | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lanes` | array or null | no | The take lanes to copy. Left out, the take lanes whose headers are selected. |

Result: [`LanesResult`](#lanesresult).

#### `take_lane.insert`

**Insert Take Lane**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Adds an empty take lane to each of the audio or MIDI `tracks` (left out, the selected tracks): directly after the take lane of that track listed in `after` (left out, the take lanes whose headers are selected), or after its last take lane. Each is named `Take N`, one more than the highest number of a lane of the track named `Take` and a number, `Take 1` on a track with none. All of them are one undo step. The tracks' take lanes show afterwards, and Automation Mode is switched off to show them. The result's `lanes` are the new lanes' IDs.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-COMP-004 | `Shift+Option+T` | `Shift+Alt+T` | `arrangement` | Add a take lane | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `after` | array of [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) | no | Take lanes to add the new ones directly after, for the tracks they belong to. A track with none of them gets its new lane after its last take lane. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The audio or MIDI tracks to add a take lane to. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`LanesResult`](#lanesresult).

#### `take_lane.move`

**Move Take Lane(s)**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves take lanes, which must all be on one track, to a new place among that track's take lanes, keeping their order: `index` counts from 0, the lane nearest the main lane, among the lanes that are not moved. The main lane stays first.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lanes` | array of [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) | yes | The take lanes. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The place they take among the track's other take lanes, counted from 0 for the lane nearest the main lane. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `take_lane.move_comp_edge`

**Move Comp Edge**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Moves the boundary between two adjacent main-lane clips that each play a take-lane clip (`take_lane.comp_sources`) from `from` to `to`: the earlier clip's right edge and the later clip's left edge move together, each playing on what its take-lane clip plays there. The boundary goes no further than the growing clip's take-lane clip reaches, and leaves each clip at least a tick long. It is one undo step.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The audio or MIDI track. |
| `from` | [`Position`](#position) | yes | Where two adjacent main-lane clips meet now. |
| `to` | [`Position`](#position) | yes | Where they should meet. |

Result: [`CompResult`](#compresult).

#### `take_lane.rename`

**Rename Take Lane**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Gives a take lane a new name. An empty name is refused.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lane` | [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) | yes | The take lane. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its new name, which can't be empty. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `take_lane.replace_with_take`

**Replace with Next or Previous Take**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Replaces a track's main-lane material in `start`..`end` with the next take's (`direction` `next`, the take lane below) or the previous take's (`previous`, the one above). With `track`, `start`, `end` and `lane` left out it takes them from the selection, on each audio or MIDI track the selection is on, as Cmd+Down and Cmd+Up do. The take is placed as `take_lane.copy_to_main_lane` places it, skipping take lanes with no clip in the range. With `lane` given, the selection is on that take lane and the next or previous take is counted from it; left out, the selection is on the main lane, and each main-lane clip's part of the range is counted from the take lane it uses (`take_lane.comp_sources`), a part that uses none from before the first take lane. A part with no take lane left in that direction is left as it was. It is one undo step, an edit, and destructive as well when it replaces or shortens a main-lane clip. A frozen track refuses it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | [`TakeDirection`](#takedirection) | yes | Whether to take the next or the previous take. |
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the range ends, after `start`. Left out, the selection's end. |
| `lane` | [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) or null | no | The take lane the selection is on, from which the next or previous take is counted. Left out with `track` given, the selection is on the main lane, and each of its clips counts from the take lane it uses; left out with `track`, the selection says. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the range starts, in ticks or as `bar.beat.sixteenth` text. Left out, the time selection's start, or the selected clips'. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The audio or MIDI track whose main lane is changed. Left out, each audio or MIDI track the selection is on. |

Result: [`CompResult`](#compresult).

#### `take_lane.set_audition`

**Audition Take Lane**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Switches the audition of a take lane on or off. While a take lane is auditioned, its track plays that lane's clips in place of its main lane's, from the next block; a track has at most one, so switching one on switches off the one auditioned before. Session clips are unaffected. It is saved with the set.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lane` | [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) | yes | The take lane. |
| `on` | boolean | yes | Whether it is auditioned. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

### Area `track`

#### `track.add_take_lane`

**Add Take Lane**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`.

Adds a take lane under an audio or MIDI track's main lane, after the lanes it has, or at `index` among them (0 is the lane nearest the main lane). `lane.name` names it and `lane.clips` are the clips it holds, each with a `name`, a `start` and `length` in ticks (705,600 to the quarter note), and `data`: audio as `clip.create` takes it, or tagged `audio` or `midi`. The lane and its clips are given IDs when `id` is left out. A lane holds clips of its track's kind. The track plays only its main lane, or the take lane that is auditioned in its place (`take_lane.set_audition`); recording adds a lane for every take and copies the latest to the main lane. Read the lanes back with the query tool's `track` `take_lanes`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The audio or MIDI track. |
| `lane` | [`NewTakeLane`](#newtakelane) | yes | The lane and its clips. |
| `index` | integer or null | no | Where among the track's take lanes the new one goes, counted from 0 for the lane nearest the main lane. Left out, after the last. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `track.bounce_in_place`

**Bounce Track in Place**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `session`, `track-headers`.

Renders the selected tracks to audio and replaces each with an audio track holding it: no devices, the track's name with " (Bounce)" after it, its volume, pan, sends, activator, solo, output routing, and mixer automation, and its clips playing the bounced audio. `tracks` names them (left out, the selected tracks). A group is bounced as one track, after its mixer. The files go into Samples/Processed/Bounce. It is destructive, since it deletes the track's devices and clips, and undoing it gives the source track back exactly.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channels` | [`Channels`](#channels) | no | How many channels the bounced files hold. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks to bounce. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`BounceResult`](#bounceresult).

#### `track.bounce_to_new_track`

**Bounce to New Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `session`, `track-headers`.

Renders the selected clips, or the time selection on the selected tracks, to audio on a new track directly after each source track, and switches the source material off. `tracks` names the source tracks (left out, the selected ones), `clips` the clips to bounce (left out, the selected clips, or the time selection), and `start` and `end` the time selection. The new track takes its source's name with " (Bounce)" after it, its colour, and its mixer settings, and the files go into Samples/Processed/Bounce. It is an edit.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-BOUNCE-001 | `Cmd+B` | `Ctrl+B` | `global` | Bounce the selection to a new audio track | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channels` | [`Channels`](#channels) | no | How many channels the bounced files hold. |
| `clips` | array or null | no | The clips to bounce. Left out, the selected clips, or the time selection on the tracks. |
| `end` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the time selection ends. Left out, the Arrangement's time selection. |
| `start` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the time selection starts. Left out, the Arrangement's time selection. |
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks to bounce. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`BounceResult`](#bounceresult).

Plays tracks through their devices and clips again, dropping their frozen audio and restoring the clip data the freeze kept. `tracks` names them. `track.unfreeze` is the command a person and an agent run.

#### `track.create`

**Insert Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Creates an empty track: audio (holds audio clips), MIDI (holds MIDI clips), group (holds other tracks), or return (receives sends). It starts at unity volume and centre pan, with no devices or clips. Audio, MIDI, and group tracks go at `index` among the top-level tracks, or inside the group `parent`; return tracks go at `index` among the returns. `id` must be a new ID the project has issued for it. The Main track always exists and can't be created.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-001 | `Cmd+T` | `Ctrl+T` | `global` | Insert an audio track | fixes `kind` = `"audio"` |
| S-TRACK-002 | `Cmd+Shift+T` | `Ctrl+Shift+T` | `global` | Insert a MIDI track | fixes `kind` = `"midi"` |
| S-TRACK-003 | `Cmd+Option+T` | `Ctrl+Alt+T` | `global` | Insert a return track | fixes `kind` = `"return"` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The new track's ID. |
| `kind` | [`TrackKind`](#trackkind) | yes | Its kind. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its name. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in its list, from 0 to the list's length. |
| `parent` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The group to put it in, or `null` (or nothing) for the top level. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `track.create_bounced_track`

**Create Bounced Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`, `arrangement`, `session`.

Makes a new audio track directly after the track that was bounced, holding the bounced audio. `bounced` is what the new track holds. `track.bounce_to_new_track` is the command a person and an agent run: it renders the file and applies this one. #### `track.delete`

**Delete Track**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `track-headers`.

Deletes a track with its clips and devices. Deleting a group track also deletes every track inside it. Use it to remove a track the song no longer needs; to silence a track and keep it, use `mixer.set_mute`. Undo restores everything it deleted, but because it removes the person's work an agent asks first. The Main track can't be deleted.

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

#### `track.duplicate`

**Duplicate Track(s)**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`.

Duplicates the selected tracks (`tracks`, or the tracks named), each straight after itself, with everything it holds: its name (the next number where the name starts with the track's number), colour, mixer, sends, routing, devices with their states and sidechains, its Arrangement clips, take lanes and Session clips, its automation and clip envelopes, and its frozen state, all under new IDs. A reference between tracks copied together points at the copies; a reference to a track not copied stays as it is. The copies become the selected tracks. One undo step, named Duplicate Track(s). Main can't be duplicated.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-EDIT-004 | `Cmd+D` | `Ctrl+D` | `global` | Duplicate | runs it |

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks; the selected tracks if left out. |

Result: [`TracksDuplicated`](#tracksduplicated).

#### `track.duplicate_without_clips`

**Duplicate Track Without Clips**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`, `session`, `track-headers`.

Duplicates tracks (`tracks`, or the selected tracks) without their clips or arrangement automation: each copy goes straight after its track, with its name (the next number where the name starts with the track's number), mixer settings, sends, routing, and devices with their settings, and the copies become the selected tracks. A group's copy holds copies of its tracks, without clips. Use it to start a new part with a track's sound. One undo step, named Duplicate Track(s) Without Clips. Main can't be duplicated.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks; the selected tracks if left out. |

Result: [`TracksDuplicated`](#tracksduplicated).

#### `track.freeze`

**Freeze Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `session`, `track-headers`.

Renders the selected tracks to audio and plays that instead of their devices: an audio or MIDI track's Arrangement from 1.1.1 to the end of its last tail, and each Session clip on its own, taken after the devices and before the mixer. `tracks` names them (left out, the selected tracks). A group renders its tracks through their mixers and devices and, for each return they send to, the sum of those sends; a return renders from 1.1.1 to the end of the set. The track keeps its mixer, and its clips keep their places; its devices and clip settings are locked while frozen. The freeze runs offline through the processed-file writer, one undo step when every file is whole. It's an edit.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-017 | `Cmd+Option+Shift+F` | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F` | `track-headers` | Freeze or unfreeze the selected tracks | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks to freeze or unfreeze. Left out, the selected tracks. |

Result: [`FreezeResult`](#freezeresult).

#### `track.group`

**Group Tracks**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`, `session`, `track-headers`.

Groups tracks (`tracks`, or the selected tracks): inserts a group track named "Group" where the first track was, moves the tracks into it in order, routes each member to the group and the group to Main, leaves the group unfolded, and selects it. One undo step, named Group Tracks.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRACK-006 | `Cmd+G` | `Ctrl+G` | `track-headers` | Group the selected tracks | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tracks` | array or null | no | The tracks to group; the selected tracks if left out. |

Result: [`TracksGrouped`](#tracksgrouped).

#### `track.move`

**Move Track**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`.

Moves a track to `index` in the top-level track list, or inside the group `parent`. A return track moves among the returns. The index counts positions after the track is taken out of its current place, so moving a track down past its neighbour is its current index plus one. Use it to reorder tracks or to put tracks into or out of groups. A group can't go inside itself, and the Main track can't be moved.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The track. |
| `index` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Where it goes in that list. |
| `parent` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The group to move it into, or `null` (or nothing) for the top level. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `track.paste`

**Paste Track(s)**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `track-headers`.

Pastes the tracks on the clipboard, with everything they hold under new IDs, straight after the last selected track, at its level and inside its group when it is in one, or after the last track when none is selected. Each paste makes new copies, and the tracks pasted are selected afterwards. One undo step, named Paste Track(s). References to tracks that are not in the set are settled as a set added from another set settles them. The files the tracks play go into the set's media table. With the Arrangement's material on the clipboard it is unavailable: that is pasted with `arrangement.paste`.

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track to paste after; the last selected track if left out. |

Result: [`TracksCopied`](#trackscopied).

#### `track.paste_bounced_audio`

**Paste Bounced Audio**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `arrangement`, `session`, `track-headers`.

Renders what Copy last put on the clipboard as it is at the moment of pasting, and places it as Paste places clips: on the track, or in the slot, named. The destination is an audio track, an empty MIDI track, which becomes an audio track, or a take lane. The audio replaces what it covers. With nothing copied, or with the copied source deleted, the command is unavailable. It is an edit, and destructive when it would replace or shorten a clip.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-BOUNCE-002 | `Cmd+Option+V` | `Ctrl+Alt+V` | `arrangement` | Paste bounced audio into the lane or slot | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `at` | [`Position`](#position) or null | no | Where the audio goes in the Arrangement. Left out, the time selection's start, or the insert marker. |
| `channels` | [`Channels`](#channels) | no | How many channels the pasted file holds. |
| `lane` | [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) or null | no | The take lane to paste onto, of an audio track. The first source's audio goes on it, and each later source's on the take lane at the same place among the take lanes of the track it lands on, a lane being added where the track has none there. Left out, the main lane. |
| `scene` | [`SceneId`](#sceneid) or null | no | The Session slot to paste into. Left out, the Arrangement. |
| `track` | [`TrackId`](#trackid) or null | no | The track to paste onto. Left out, the selected track. |

Result: [`BounceResult`](#bounceresult).

#### `transport.continue`

**Continue Playback**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRANS-002 | `Shift+Space` | `Shift+Space` | `global` | Continue playing from where playback stopped | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.insert_marker_to_playhead`

**Move Insert Marker To Playhead**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Moves the insert marker to the playhead: where the song is playing now, or where playback stopped. Use it to start again later from the current point. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-033 | `Cmd+Shift+Space` | `Ctrl+Shift+Space` | `arrangement` | Move the insert marker to the play position | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

#### `transport.locate`

**Set Arrangement Position**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves the insert marker, where playback starts, to `position`, in ticks from the start of the arrangement (705,600 to the quarter note, so bar 2 of a 4/4 song is 2,822,400), as typing into the Control Bar's Arrangement Position fields does. While the song plays, playback jumps there at once; while it's stopped, `transport.continue` still resumes where playback stopped. With `quantized` set, the jump waits while the song plays for the next line of the global launch quantisation and lands on that line's exact frame, as a locator's jump and a click in the scrub area do (the transport spec, R22); with the quantisation off or None, it jumps at once. Position 0 returns to 1.1.1, as the Home key and Return Play Position to 1.1.1 do. A position before 0 is taken as 0. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRANS-005 | `Home`, `Fn+Left` | `Home` | `global` | Move the insert marker to the start | fixes `position` = `0` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | The new insert marker, in ticks from 1.1.1. A position before 1.1.1 is taken as 1.1.1. |
| `quantized` | boolean | no | Whether the jump waits for the next line of the global launch quantisation while the song plays, as a locator's jump and a click in the scrub area do (the transport spec, R22). With it off, or with the quantisation off or None, the jump happens at once. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.play`

**Play**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Starts playback from the insert marker, as the Control Bar's Play button does; while the song plays, starts it again from the insert marker. When the song has a song start time (the transport spec, R21), it starts from that instead and leaves the insert marker where it is. Set the insert marker first with `transport.locate`. With the Arrangement loop on, playback that reaches the loop's end goes on from its start. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.play_from_insert_marker`

**Play From Insert Marker**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Starts playback from the insert marker, even when the song has a song start time (the transport spec, R21). Until the arrangement has time selections, this does what `transport.play` does. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-ARR-032 | `Option+Space` | `Ctrl+Space` | `arrangement` | Play from the insert marker in the selected clip | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.play_stop`

**Play/Stop**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Stops playback if the song is playing, and otherwise starts it from the insert marker: the space bar, and the Playback menu's Play item, which reads Stop while the song plays. Unlike `transport.stop`, it never returns to 1.1.1. An agent that knows what it wants should use `transport.play` or `transport.stop` instead.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRANS-001 | `Space` | `Space` | `global` | Play from the start marker, or stop | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.return_to_start`

**Return Play Position to 1.1.1**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Moves the insert marker, where playback starts, back to the start of the arrangement (1.1.1), as the Playback menu's Return Play Position to 1.1.1 does. While the song plays, playback jumps there at once; while it's stopped, `transport.continue` still resumes where playback stopped. The same as `transport.locate` at position 0, which the Home key runs. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.set_loop`

**Set Loop Brace**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Moves the Arrangement loop brace to start at `start` and run for `length` ticks (705,600 to the quarter note; a 4/4 bar is 2,822,400), as the Control Bar's Loop Start and Loop Length fields do. It doesn't switch the loop on or off: use `transport.set_loop_enabled` for that. While the loop is on, playback that reaches the brace's end jumps back to its start; playback that starts at or after the end plays on. The start must be 0 (1.1.1) or later and the length more than 0. The brace is saved with the set, and undo moves it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the loop starts: 0 (1.1.1) or later. |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How long it is: more than 0. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_loop_enabled`

**Arrangement Loop On/Off**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`, `arrangement`.

Switches the Arrangement loop on or off, as the Control Bar's Loop switch does, leaving the brace where it is. With it on, playback that reaches the brace's end jumps back to its start, on the exact sample, until it's switched off or playback stops. Use `transport.set_loop` to move the brace first. The switch is saved with the set, and undo switches it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether playback loops between the brace's start and end. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_metronome_count_in`

**Metronome Count-In**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the metronome count-in length: `none`, `1_bar`, `2_bars`, or `4_bars`. When enabled, starting playback or recording plays the chosen bars of metronome clicks before the transport moves. The setting is saved with the set, and undo restores it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count_in` | [`CountIn`](#countin) | yes | The count-in duration in bars: none, 1 bar, 2 bars, or 4 bars. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_metronome_enabled`

**Metronome**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches the metronome on or off, as the Control Bar's Metronome switch and the Playback menu's Metronome item do. When on, the metronome clicks on each beat of the song, with the downbeat accented. The switch is saved with the set, and undo switches it back.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-TRANS-011 | `O` | `O` | `global` | Turn the metronome on or off | toggles `enabled` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether the metronome clicks during playback. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_metronome_only_while_recording`

**Hear Metronome Only While Recording**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches whether the metronome clicks only while recording or during playback as well, as the Playback menu and Metronome Settings menu do. The setting is saved with the set, and undo switches it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `only_while_recording` | boolean | yes | When on, clicks only sound while recording. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_metronome_rhythm`

**Metronome Rhythm**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the rhythmic division the metronome clicks at: `auto` (follows the time signature's denominator), `1_bar`, `1/2`, `1/2t`, `1/4`, `1/4t`, `1/8`, `1/8t`, `1/16`, or `1/16t`. If a division exceeds the bar length under the current time signature, clicks follow the auto interval. The setting is saved with the set, and undo restores it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rhythm` | [`MetronomeRhythm`](#metronomerhythm) | yes | The rhythm division. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_metronome_sound`

**Metronome Sound**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Chooses the metronome's sound character: `classic`, `click`, or `wood`. All sounds are synthesized in code. The setting is saved with the set, and undo restores it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sound` | [`MetronomeSound`](#metronomesound) | yes | The synthesised sound character. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_midi_overdub`

**MIDI Arrangement Overdub**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches MIDI Arrangement Overdub on or off, as the Control Bar's overdub switch does. With it on, notes recorded into the Arrangement merge into the MIDI clips already on the track instead of replacing them. The switch is saved with the set, and undo switches it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | When on, MIDI recorded into the Arrangement merges into the clips already there instead of replacing them. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_punch_in`

**Punch-In**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Punch-In on or off, as the Control Bar's Punch-In switch does. With it on, recording into the Arrangement starts at the Arrangement loop brace's start, whether or not the Loop switch is on: playback that starts before the brace records nothing until it reaches the brace, and playback that starts inside the brace records from where it starts. The metronome's "only while recording" setting sounds from the punch-in point. Use `transport.set_loop` to move the brace. The switch is saved with the set, and undo switches it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether recording starts at the brace's start. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_punch_out`

**Punch-Out**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Punch-Out on or off, as the Control Bar's Punch-Out switch does. With it on, recording into the Arrangement ends at the Arrangement loop brace's end, whether or not the Loop switch is on: the recording stops there, playback carries on, and Arrangement Record stays on but writes nothing more. Use `transport.set_loop` to move the brace. The switch is saved with the set, and undo switches it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether recording ends at the brace's end. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `transport.set_recording`

**Set Recording**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets whether the transport is recording: while it is, each armed audio track records its input into the project's Samples/Recorded/, each armed MIDI track records the notes it receives, and the recording becomes a clip on its track when it ends; a count-in starts it a bar or more later. With MIDI Arrangement Overdub on, recorded notes merge into the MIDI clips already there. Features like Hear Metronome Only While Recording follow it too. Recording captures input devices, including a microphone, so the person is asked first, whichever way you set it: to stop a recording without asking, run `transport.stop_recording`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recording` | boolean | yes | Whether the transport is recording. |

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.state`

**Transport Status**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports what the Control Bar's transport section shows: whether the song plays, the play position and the insert marker (in ticks from 1.1.1, and the Arrangement Position fields' bar.beat.sixteenth), the Arrangement loop's start, length, and switch, the tempo, and the time signature, the metronome, Arrangement Record and whether a take is running or the count-in is sounding, Punch-In and Punch-Out, MIDI Arrangement Overdub, Automation Arm and the mode an Arrangement recording writes control moves in, the recording under way (its armed tracks and dropped frames) and what the last recording came to, and whether the audio engine runs so the transport can play. Every `transport.set_*` setting reads back here. Changes nothing. Use it to check where the song is before and after `transport.play`, `transport.stop`, `transport.locate`, or `transport.set_loop`.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`TransportState`](#transportstate).

#### `transport.stop`

**Stop**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Stops playback, as the Control Bar's Stop button does, and keeps the position where it stopped, so `transport.continue` can resume there. Run it again while stopped to return the insert marker and the play position to the start of the arrangement (1.1.1), as pressing Stop twice does. It changes nothing in the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

#### `transport.stop_recording`

**Stop Recording**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Stops recording, the same as `transport.set_recording` with `recording` false, and without asking the person. The recording becomes a clip on its track; playback goes on. It does nothing when the transport isn't recording.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: nothing (`null`).

### Area `tuning`

#### `tuning.load`

**Load Tuning**. Permission: `external`. Contexts: `global`.

Reads a Scala `.scl` file, or an `.ascl` file read as one, and makes it the set's tuning in place of any other, as one undo step named "Load Tuning". The set keeps the tuning inside it. A file that holds no pitches, a count that doesn't match its lines, a ratio of 0 or less, or a pseudo-octave at or below the unison is refused with an error naming the problem, and the set's tuning stays as it was. The tuning is named after the file, without its extension, and takes the default reference pitch (octave 3, degree 0, 261.626 Hz) and the 128 notes that put degree 0 of that octave on key 60. With `retune` true, every note of the MIDI clips on tracks that play the tuning moves to the key whose new pitch is nearest the pitch it had; left out, `retune` follows Retune Set On Loading Tuning Systems. The result is the tuning, as `tuning.state` reads it. Reads a file outside the project.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | The `.scl` or `.ascl` file to read, absolute or relative to the app's working directory. The tuning is named after the file, without its extension. |
| `retune` | boolean or null | no | Whether every note of the MIDI clips on tracks that play the tuning moves to the key whose new pitch is nearest the pitch it had. Left out, it follows Retune Set On Loading Tuning Systems. |

Result: [`TuningState`](#tuningstate).

#### `tuning.remove`

**Remove Tuning**. Permission: `destructive`. Contexts: `global`.

Removes the set's tuning, which puts the set back to twelve equal steps. With `retune` true, every note of the MIDI clips on tracks that play the tuning moves to the key nearest the pitch it had under the tuning; with it false the notes keep their keys and may sound other pitches. Refused when the set has no tuning. It is one undo step, named "Remove Tuning", and undo brings the tuning back. `tuning.state` reads it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `retune` | boolean | no | Whether the notes are retuned. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `tuning.set`

**Set Tuning**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Makes a tuning, given whole (`tuning`: its name, description, the `cents` of its degrees above the unison with the pseudo-octave last, optional note `names` and `link`, its `reference` pitch and its `range` of notes), the set's tuning in place of any other. `tuning.load` makes one from a `.scl` or `.ascl` file instead. With `retune` true, every note of the MIDI clips on tracks that play the tuning moves to the key whose new pitch is nearest the pitch it had (the lower key on a tie; of two overlapping notes that land on one key the earlier is shortened, and of two that start together the shorter is deleted); with it false the notes keep their keys. A tuning that breaks the rules (no pitches, a pseudo-octave at or below the unison, a range of more than 128 notes) is refused and the set's tuning stays as it was. It is one undo step, named "Load Tuning", and the set is saved with the tuning inside it. `tuning.state` reads it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tuning` | [`Tuning`](#tuning) | yes | The tuning. |
| `retune` | boolean | no | Whether the notes are retuned. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `tuning.set_range`

**Set Tuning Range**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the set's tuning's note range: the `lowest` note, which key 0 plays, and the `highest`, each an `octave` and a `degree`. Given one, the other moves by as many notes, so the number of notes stays; given both, they are the range. A range of more than 128 notes, or one that starts above its end, is refused. Keys above the highest note play nothing. Refused when the set has no tuning. It is one undo step, named "Change Tuning Range". `tuning.state` reads it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `highest` | [`TuningNote`](#tuningnote) or null | no | The highest note. |
| `lowest` | [`TuningNote`](#tuningnote) or null | no | The lowest note. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `tuning.set_reference`

**Set Tuning Reference Pitch**. Permission: `edit`. Contexts: `global`.

Sets the set's tuning's reference pitch: an `octave`, a `degree` of the tuning and a `frequency` in Hz; a value left out stays as it was. Changing the octave or the degree only names another note as the reference: the frequency becomes that note's present frequency and nothing sounds different. Changing the frequency moves every pitch of the set by one ratio. Refused when the set has no tuning, for a degree the tuning doesn't have, or for a frequency that isn't above 0. It is one undo step, named "Change Reference Pitch". `tuning.state` reads it back.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `degree` | integer or null | no | The reference note's degree. |
| `frequency` | number or null | no | The reference note's frequency in Hz. |
| `octave` | integer or null | no | The reference note's octave. |

Result: [`ChangeSet`](#changeset).

#### `tuning.state`

**Tuning State**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Reports the set's tuning: its name, description, how many notes it holds to the pseudo-octave, the pitch of each in cents, the pseudo-octave's size, the note names and link where it has them, the reference pitch (octave, degree and frequency in Hz), the note range (the lowest note, which key 0 plays, and the highest) and the frequency of each key 0 to 127 (null for a key above the range, which plays nothing). `tuning` is null when the set plays twelve equal steps. Changes nothing. The commands that change the tuning read back through it.

Default keys: none.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`TuningState`](#tuningstate).

### Area `view`

#### `view.clip_envelope`

**Clip View Envelope**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `envelope`.

Chooses the parameter whose envelope the Clip View's Envelopes tab shows and edits, as its device and control choosers do: `target` is a control of the shown clip's track's mixer, one of its sends, or a parameter of a device in its chain, named as `clip.set_envelope_breakpoint` names it; `null` shows none. Changes only the view, so it's no undo step. Editing the envelope is done by the `clip.*envelope*` commands. The result says which parameter shows.

Default keys: none.

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) or null | no | The parameter of the shown clip's track whose envelope the Envelopes tab shows, or `null` to show none. |

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `view.clip_tab`

**Clip View Tab**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `note-editor`, `sample-editor`, `envelope`.

Chooses the tab the Clip View shows for its clip: `notes` (the MIDI Note Editor, Option+Shift+1) or `envelopes` (the clip's envelopes, Option+Shift+2). Left out, `tab` goes on to the next tab and round to the first after the last (Option+Tab). The Clip View shows the clip most recently selected, in the Arrangement or in a Session slot. Changes only the view, so it's no undo step and isn't saved with the set. The result says which tab shows.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-CLIPMODE-001 | `Option+Tab` | `Ctrl+Tab` | `sample-editor` | Switch between the Sample and Envelopes tabs | runs it |
| S-CLIPMODE-002 | `Option+Tab` | `Ctrl+Tab` | `note-editor` | Cycle the Notes, Envelopes and MPE tabs | runs it |
| S-CLIPMODE-003 | `Option+Shift+1` | `Alt+Shift+1` | `clip-view` | Show the Content Editor (the Sample or Notes tab) | fixes `tab` = `"notes"` |
| S-CLIPMODE-004 | `Option+Shift+2` | `Alt+Shift+2` | `clip-view` | Show the Envelope Editor (the Envelopes tab) | fixes `tab` = `"envelopes"` |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tab` | [`ClipTab`](#cliptab) or null | no | The tab to show. Left out, the Clip View goes on to the next one. |

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `view.close_plug_in_windows`

**Close All Plug-in Windows**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Closes every open plug-in editor window at once, as View ▸ Close All Plug-in Windows does. It closes editors only: floating native device windows stay as they are, so it changes nothing in the set, isn't an undo step, and is in the read class. It has no key. Returns how many editor windows it closed.

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

Result: [`ClosedPlugInWindows`](#closedpluginwindows).

#### `view.draw_mode`

**Draw Mode**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches Draw Mode (B; Options ▸ Draw Mode), which changes what a click in the MIDI Note Editor's note area does: with it on, clicking empty grid adds a note one grid step long, and clicking a note removes it; with it off, clicking selects. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step. The result says whether it's on.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-GRID-001 | `B` | `B` | `global` | Toggle Draw Mode | runs it |

Arguments: none (send `{}`).

#### `view.expand_clip_view`

**Expand Clip View**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`.

Gives the Clip View its largest height, the one that leaves the main view 80 points, and run again gives back the height it had before. Refused while the Clip View is hidden. Dragging the detail area's top edge, or hiding the Clip View, ends the expansion. Changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step. The result is the detail area's state, whose `expanded` says which way it went. With the second window open it acts on the window `window` names, `main` or `second`, and on the window with the focus without it.

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | [`WindowName`](#windowname) or null | no | The window to act on, `main` or `second`. Left out, the window with the focus. |

Result: [`DetailState`](#detailstate).

#### `view.fold_notes`

**Fold to Notes**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `clip-view`, `note-editor`.

Folds or unfolds the MIDI Note Editor (F, View ▸ Fold to Notes): while it's folded, the editor shows only the key rows that hold notes, one under the next, and not the empty rows between them. `clip` names the clip; left out, the one the editor shows. `folded` says which way; left out, it switches. Folding changes nothing in the set and isn't an undo step: it's saved with the set beside the song, so it's there again when the set is reopened. The result says whether the editor is folded now.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S-NOTE-038 | `F` | `F` | `note-editor` | Fold the editor to the key tracks that hold notes | runs it |

Arguments:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | no | The MIDI clip. Left out, the one the Clip View shows (the Arrangement's selected clip). |
| `folded` | boolean or null | no | Fold (true) or unfold (false); switches if left out. |

Result: [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate).

#### `view.full_screen`

**Full Screen**. Permission: `read`. Contexts: `global`.

Switches the main window into or out of full-screen mode. Changes nothing in the set. With the second window open it acts on the window `window` names, `main` or `second`, and on the window with the focus without it.

Default keys:

| Shortcut | macOS | Windows | Context | Action in the reference | Binding |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
