### `Position`

A position in the song: ticks (705,600 to the quarter note; 0 is 1.1.1, the start of the arrangement), or bars, beats, and sixteenths as text under the song's time signatures, such as "5", "5.3", or "5.3.2" (missing fields are 1). There's no bar 0: the bar before 1 is -1.

One of:

- [`Ticks`](#ticks)
- string matching `^\s*-?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+){0,2}\s*$`

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "anyOf": [
    {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks"
    },
    {
      "pattern": "^\\s*-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+){0,2}\\s*$",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ],
  "description": "A position in the song: ticks (705,600 to the quarter note; 0 is 1.1.1, the start of the arrangement), or bars, beats, and sixteenths as text under the song's time signatures, such as \"5\", \"5.3\", or \"5.3.2\" (missing fields are 1). There's no bar 0: the bar before 1 is -1."
}
```

</details>

### `Preserve`

What Beats keeps (R2): its transients, or the lines of a grid in the clip's own beats.

One of:

- `"transients"`: A segment at each transient; the default.
- `"1_bar"`: A segment at each bar.
- `"half"`: At each half note.
- `"quarter"`: At each quarter note.
- `"eighth"`: At each eighth note.
- `"sixteenth"`: At each sixteenth note.
- `"thirty_second"`: At each thirty-second note.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What Beats keeps (R2): its transients, or the lines of a grid in the clip's own beats.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "transients",
      "description": "A segment at each transient; the default.",
      "type": "string"
```

### `QuantizeSettings`

The Clip View's Quantize settings, as `clip_view.quantize_settings` reports them: what `note.quantize` uses when its arguments leave them out.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grid` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | yes | The spacing between the quantise grid's lines, in ticks. `null` (nothing) follows the Clip View's editing grid, the step the note area draws, at the moment the command runs. |
| `target` | [`QuantizeTarget`](#quantizetarget) | yes | Whether quantise moves note starts or note ends. |
| `amount` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | How far each note moves toward its grid line, as a percentage from 0 (nothing moves) to 100 (every note lands on the line). |

### `QuantizeTarget`

What `note.quantize` moves toward the grid: `note_start` (the default) moves each note's start, `note_end` moves its end instead, leaving the start alone.

One of:

- `"note_start"`: Move the notes' starts.
- `"note_end"`: Move the notes' ends; the starts stay put.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What `note.quantize` moves toward the grid: `note_start` (the default) moves each note's start, `note_end` moves its end instead, leaving the start alone.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "note_start",
      "description": "Move the notes' starts.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "note_end",
      "description": "Move the notes' ends; the starts stay put.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `RackFrame`

A rack as the Device View shows it (WP-5.2; the racks spec, R18 to R23): a view column of selectors, then each view that's shown, left to right.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | [`RackKind`](#rackkind) | yes | Its kind. |
| `views` | [`RackViews`](#rackviews) | yes | Which views it shows: kept with the set, so reopening it shows them. |
| `chains` | array of [`ChainRow`](#chainrow) | yes | Its chains, in order. |
| `selected_chains` | array of [`ChainId`](#chainid) | yes | The selected chains: those clicked, or the first chain while none is. |
| `devices` | array of [`DeviceFrame`](#deviceframe) | yes | The devices of the selected chain, left to right: empty while no chain or several are selected. |
| `chain_list_focused` | boolean | yes | Whether the chain list has the focus, so S solos the selected chain. |
| `selector` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The chain selector's value (racks spec, R33): 0 to 127. |
| `filters_midi_ctrl` | boolean | yes | Chain Selector Filters MIDI Ctrl (racks spec, R31). |

| `note` | string or null | no | What the devices view says instead of devices while several chains are selected, such as `3 chains selected`. |
| `pads` | [`PadFrame`](#padframe) or null | no | A drum rack's pad view (drum racks spec, R11); left out for any other rack. |

### `RackKind`

The four kinds of rack. A rack has the role of what it holds ([`RackKind::role`]).

One of:

- `"instrument"`: Holds MIDI effects, an instrument and audio effects in each chain.
- `"audio_effect"`: Holds audio effects only.
- `"midi_effect"`: Holds MIDI effects only.
- `"drum"`: An instrument rack whose chains are keyed to notes (WP-5.6).

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json

  "description": "The four kinds of rack. A rack has the role of what it holds ([`RackKind::role`]).",

      "const": "instrument",
      "description": "Holds MIDI effects, an instrument and audio effects in each chain.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "audio_effect",
      "description": "Holds audio effects only.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "midi_effect",
      "description": "Holds MIDI effects only.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "drum",
      "description": "An instrument rack whose chains are keyed to notes (WP-5.6).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `RackViews`

Which views of a rack are shown: `macros` (the Macro Controls), `variations` (the Macro Variations, off in a new rack), `chain_list` and `devices` (the selected chain's devices), the last three on in a new rack. A drum rack also has `pads` (the pad view, on in a new rack) with `first_pad` (the lowest note it shows, a multiple of 4, 36 in a new rack), and the switches `input_output` (each chain's Preview, Receive, Play and Choke), `send` (its send sliders) and `returns` (the return chains' section), all off in a new rack. Every rack has `zone_editor` (`key`, `velocity` or `select`, none in a new rack; not a drum rack) and `auto_select` (the chain list follows the notes, off in a new rack).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `macros` | boolean | yes | The Macro Controls. |
| `chain_list` | boolean | yes | The chain list. |
| `devices` | boolean | yes | The selected chain's devices. |
| `auto_select` | boolean | no | Auto Select: the chain list selects the chains that are processing (racks spec, R37; drum racks follow their notes). Off in a new rack. |
| `first_pad` | integer from 0 to 255 | no | The lowest note the pad view shows: 36 (C1) in a new drum rack. |
| `input_output` | boolean | no | A drum rack's Input/Output switch. |
| `macro_count` | integer from 0 to 255 | no | How many macros the Macro Controls show, from 1 to 16 (macros spec, R2): 8 in a new rack. |
| `pads` | boolean | no | A drum rack's pad view. |
| `returns` | boolean | no | A drum rack's Return switch. |
| `send` | boolean | no | A drum rack's Send switch. |
| `variations` | boolean | no | The Macro Variations (macros spec, R25): hidden in a new rack. |
| `zone_editor` | [`ZoneKind`](#zonekind) or null | no | The zone editor beside the chain list (racks spec, R35): the Key, Vel (`velocity`) or Chain (`select`) editor, or none while Hide is on, as in a new rack. |

A drum rack also has `pads` (the pad view, on in a new rack) with `first_pad` (the lowest note it shows, a multiple of 4, 36 in a new rack), and the switches `input_output` (each chain's Preview, Receive, Play and Choke), `send` (its send sliders) and `returns` (the return chains' section), all off in a new rack. Every rack has `zone_editor` (`key`, `velocity` or `select`, none in a new rack; not a drum rack) and `auto_select` (the chain list follows the notes, off in a new rack).",

### `RandomizeAmounts`

The Randomize amount of each lane, which the footer's control holds (Spec: note-editing R13). A new editor has 0 for each.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `velocity` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The Velocity lane's, from 0 to 127. |
| `chance` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The Chance lane's, a percentage from 0 to 100. |
| `release_velocity` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The Release Velocity lane's, from 0 to 127. |

```json
  "description": "The Randomize amount of each lane, which the footer's control holds (Spec: note-editing R13). A new editor has 0 for each.",
```

### `RealtimePhase`

What the real-time render is doing now (the external devices spec, R23).

One of:

- `"idle"`: Nothing is rendering.
- an object with `waiting` (object with `seconds` (number)): Waiting for the hardware's sound to die away, with the seconds left.
- `"rendering"`: Rendering the range.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What the real-time render is doing now (the external devices spec, R23).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "idle",
      "description": "Nothing is rendering.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Waiting for the hardware's sound to die away, with the seconds left.",
      "properties": {
        "waiting": {
          "properties": {
            "seconds": {
              "description": "The seconds left before the render starts.",
              "format": "double",
              "type": "number"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "seconds"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "waiting"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "const": "rendering",
      "description": "Rendering the range.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `ReleaseMode`

What a note's end does while a sustain loop is on (R18).

One of:

- `"off"`: Keeps the voice in the sustain loop until the release ends.
- `"release"`: Plays on through Loop End to Sample End.
- `"loop"`: Plays on, then loops from the release loop point to Sample End.
- `"back_and_forth"`: As `loop`, back and forth.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What a note's end does while a sustain loop is on (R18).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "off",
      "description": "Keeps the voice in the sustain loop until the release ends.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "release",
      "description": "Plays on through Loop End to Sample End.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "loop",
      "description": "Plays on, then loops from the release loop point to Sample End.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "back_and_forth",
      "description": "As `loop`, back and forth.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `SampleEditKind`

What an edit does (R55).

One of:

- `"trim"`: Keeps the selection and drops the rest.
- `"cut"`: Removes the selection and closes the gap.
- `"reverse"`: Reverses the selection, or the whole sample with none.
- `"fade_in"`: A straight line in gain from silence to full over the selection, or the whole sample with none.
- `"fade_out"`: A straight line in gain from full to silence over the selection, or the whole sample with none.
- `"normalize"`: Scales the selection, or the whole sample with none, so its largest magnitude reaches 0 dBFS.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What an edit does (R55).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "trim",
      "description": "Keeps the selection and drops the rest.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "cut",
      "description": "Removes the selection and closes the gap.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "reverse",
      "description": "Reverses the selection, or the whole sample with none.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "fade_in",
      "description": "A straight line in gain from silence to full over the selection, or the whole sample with none.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "fade_out",
      "description": "A straight line in gain from full to silence over the selection, or the whole sample with none.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "normalize",
      "description": "Scales the selection, or the whole sample with none, so its largest magnitude reaches 0 dBFS.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `SampleViewChange`

How to change the Sample Editor's view: `selection` zooms to the time selection (Z), `back` goes to the view before the last zoom (X), `whole` fits the whole file across the editor (W), `height` switches fitting the waveform to the editor's height (H), `span` shows the span `start` to `end`, `scroll` shows it without remembering the view before, and `page` does the same without pausing Follow.

One of:

- `"selection"`: Zoom to the time selection.
- `"back"`: Go back to the view before the last zoom.
- `"whole"`: Fit the whole file across the editor.
- `"height"`: Switch fitting the waveform to the editor's height.
- `"span"`: Show a span.
- `"scroll"`: Show a span without remembering the view before, as scrolling does.
- `"page"`: Show a span without remembering the view before or pausing Follow, as Follow turning the page does.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How to change the Sample Editor's view: `selection` zooms to the time selection (Z), `back` goes to the view before the last zoom (X), `whole` fits the whole file across the editor (W), `height` switches fitting the waveform to the editor's height (H), `span` shows the span `start` to `end`, `scroll` shows it without remembering the view before, and `page` does the same without pausing Follow.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "selection",
      "description": "Zoom to the time selection.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "back",
      "description": "Go back to the view before the last zoom.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "whole",
      "description": "Fit the whole file across the editor.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "height",
      "description": "Switch fitting the waveform to the editor's height.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "span",
      "description": "Show a span.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "scroll",
      "description": "Show a span without remembering the view before, as scrolling does.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "page",
      "description": "Show a span without remembering the view before or pausing Follow, as Follow turning the page does.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `Scale`

A scale: whether Scale Mode is on (`enabled`), the root note (0 is C, 11 is B), and the scale's `name`, from the scale list. A scale with `enabled` false is the chromatic scale, whose degree is a semitone.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether Scale Mode is on: the scale's keys are the ones the rest of the set reads. |
| `root` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The root note: 0 (C) to 11 (B). |
| `name` | [`ScaleName`](#scalename) | yes | The scale's name, from the scale list. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json

  "description": "A scale: whether Scale Mode is on (`enabled`), the root note (0 is C, 11 is B), and the scale's `name`, from the scale list. A scale with `enabled` false is the chromatic scale, whose degree is a semitone.",

    "enabled": {
      "description": "Whether Scale Mode is on: the scale's keys are the ones the rest of the set reads.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "name": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ScaleName",
      "description": "The scale's name, from the scale list."
    },
    "root": {
      "description": "The root note: 0 (C) to 11 (B).",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "enabled",
    "root",
    "name"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `SelectEdge`

Which edge of the current scene to select (S-SES-020 to S-SES-022).

One of:

- `"last"`: The last track of the current scene; pressed again on the last track, the scene itself (End).

```json
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `SelectMode`

How to change the clip selection: `replace` it (a click), `add` to it, `toggle` each clip in or out (Cmd-click, Ctrl-click on Windows), or `extend` it to every clip between the first selected clip and these (Shift-click).

One of:

- `"replace"`: Select only these clips.
- `"add"`: Add these clips.
- `"toggle"`: Select each clip that isn't selected and deselect each that is.
- `"extend"`: Add these clips and every clip between them and the first selected clip, in time and in the track list.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How to change the clip selection: `replace` it (a click), `add` to it, `toggle` each clip in or out (Cmd-click, Ctrl-click on Windows), or `extend` it to every clip between the first selected clip and these (Shift-click).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "replace",
      "description": "Select only these clips.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "add",
      "description": "Add these clips.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "toggle",
      "description": "Select each clip that isn't selected and deselect each that is.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "extend",
      "description": "Add these clips and every clip between them and the first selected clip, in time and in the track list.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `SendTap`

Where a return track's sends take their signal from each sending track: `post` (the default) after the sending track's pan, volume, and activator, or `pre` before them, straight after its device chain.

One of:

- `"post"`: After the sending track's pan, volume, and activator: the default.
- `"pre"`: Before them, straight after the sending track's device chain.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
      "type": "string"
    },

      "description": "Before them, straight after the sending track's device chain.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `SettingsPage`

A page of the Settings window, in Live's order (L-SET-002).

One of:

- `"display-input"`: Display & Input (L-SET-010).
- `"shortcuts"`: Shortcuts. Beatlayer's own page: the person's own keyboard shortcuts (IMP-17; the custom shortcuts spec). It follows Display & Input, the page Live keeps its keyboard settings in (L-SET-002).
- `"theme-colors"`: Theme & Colors (L-SET-011).
- `"audio"`: Audio (L-SET-012). The page the window first opens on.
- `"link"`: Link (L-SET-013).
- `"tempo-midi"`: Tempo & MIDI (L-SET-014).
- `"file-folder"`: File & Folder (L-SET-015).
- `"library"`: Library (L-SET-016).
- `"plug-ins"`: Plug-Ins (L-SET-017).
- `"agents"`: Agents (L-SET-020). Beatlayer's own page: the agent server's settings (WP-1.15), which Live doesn't have. It follows Plug-Ins in the chooser (a Beatlayer addition, decided 14 October 2026).
- `"record-warp-launch"`: Record, Warp & Launch (L-SET-018).
- `"licenses-updates"`: Licenses & Updates (L-SET-019).

### `SettingsState`

What `settings.state` returns: the Settings window's preferences by page. Pages whose settings no package has built yet are left out.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | [`SettingsPage`](#settingspage) | yes | The page the Settings window shows, or showed last. |
| `display_input` | [`DisplayInputSettings`](#displayinputsettings) | yes | Display & Input. |
| `theme_colors` | [`ThemeColorsSettings`](#themecolorssettings) | yes | Theme & Colors: the Theme and Customization sections, as the `settings.set_theme` to `settings.set_color_hue` commands set them. |
| `audio` | [`AudioPageSettings`](#audiopagesettings) | yes | Audio. |
| `tempo_midi` | [`MidiPortsResult`](#midiportsresult) | yes | Tempo & MIDI: the MIDI ports' switches and the computer MIDI keyboard, the same as `midi.ports` reports. |
| `create_fades_on_clip_edges` | boolean | yes | Record, Warp & Launch: Create Fades on Clip Edges, as `settings.set_create_fades_on_clip_edges` sets it. |
| `retune_on_tuning_load` | boolean | yes | Options ▸ Retune Set On Loading Tuning Systems, as `settings.set_retune_on_tuning_load` sets it (the tunings spec, R15). |
| `warp_recorded_audio` | boolean | yes | Record, Warp & Launch: Warp Recorded Audio, as `settings.set_warp_recorded_audio` sets it. |
| `warp` | [`WarpPrefs`](#warpprefs) | yes | Record, Warp & Launch: Loop/Warp Short Samples, Auto-Warp Long Samples and Default Warp Mode. |
| `launch` | [`LaunchPrefs`](#launchprefs) | yes | Record, Warp & Launch: the Launch section, as the `settings.set_default_launch_*`, `settings.set_select_on_launch`, `settings.set_select_next_scene_on_launch` and `settings.set_start_recording_on_scene_launch` commands set it. |
| `record_session_automation_in` | [`SessionAutomationTracks`](#sessionautomationtracks) | yes | Record, Warp & Launch: Record Session automation in, as `settings.set_record_session_automation_in` sets it. |
| `automation_record_mode` | [`AutomationRecordMode`](#automationrecordmode) | yes | The mode an Arrangement recording writes control moves in, as `settings.set_automation_record_mode` sets it (the automation spec, R18). |
| `file_folder` | [`FileFolderSettings`](#filefoldersettings) | yes | File & Folder: the Temporary Folder, as `settings.set_temporary_folder` sets it. |
| `library` | [`LibrarySettings`](#librarysettings) | yes | Library: Collect Files on Export and the User Library's folder. |
| `auto_hide_plug_in_windows` | boolean | yes | Plug-Ins: Auto-Hide Plug-In Windows, as `settings.set_auto_hide_plug_in_windows` sets it. |
| `plug_ins` | [`PluginSettings`](#pluginsettings) | yes | Plug-Ins: how the Browser shows plug-ins, as `plugin.settings` sets it. |
| `agents` | [`AgentsPageSettings`](#agentspagesettings) | yes | Agents. |
| `assistant` | [`AssistantState`](#assistantstate) | yes | Agents, the assistant: provider, base URL, model, and whether an API key is stored for the provider (the key itself is never reported). |

### `Shape`

An automation shape: the waveforms `sine`, `triangle`, `sawtooth`, `inverse_sawtooth` and `square`, which run one cycle across the span between the bottom and top of the parameter's range; the ramps `rise` (from the value at the span's start to the top), `fall` (to the bottom), `rise_to` (from the bottom to the value at the span's end) and `fall_to` (from the top); and `adsr`.

One of:

- `"sine"`: One sine cycle, from the middle, rising first.
- `"triangle"`: Bottom to top at the span's middle and back.
- `"sawtooth"`: Bottom rising to top.
- `"inverse_sawtooth"`: Top falling to bottom.
- `"square"`: Top for the first half, bottom for the second.
- `"rise"`: The value at the span's start, rising to the top.
- `"fall"`: The value at the span's start, falling to the bottom.
- `"rise_to"`: The bottom, rising to the value at the span's end.
- `"fall_to"`: The top, falling to the value at the span's end.
- `"adsr"`: Attack, decay, sustain and release.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "An automation shape: the waveforms `sine`, `triangle`, `sawtooth`, `inverse_sawtooth` and `square`, which run one cycle across the span between the bottom and top of the parameter's range; the ramps `rise` (from the value at the span's start to the top), `fall` (to the bottom), `rise_to` (from the bottom to the value at the span's end) and `fall_to` (from the top); and `adsr`.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "sine",
      "description": "One sine cycle, from the middle, rising first.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "triangle",
      "description": "Bottom to top at the span's middle and back.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "sawtooth",
      "description": "Bottom rising to top.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "inverse_sawtooth",
      "description": "Top falling to bottom.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "square",
      "description": "Top for the first half, bottom for the second.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "rise",
      "description": "The value at the span's start, rising to the top.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "fall",
      "description": "The value at the span's start, falling to the bottom.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "rise_to",
      "description": "The bottom, rising to the value at the span's end.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "fall_to",
      "description": "The top, falling to the value at the span's end.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "adsr",
      "description": "Attack, decay, sustain and release.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `ShapePoint`

One breakpoint of a Shaper's shape (R23): a place in the cycle, the output there, and the bend of the segment starting at it.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | number | yes | Where in the cycle, from 0 (its start) to 1 (its end). |
| `y` | number | yes | The output there, from 0 to 1. |
| `bend` | number | no | The bend of the segment starting here, from −1 to 1, by the automation spec's curve law; 0 is straight. |
| `sustain` | boolean | no | Whether it is the Shaper MIDI's sustain breakpoint (R26): at most one in a shape. |

```json
      "type": "number"
    }

  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `Sidechain`

A device's sidechain input: `enabled` (the External switch), `input` (Source: `none`, or `track` with a track and a `tap`), `gain` (SC Gain, linear, 1 is 0 dB), `mix` (0 the device's own input to 1 the sidechain alone), and `listen` (Sidechain Listen: hear what the detector hears).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | no | External: whether the device's detector listens to the sidechain rather than its own input. Off on a new device. |
| `gain` | number | no | SC Gain, linear: 1 (0 dB) on a new device. |
| `input` | [`Input`](#input) | no | Source: No Input on a new device, or a track tapped Pre FX, Post FX (what choosing a track picks), or Post Mixer. |
| `listen` | boolean | no | Sidechain Listen: the device's output is what its detector hears. |
| `mix` | number | no | Mix: how much of the detector's signal is the sidechain, from 0 (the device's own input) to 1 (the sidechain alone, 100 %, as on a new device). |

```json

  "description": "A device's sidechain input: `enabled` (the External switch), `input` (Source: `none`, or `track` with a track and a `tap`), `gain` (SC Gain, linear, 1 is 0 dB), `mix` (0 the device's own input to 1 the sidechain alone), and `listen` (Sidechain Listen: hear what the detector hears).",
  "properties": {
    "enabled": {
      "description": "External: whether the device's detector listens to the sidechain rather than its own input. Off on a new device.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "gain": {
      "description": "SC Gain, linear: 1 (0 dB) on a new device.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "input": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Input",
      "description": "Source: No Input on a new device, or a track tapped Pre FX, Post FX (what choosing a track picks), or Post Mixer."
    },
    "listen": {
      "description": "Sidechain Listen: the device's output is what its detector hears.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "mix": {
      "description": "Mix: how much of the detector's signal is the sidechain, from 0 (the device's own input) to 1 (the sidechain alone, 100 %, as on a new device).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `StemKind`

A part of the mix to separate (the dialog's four switches).

One of:

- `"vocals"`: Voices.
- `"drums"`: Drums and percussion.

```json
  "properties": {
    "data": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/TakeClipData",
      "description": "What it plays."
    },
    "id": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ClipId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The clip's ID. Left out, the editor issues one."
    },
    "length": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",
      "description": "How long the clip is. Always positive."
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "The clip's name, which may be empty.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "start": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",
      "description": "Where the clip starts in the arrangement. Never negative."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name",
    "start",
    "length",
    "data"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `Taper`

How a continuous parameter's control travel maps onto its range.

One of:

- `"linear"`: Evenly in the value.
- `"logarithmic"`: Evenly in the value's logarithm, as frequencies and times are: each octave or doubling takes the same travel. Needs a range above 0.
- an object with `power` (integer from 0 to 255): As a power of the travel: the value is `min + (max − min) × nᵏ` at travel `n`, for times and rates whose knobs reach 0, such as an envelope's `32 s × n⁵`. `k` is 2 to 8.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How a continuous parameter's control travel maps onto its range.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "linear",
      "description": "Evenly in the value.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "logarithmic",
      "description": "Evenly in the value's logarithm, as frequencies and times are: each octave or doubling takes the same travel. Needs a range above 0.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "As a power of the travel: the value is `min + (max − min) × nᵏ` at travel `n`, for times and rates whose knobs reach 0, such as an envelope's `32 s × n⁵`. `k` is 2 to 8.",
      "properties": {
        "power": {
          "format": "uint8",
          "maximum": 255,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "power"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

```json
    "$ref": "#/$defs/TempoSegment"
  },
  "minItems": 1,
  "type": "array"
}
```

### `TempoSegment`

One piece of a tempo map. It runs from its start to the next segment's start; the last one runs on for ever.

One of:

- an object with `kind` = `"constant"`, `start` ([`Ticks`](#ticks)), `bpm` ([`Bpm`](#bpm)): A steady tempo.
- an object with `kind` = `"ramp"`, `start` ([`Ticks`](#ticks)), `from` ([`Bpm`](#bpm)), `to` ([`Bpm`](#bpm)): A tempo that changes in a straight line against musical position, from `from` at `start` to `to` at the next segment's start. The next segment may start at a different tempo, which makes a jump.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "One piece of a tempo map. It runs from its start to the next segment's start; the last one runs on for ever.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "description": "A steady tempo.",
      "properties": {
        "bpm": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Bpm"
        },
        "kind": {
          "const": "constant",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "start": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "kind",
        "start",
        "bpm"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
```

### `Ticks`

A musical position or length in ticks: 705,600 to the quarter note, so a sixteenth note is 176,400, a beat in 4/4 is 705,600, and a 4/4 bar is 2,822,400. Position 0 is the start of the arrangement (bar 1, beat 1); positions before it are negative.

Type: integer.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A musical position or length in ticks: 705,600 to the quarter note, so a sixteenth note is 176,400, a beat in 4/4 is 705,600, and a 4/4 bar is 2,822,400. Position 0 is the start of the arrangement (bar 1, beat 1); positions before it are negative.",
  "format": "int64",
  "type": "integer"
}
```

</details>

```json
  },
  "minItems": 1,
  "type": "array"
}
```

### `TrackDelay`

A track's delay (the mixer spec): `{ "unit": "milliseconds", "value": 10.0 }` (−1000 to 1000, two decimals; kept in milliseconds when the sample rate changes) or `{ "unit": "samples", "value": 480 }` (−192000 to 192000; kept in samples). Positive delays the track, negative plays it early.

One of:

- an object with `unit` = `"milliseconds"`, `value` (number): Milliseconds, −1000 to 1000.
- an object with `unit` = `"samples"`, `value` (integer): Samples (frames of the current sample rate), −192000 to 192000.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A track's delay (the mixer spec): `{ \"unit\": \"milliseconds\", \"value\": 10.0 }` (−1000 to 1000, two decimals; kept in milliseconds when the sample rate changes) or `{ \"unit\": \"samples\", \"value\": 480 }` (−192000 to 192000; kept in samples). Positive delays the track, negative plays it early.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "description": "Milliseconds, −1000 to 1000.",
      "properties": {
        "unit": {
          "const": "milliseconds",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "value": {
          "description": "The delay: positive delays the track, negative plays it early.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "unit",
        "value"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "description": "Samples (frames of the current sample rate), −192000 to 192000.",
      "properties": {
        "unit": {
          "const": "samples",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "value": {
          "description": "The delay: positive delays the track, negative plays it early.",
          "format": "int64",
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "unit",
        "value"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `TrackKind`

The kind of a track, fixed when the track is created.

One of:

- `"audio"`: Holds audio clips.
- `"midi"`: Holds MIDI clips.
- `"group"`: Holds other tracks and sums their output.
- `"return"`: Receives sends from other tracks.
- `"main"`: The song's output. There is exactly one.

```json
}
```

### `TransientLoopMode`

How Beats fills the time a segment's own audio doesn't (R2).

One of:

- `"loop_off"`: Silence until the next segment.
- `"loop_forward"`: Back to the segment's middle, forwards again; the default.
- `"loop_back_and_forth"`: Backwards to the middle, then forwards.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "loop_forward",
      "description": "Back to the segment's middle, forwards again; the default.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "loop_back_and_forth",
      "description": "Backwards to the middle, then forwards.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

### `TransportState`

What `transport.state` returns: the transport and the Control Bar's transport section, as they are now.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `engine_running` | boolean | yes | Whether the audio engine runs on a device, so the transport can play. While it doesn't, the transport's commands are refused. |
| `playing` | boolean | yes | Whether the song is playing. |
| `position` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | The play position (the playhead), in ticks from 1.1.1 (705,600 to the quarter note): where the song plays now, or where playback stopped, which is where `transport.continue` resumes. |
| `insert_marker` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | The insert marker, where `transport.play` starts, in ticks. |
| `arrangement_position` | string | yes | What the Control Bar's Arrangement Position fields show, as bar.beat.sixteenth by the song's time signatures: the play position while the song plays, and the insert marker while it's stopped. |
| `loop_start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the Arrangement loop brace starts, in ticks. |
| `loop_length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How long the loop brace is, in ticks. |
| `loop_on` | boolean | yes | Whether the Arrangement Loop switch is on. |
| `loop_start_position` | string | yes | The loop brace's start as the Loop Start fields show it, as bar.beat.sixteenth. |
| `loop_length_bars` | string | yes | The brace's length as the Loop Length fields show it: bars, beats, and sixteenths counted from 0, such as `4.0.0` for four bars. |
| `tempo` | number | yes | The tempo where the Arrangement Position fields are, in quarter notes per minute, as the Tempo field shows it. |
| `tempo_editable` | boolean | yes | Whether the tempo is one constant tempo, so the Tempo field can set it. With tempo changes along the song, change it with `song.set_tempo`'s full map instead. |
| `time_signature` | string | yes | The time signature there, such as `4/4`, as the time-signature fields show it. |
| `time_signature_editable` | boolean | yes | Whether the song has one time signature throughout, so the time-signature fields can set it. |
| `metronome` | [`MetronomeSettings`](#metronomesettings) | yes | The metronome settings: enabled, count-in, sound, rhythm, and only while recording (WP-2.15). |
| `arrangement_record` | boolean | yes | Whether Arrangement Record is on, as the Control Bar's record button shows it. While it is on and the song plays, armed tracks record. |
| `take_running` | boolean | yes | Whether a take is running: Arrangement Record is on and the armed tracks' input is being written, so playback is past the count-in and any punch-in point. It ends at the punch-out point or when recording does. |
| `counting_in` | boolean | yes | Whether the count-in is sounding, before playback and recording start. |
| `punch_in` | boolean | yes | Whether Punch-In is on. |
| `punch_out` | boolean | yes | Whether Punch-Out is on. |
| `midi_overdub` | boolean | yes | Whether MIDI Arrangement Overdub is on. |
| `automation_arm` | boolean | yes | Whether Automation Arm is on (view state, not saved with the set). |
| `automation_record_mode` | [`AutomationRecordMode`](#automationrecordmode) | yes | The mode an Arrangement recording writes control moves in, as `settings.set_automation_record_mode` sets it (the automation spec, R18). |
| `recording` | [`RunningRecording`](#runningrecording) or null | yes | The recording under way, from the moment recording starts until its clips are made; null when none is. |
| `last_recording` | [`RecordingReport`](#recordingreport) or null | yes | What the last recording that ended came to; null until one has ended in this session. |
| `capture_midi_ready` | boolean | yes | Whether Capture MIDI has notes to bring back: a monitoring MIDI track was played since the last capture or recording, so `midi.capture` runs and the Control Bar's button and Create menu item are enabled. |

```json
}
```

</details>

### `Trigger`

How a shortcut acts.

One of:

- `"press"`: Once, when pressed.
- `"held"`: While held.
- `"latch"`: Toggles when tapped; acts only while held if held for about half a second (Live 12's momentary shortcuts).

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How a shortcut acts.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "press",
      "description": "Once, when pressed.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "held",
      "description": "While held.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "latch",
      "description": "Toggles when tapped; acts only while held if held for about half a second (Live 12's momentary shortcuts).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `Tuning`

A tuning: its `name`, `description`, the `cents` of degrees 1 to n above the unison (the last is the pseudo-octave), optional note `names` (one per degree) and `link`, its `reference` pitch (octave, degree and frequency in Hz) and its `range` of notes (the `lowest` on key 0 and the `highest`, at most 128 notes).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The tuning's name: its file's name without the extension. |
| `description` | string | yes | The tuning's description, from its file. |
| `cents` | array of number | yes | The pitch of degrees 1 to n above degree 0 in cents; the last is the pseudo-octave. The pitches needn't rise in order. |
| `reference` | [`Reference`](#reference) | yes | The reference pitch. |
| `range` | [`TuningRange`](#tuningrange) | yes | The note range. |
| `link` | string or null | no | A link to a page about the tuning. |
| `names` | array of string | no | The name of each degree, 0 to n − 1, or none at all. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A tuning: its `name`, `description`, the `cents` of degrees 1 to n above the unison (the last is the pseudo-octave), optional note `names` (one per degree) and `link`, its `reference` pitch (octave, degree and frequency in Hz) and its `range` of notes (the `lowest` on key 0 and the `highest`, at most 128 notes).",
  "properties": {
    "cents": {
      "description": "The pitch of degrees 1 to n above degree 0 in cents; the last is the pseudo-octave. The pitches needn't rise in order.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "description": {
      "description": "The tuning's description, from its file.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "link": {
      "description": "A link to a page about the tuning.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "The tuning's name: its file's name without the extension.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "names": {
      "description": "The name of each degree, 0 to n − 1, or none at all.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "range": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/TuningRange",
      "description": "The note range."
    },
    "reference": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Reference",
      "description": "The reference pitch."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name",
    "description",
    "cents",
    "reference",
    "range"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `TuningNote`

A note of a tuning: a degree in an octave. Octave 0 starts at degree 0 of the unison; a note below it has a negative octave.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `octave` | integer | yes | The octave (a pseudo-octave of the tuning), negative below the first. |
| `degree` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The degree within it, 0 to the tuning's degrees − 1. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A note of a tuning: a degree in an octave. Octave 0 starts at degree 0 of the unison; a note below it has a negative octave.",
  "properties": {
    "degree": {
      "description": "The degree within it, 0 to the tuning's degrees − 1.",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "octave": {
      "description": "The octave (a pseudo-octave of the tuning), negative below the first.",
      "format": "int32",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "octave",
    "degree"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

A tuning's note range (the tunings spec, R8): the notes the keys play, from the lowest, on key 0, to the highest.

|---|---|---|---|

```json
      "description": "The note key 0 plays."
    }
  },
  "required": [

  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `ViewState`

What `view.state` returns: what the view commands switch, without switching any of it.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | [`ViewResult`](#viewresult) | yes | The main window: the main view, the browser, the Info View, full-screen mode and the interface zoom. |
| `second_window` | [`SecondWindowState`](#secondwindowstate) | yes | The second window: whether it is open, the main view it shows, its browser, zoom, frame and detail area. |
| `focused_window` | [`WindowName`](#windowname) | yes | The window the commands that act on one window act on when they aren't told which: the one with the focus. |
| `clip_view` | [`ClipViewState`](#clipviewstate) | yes | The Clip View and its note editor: whether it shows, Draw Mode, the clip it holds, the selected notes, the lane and Fold. |
| `detail` | [`DetailState`](#detailstate) | yes | The detail area: which of the Clip View and the Device View show, the Clip View's height, and where the focus is. |
| `plugin_list` | [`PluginListState`](#pluginliststate) | yes | The list of the set's plug-ins: whether it shows, and whether Show Only Missing is on. |
| `assistant` | [`AssistantPanelState`](#assistantpanelstate) | yes | The assistant's panel. |
| `undo_history` | boolean | yes | Whether the Undo History panel shows. |
| `save_history` | boolean | yes | Whether the Save History panel shows. |
| `plug_in_windows` | boolean | yes | Whether floating devices' and plug-ins' windows are shown, as `view.toggle_plug_in_windows` sets it. |

### `WarpFrom`

How Warp From Here warps what follows its point (the warping spec, R39).

One of:

- `"auto"`: Warp From Here: a marker on every bar after it, from the tempo found there.
- `"start_at"`: Warp From Here (Start At …): the same, starting from the tempo `bpm` (the set's tempo there unless given).
- `"straight"`: Warp From Here (Straight): no markers after it, the clip's tempo the tempo found after it.
- `"bpm"`: Warp … BPM From Here: no markers after it, the clip's tempo `bpm` (the set's tempo there unless given).

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How Warp From Here warps what follows its point (the warping spec, R39).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "auto",
      "description": "Warp From Here: a marker on every bar after it, from the tempo found there.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "start_at",
      "description": "Warp From Here (Start At …): the same, starting from the tempo `bpm` (the set's tempo there unless given).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "straight",
      "description": "Warp From Here (Straight): no markers after it, the clip's tempo the tempo found after it.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "bpm",
      "description": "Warp … BPM From Here: no markers after it, the clip's tempo `bpm` (the set's tempo there unless given).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `WarpMarker`

A warp marker: `time`, seconds into the audio file, plays on `beat`, in ticks (705,600 to the quarter note) counted from the clip's 1.1.1 (negative before it).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `time` | number, at least 0 | yes | Seconds into the file: 0 or more. |
| `beat` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | The beat the time plays on, in ticks from the clip's 1.1.1. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A warp marker: `time`, seconds into the audio file, plays on `beat`, in ticks (705,600 to the quarter note) counted from the clip's 1.1.1 (negative before it).",
  "properties": {
    "beat": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",
      "description": "The beat the time plays on, in ticks from the clip's 1.1.1."
    },
    "time": {
      "description": "Seconds into the file: 0 or more.",
      "format": "double",
      "minimum": 0.0,
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "time",
    "beat"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `WarpMode`

How a warped clip's audio is fitted to the speed its warp map sets: the six warp modes, in the order the Audio panel offers them (R1).

One of:

- `"beats"`: Segments cut at transients or on a grid, for rhythmic material. The default of a new clip.
- `"tones"`: Grains that keep the pitch of pitched material.
- `"texture"`: Overlapping grains with some randomness, for material without a clear pitch.
- `"re_pitch"`: Plays the file faster or slower, so pitch follows speed.
- `"complex"`: Frequency-domain stretching, for whole mixes.
- `"complex_pro"`: Complex, with finer settings and Formants.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How a warped clip's audio is fitted to the speed its warp map sets: the six warp modes, in the order the Audio panel offers them (R1).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "beats",
      "description": "Segments cut at transients or on a grid, for rhythmic material. The default of a new clip.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "tones",
      "description": "Grains that keep the pitch of pitched material.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "texture",
      "description": "Overlapping grains with some randomness, for material without a clear pitch.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "re_pitch",
      "description": "Plays the file faster or slower, so pitch follows speed.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "complex",
      "description": "Frequency-domain stretching, for whole mixes.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "complex_pro",
      "description": "Complex, with finer settings and Formants.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `WarpPrefs`

The first three rows of the Warp/Fades section (L-SET-018; WP-4.9), with the defaults observed in Live 12.4.6. They are preferences, kept between starts and not saved with a set.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `loop_warp_short_samples` | [`LoopWarpShortSamples`](#loopwarpshortsamples) | yes | Loop/Warp Short Samples, as `settings.set_loop_warp_short_samples` sets it. |
| `auto_warp_long_samples` | boolean | yes | Auto-Warp Long Samples, as `settings.set_auto_warp_long_samples` sets it. |
| `default_warp_mode` | [`DefaultWarpMode`](#defaultwarpmode) | yes | Default Warp Mode, as `settings.set_default_warp_mode` sets it. |

```json

      "$ref": "#/$defs/LoopWarpShortSamples",
      "default": "auto",
      "description": "Loop/Warp Short Samples, as `settings.set_loop_warp_short_samples` sets it."

  },
  "required": [

}
```

### `Widget`

How a control draws its parameter.

One of:

- `"knob"`: A round knob with its name above and its value below: continuous values and gains.
- `"toggle"`: A switch button with its name above: toggles.
- `"chooser"`: A field that opens a menu of choices, with its name above.
- `"number"`: A number field, dragged or typed, with its name above.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json

  "description": "How a control draws its parameter.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "knob",
      "description": "A round knob with its name above and its value below: continuous values and gains.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "toggle",
      "description": "A switch button with its name above: toggles.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "chooser",
      "description": "A field that opens a menu of choices, with its name above.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "number",
      "description": "A number field, dragged or typed, with its name above.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `WindowFrame`

Where a floating device's window sits and how big it is (IMP-14, WP-2.5b), in points on the screen: the top-left corner of its outer frame, and the size of what it shows inside. It's saved with the set beside the document, so moving or resizing a window is never an undo step.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | number | yes | The left edge of the window's outer frame, in points from the left of the main screen. |
| `y` | number | yes | The top of the window's outer frame, in points from the top of the main screen. |
| `width` | number | yes | The width of the window's contents, in points. |
| `height` | number | yes | The height of the window's contents, in points. |

```json
  "properties": {
    "height": {
      "description": "The height of the window's contents, in points.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "width": {
      "description": "The width of the window's contents, in points.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "x": {
      "description": "The left edge of the window's outer frame, in points from the left of the main screen.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },

      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }

    "height"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `Zone`

A range of values with a fade at each end (R5): the layer is silent at the lowest and highest value when it has a fade there, and reaches full level `fade_low` values above the lowest and `fade_high` below the highest.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `low` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The lowest value in the zone. |
| `high` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The highest value in the zone. |
| `fade_high` | integer from 0 to 255 | no | How many values the fade at the high end spans; 0 for none. |
| `fade_low` | integer from 0 to 255 | no | How many values the fade at the low end spans; 0 for none. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "A range of values with a fade at each end (R5): the layer is silent at the lowest and highest value when it has a fade there, and reaches full level `fade_low` values above the lowest and `fade_high` below the highest.",
  "properties": {
    "fade_high": {
      "description": "How many values the fade at the high end spans; 0 for none.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "fade_low": {
      "description": "How many values the fade at the low end spans; 0 for none.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "high": {
      "description": "The highest value in the zone.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "low": {
      "description": "The lowest value in the zone.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "low",
    "high"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `ZoneKind`

Which of a layer's three zones.

One of:

- `"key"`: The notes it plays over, 0 to 127.
- `"velocity"`: The note-on velocities it plays at, 1 to 127.
- `"select"`: The Sample Selector values it plays at, 0 to 127.

```json
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "select",
```
